news.title: Update your IDE to restore agent activity in Copilot usage metrics
news.body: If your Copilot usage metrics have shown agent activity or agent lines of code falling while Copilot usage kept growing, we’ve found the cause, and a fix is rolling out to each IDE. Several IDEs recently moved Copilot agent sessions to the Copilot SDK. Those sessions didn’t identify which IDE they came from, so usage metrics couldn’t attribute them correctly. Most of that activity was left out of reports, and some was counted as Copilot CLI activity. Only IDE versions that use the Copilot SDK for agent mode are affected. Developers on earlier versions are still counted. The fix is available now in Visual Studio Code. Other IDEs will receive it in upcoming releases, which we expect to finish rolling out by November 2026. Once developers update, their agent activity is counted again in the Copilot usage metrics dashboard and API. Update your IDE Agent activity is counted again once developers are on these versions. If your developers are on an affected version, update as soon as the fixed version is available, because their activity can’t be recovered later. news.title: Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire
news.body: Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire 48 hours after creation and can no longer authorize publishing. This limits the risk of trusting a repository or project name that changes ownership. Your configuration becomes validated and exempt from expiry after its first successful publish. Changing the repository or project identity requires a new trust relationship with a fresh 48-hour validation window—ordinary edits don’t restart the deadline. If your configuration expires, recreate it to start a new 48-hour window. Expired configurations remain visible in trusted publisher settings but don’t count toward per-package limits. Other valid configurations on the package are unaffected. npm also now rejects trusted publishing tokens from GitHub Actions issue_comment events, alongside the existing pull_request_target restriction. If affected, move publishing to a permitted event such as push, release, or workflow_dispatch. Join the discussion within GitHub Community. The post Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

news.title: Stateless GitHub App installation tokens rolled out
news.body: The staged rollout of the stateless GitHub App installation token format, which began on April 27, 2026, is complete. By default, all newly minted GitHub App installation tokens will be in the stateless ghs_APPID_JWT format, which makes token issuance and validation faster and improves the reliability of the GitHub API. What’s changed Installation tokens still start with the ghs_ prefix, but they’re now about 520 characters long instead of 40. Token permissions, repository scoping, the one-hour expiration, and the installation access token REST API endpoint are unchanged. Tokens minted before the change continue to work until they expire. What to expect going forward The temporary X-GitHub-Stateless-S2S-Token request header, which we introduced so you could validate the new format on demand, will be deprecated on November 30, 2026. After that date, GitHub will no longer respect the header, and all eligible apps will always receive stateless tokens. To learn more about the temporary header, see our original changelog for its release. news.title: New fields for SecurityAdvisory GraphQL API
news.body: You can now read more of the GitHub Advisory Database directly from the GraphQL API without falling back to the REST API. The SecurityAdvisory object gained five new fields: cveId: The advisory’s CVE identifier. sourceCodeLocation: A link to the affected source code relevant to the advisory. githubReviewedAt: When GitHub reviewed the advisory. nvdPublishedAt: When the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) published its record. repositoryAdvisoryUrl: A link to the linked repository security advisory when there is one. The securityAdvisories query also gained two new filters, severities and isWithdrawn, so you can narrow results on the server instead of downloading everything and filtering it yourself. They work alongside the filters you already use, such as classification, identifier, EPSS, and published or updated since. This means fewer round trips, one authentication path, and one rate limit budget for integrations that read advisory data. It also makes it easier to build things like severity-based triage feeds, withdrawn advisory audits, and tracking of how quickly advisories move from NVD publication to GitHub review. news.title: Repository security advisory comments API in public preview
news.body: You can now read, add, and edit comments on repository security advisories using the REST API, including advisories created from private vulnerability reports. Until now, the discussion on an advisory was only reachable in the web UI, even though it often holds the most useful triage context on a vulnerability report. With the new endpoints, you can: List the comments on a repository security advisory, optionally limited to those updated since a given time. Get a single comment. Add a comment. Edit a comment. Repository security advisory responses also now include a comments count, and global advisory responses include the count for their linked repository advisory, so you can tell which advisories have discussion before you fetch it. These fields count non-confidential comments and help identify advisories with comment activity before fetching the comments. This helps you export advisory discussions for audits and migrations, automatically add triage notes, and build advisory workflows that work the same way as the ones you already have for issues and pull requests. news.title: Confidential comments on repository security advisories
news.body: You can now post confidential comments on repository security advisories. Confidential comments are visible only to people with write access to the repository, so you can discuss a report with your team without the reporter or other invited collaborators seeing it. Previously, every comment on an advisory was visible to all of its collaborators, including the reporter. To discuss suspected abuse, investigation details, or coordination notes, you had to move the conversation somewhere else and lose it from the advisory’s history. With this update: Select Confidential. Only maintainers will see this comment below the comment box before you post. Confidential comments are clearly marked in the advisory timeline. Reporters and invited collaborators without write access can’t see confidential comments and aren’t notified about them. Access follows current repository permissions. If someone loses write access, they can no longer read confidential comments. Views of confidential comments are recorded in the audit log. news.title: Code coverage uploads no longer fail CI for new branches
news.body: Code coverage uploads from the GitHub Code Quality upload-code-coverage action no longer fail CI when you push a branch that doesn’t yet have an open pull request. Previously, the coverage API required a pull request number for any push to a non-default branch. Since that number only exists once a pull request is open, pushing a new branch before opening a pull request caused the coverage-upload step to fail, even though nothing was actually wrong with your workflow. Now, when the action runs on a push to a branch without an associated pull request, it skips the upload instead of failing, and explains why in an Actions notice and step summary. This applies to: Pushes to branches that don’t yet have an open pull request. Subsequent pushes to those branches, until a pull request is opened. Uploads for pushes to your default branch, and for supported pull request events, continue to work exactly as before, so you don’t need to change any existing workflow configuration. If your workflow uploads coverage only on push events, opening a pull request won’t trigger a new upload by itself—coverage resumes on the next push to that branch. news.title: Dynamic workflows in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app
news.body: Dynamic workflows are now available in Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, and the GitHub Copilot SDK. These let you define an orchestration in code to get the reliability and observability that complex, multi-agent work demands. What is a dynamic workflow? A dynamic workflow is a program that defines how a task is carried out. It combines automated steps with the work of one or more agents, and those steps can run one after another, in parallel, or both. The steps, when to involve agents, and how to use their results are all defined in code, while agents handle the parts that need analysis or judgment. The program itself lives inside a GitHub Copilot extension, which means it has access to Copilot’s powerful extensibility APIs. For example, you could use a dynamic workflow to investigate a service incident: collect logs and telemetry, assign independent agents to analyze different systems, and combine their structured findings into a timeline and root-cause report. The same steps run every time. Dynamic workflows can: Run commands, use tools, or call other services. Divide a goal into tasks and run independent tasks in parallel. Pass structured results from one stage to the next.

news.title: Scheduled code scanning skips inactive repositories
news.body: Weekly scheduled scans for code scanning default setup and GitHub Code Quality now start only after a push or pull request triggers an analysis, rather than counting every kind of scan as recent activity. Previously, activity for a repository was based on any unscheduled scan, including the one-time validation scan that runs when you first enable default setup and scans triggered by a change in detected languages. That meant enabling default setup or rolling out a security configuration across many repositories at once could make a dormant repository look active for another six months and trigger weekly scheduled scans you didn’t expect. The current behavior is as follows: Enabling default setup still runs an initial validation scan and populates findings right away. Weekly scheduled scanning only begins once a push or pull request triggers an analysis. This determination is based on analysis history, not on Git activity from before scanning was enabled. Activity continues to be shared between code scanning and Code Quality. news.title: GitHub async merge API generally available
news.body: You can now use the generally available GitHub async merge API to merge individual or stacked pull requests, add pull requests to a merge queue, or merge pull requests directly. This includes optionally bypassing rules if you have permission. The API processes merges asynchronously, helping your automations handle busy repositories without waiting for complex merges to finish in a single request. Submit a merge request with PUT, then poll with GET using the returned request ID to check its status. The async merge API is now the recommended path for programmatically merging pull requests instead of the synchronous REST endpoint or GraphQL mutations. news.body: GitHub Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0 includes reliability, scalability, and observability improvements for runner scale sets. news.title: Opt-in dist-tag permissions for npm trusted publishing
news.body: Trusted publishing configurations for npm can now be granted permission to manage dist-tags (e.g., promoting a version to latest, updating next and beta pointers) using short-lived OIDC credentials instead of a long-lived access token. Previously, trusted publishing covered publishing and staging, but not dist-tag operations. That meant maintainers who had otherwise fully moved to token-free, OIDC-based workflows still had to keep a granular access token around solely to manage tags after a release or a rollback. Each trusted publishing configuration now has an opt-in Allow npm dist-tag permission. It defaults to off for both new and existing configurations, so no configuration automatically gains new capability. The permission is independent of direct publishing, so a staging-only configuration can also be granted dist-tag management. A dist-tag operation is authorized if the incoming OIDC token matches any one configuration with the permission enabled. Existing token-based dist-tag management continues to work unchanged. To use it, open your package’s trusted publishing settings and enable Allow npm dist-tag on the configurations that should be able to manage tags. Learn more abo

news.body: The HydraFusion research preview is now available in Visual Studio Code and the GitHub Copilot app, expanding beyond Copilot CLI. HydraFusion appears in the model picker, but rather than being a single model, it orchestrates multiple models. HydraFusion treats workflow selection as an optimization problem. It uses capability signals for reasoning, code generation, debugging, and tool use to select the most efficient execution pattern to meet the quality bar. HydraFusion uses one of three workflows: Single: One selected model directly solves the task. Cascade: An efficient model drafts a solution and a quality gate decides whether to accept it or escalate to a stronger model. Critique: One model drafts a result, an independent read-only critic from a different model family reviews it—following the same review pattern as Rubber Duck—and the drafting model revises once. news.title: X25519-only TLS ends for GHE.com on October 7
news.body: Beginning October 7, 2026, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency will no longer accept TLS connections from clients that offer only X25519 for key agreement. Most customers don’t need to take action. The affected endpoints will continue to support the FIPS-approved P-256 (secp256r1) and P-384 (secp384r1) groups. Current browsers, operating systems, GitHub CLI releases, and commonly used TLS libraries already support P-256. You may be affected if an application, proxy, security appliance, or TLS library is explicitly configured to offer only X25519. Before October 7, 2026, you should: Update your operating system, runtime, GitHub CLI, proxy, and TLS libraries to supported versions. Remove any X25519-only configuration. Ensure P-256 (secp256r1) is enabled. You may also enable P-384 (secp384r1). After October 7, X25519-only clients will be unable to establish HTTPS connections. This change applies only to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency. SSH connectivity is not affected. If you need help validating your TLS configuration, contact GitHub Support. news.title: Changes to query results in the GitHub Actions API and UI
news.body: Queries for workflow runs in the GitHub Actions API and UI now return a less precise but more accurate count of records when you search by workflow, event, status, branch, or actor. We will continue to return paginated results of up to 1,000 items. However, if the number of found records exceeds 2,500, we will report “2,500+” instead of attempting to return the exact number of records. This is because queries that retrieve more than 2,500 records frequently timeout and return the number of records found before the timeout rather than the true count. By implementing this limit, our counts will be more accurate and we will improve performance for customers. If your integrations or scripts rely on retrieving more than 2,500 matching workflow runs from a single query, narrow your filters (e.g., by adding a date range) to retrieve the specific runs you need. This change is rolling out now on github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud. The post Changes to query results in the GitHub Actions API and UI appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

news.title: Faster C++ code intelligence with whole codebase indexing
news.body: C++ code intelligence in GitHub Copilot CLI is now faster with support for whole codebase indexing. C++ repositories can contain millions of lines of code across deeply connected source files and headers. Without a reusable index, code-intelligence requests may need to rediscover project information as you navigate, making it slower to find a definition, locate references, or understand unfamiliar code. Whole codebase indexing (WCI) creates a persistent index of symbols across your C++ project, including files that aren’t currently open. The Microsoft C++ Language Server uses your project’s compilation information to resolve types, symbols, includes, and relationships between files. WCI makes that symbol information available for reuse instead of rediscovering it for each request. You spend less time waiting for definitions, references, implementations, and symbol search results, and more time reviewing, understanding, and changing code. news.title: Security improvements for SSH
news.body: We’re removing several SSH algorithms, adding a new algorithm, and requiring larger RSA SSH keys to improve security. The changes are as follows: We’re removing the ability to use RSA keys using SHA-1 in SSH (i.e., the ssh-rsa signature type, including ssh-rsa-cert-v01@openssh.com certificates using SHA-1). We’re removing the key exchange mechanism diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256. All new RSA SSH keys uploaded after October 14, 2026 must be at least 3072 bits in size, both for signing and authentication. We’re additionally supporting the post-quantum key exchange method mlkem768x25519-sha256 for SSH sessions on github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Data Residency, except for the U.S. region. Adding ML-KEM lets us offer a newer, more performant key exchange method that is secure against quantum computers. We’re also removing the older Diffie-Hellman method, a slow, little-used algorithm that could be broken with advances in quantum computing. For RSA, we’re removing the use of SHA-1 since it’s known to be weak, as well as increasing key sizes to align with 128-bit security requirements. news.title: Stage-only npm tokens for safer automation
news.body: You can now select Read and write (stage only) when creating an npm granular access token. This lets your automated workflows stage package versions for review without giving the token permission to publish new versions directly to the npm registry. Your workflow uses npm stage publish to submit a version. A package maintainer then reviews and approves its release with two-factor authentication (2FA). npm rejects direct npm publish attempts with that token, even if you’ve configured it to bypass 2FA for automation. Stage-only tokens retain other package write permissions, including moving dist-tags and deprecating versions. Protect them with the same care as any other write token. Prepare your automation for the token transition This release is opt-in and doesn’t change existing tokens or their direct-publish capabilities. As previously announced, npm is targeting January 2027 to remove direct publishing through bypass-2FA tokens. If you can’t move to trusted publishing yet, stage-only tokens offer a migration path for token-based automation. news.body: GitHub Copilot auto model selection now offers three tiers: efficiency, balance, and intelligence. Choose the tier that reflects how you want auto to weigh cost, quality, and response time for each prompt. Copilot will then optimize accordingly. Efficiency prioritizes keeping costs low and suits fast, straightforward tasks. Balance weighs cost, quality, and latency together, and is a good fit for everyday work. Intelligence prioritizes quality and is built for complex tasks. All three tiers use the same set of available models. Auto individually evaluates each prompt to select a best-suited model. news.title: Control GitHub Actions cache access with cache-mode
news.body: You can now use cache-mode to apply least-privilege access to the GitHub Actions cache at the workflow or job level. By granting each workflow or job only the cache access it needs, you can prevent unnecessary restores or saves and help protect trusted workflows from cache poisoning. This capability is now generally available on all plans. Choose the access each workflow or job needs: read allows cache restores but prevents cache saves. This is the default for low-trust events such as pull_request_target. write allows cache restores and saves. This is the default for trusted events such as push. write-only allows cache saves but prevents cache restores. none prevents all cache access. Job-level settings override workflow-level settings. The selected mode is enforced by the cache service and carries through reusable workflows, where a called workflow cannot receive more cache access than its caller granted. An explicitly declared cache-mode also overrides the read-only cache default for low-trust events such as pull_request_target. news.title: npm extends recovery-code security holds to all accounts
news.body: npm now places a temporary 72-hour security hold on any account after a successful recovery-code sign-in, extending a protection that previously applied only to high-impact accounts. This change applies to all npm accounts. During the hold, publishing and other security-sensitive writes, including creating access tokens, are paused. You can still sign in as well as browse and install packages. The hold expires automatically — no action or support request is needed to restore full access. This extension builds on the preventive account protection npm introduced for high-impact accounts, further slowing account-takeover attempts and reducing the risk of malicious publishing from a compromised recovery code. If you’re unexpectedly blocked from publishing and you didn’t use your recovery code to sign in, contact npm Support right away. news.title: Block pull requests with exposed secrets from merging
news.body: Repository rulesets allow you to easily add scalable protections across your repositories. Starting today, you can use repository rulesets to block pull requests from merging when the pull request introduces secret scanning alerts. The rule checks two things before a pull request can merge: A secret scan has completed for the head commit No alerts are open for secrets introduced by the pull request’s commits By default, the rule runs on open pull requests and blocks secrets found via provider patterns. You can additionally configure the rule to block other categories (e.g., custom or generic patterns). This rule is available today in public preview for customers with GitHub Secret Protection or GitHub Advanced Security. news.title: Multiple trusted publishing configurations for npm
news.body: We’re continuing to make trusted publishing smoother for npm publishers, guided by maintainers feedback. Three updates to npm publishing are now generally available: Multiple trusted publishing configurations per package Staged packages can only be approved after malware scanning is complete Maintainers can see their staged history in the package versions tab A package can now have more than one trusted publishing (OIDC) configuration. Maintainers are no longer limited to one configuration per package to separate workflows with stable, prerelease, or staging versions. Before this, maintainers had to depend on workflow workarounds or keep a long-lived token around for the paths OIDC couldn’t cover. Each configuration is independent and additive, with its own repository, workflow, and environment criteria. You can add, list, and remove them from your package’s settings page. A publish or stage is authorized if the incoming OIDC token matches any one configuration. Configurations never restrict one another, and evaluation order is not guaranteed, so don’t build logic that depends on which configuration matches. news.body: You can now set an optional expiration date on an individual user budget, and GitHub removes the budget on that date. This capability is generally available. The user then falls back to the next budget that applies to them (i.e., their cost center per-user budget or otherwise your universal budget). Previously, you had to remove every temporary budget override by hand, creating recurring cleanup work at enterprise scale. When you create or edit an individual user budget, you can choose: No expiration, which is the default and matches current behavior. Expiration at the start of the next billing cycle. Expiration on a specific date. You can change or clear an expiration date at any time. Set an expiration date in your billing settings, or use the expires_at field in the Budgets REST API when you create or update a budget. It’s not the change itself that’s hard, but the follow-through: updating docs, creating issues, and keeping everyone informed. That’s where information falls out of sync and handoffs get missed. news.title: Coding sessions: environments, browser use, and updated pricing
news.body: Linear Agent can now set up, run, and test your code before returning its work. That means fewer handoffs and changes that are further along when they come back to you. We’re also introducing lower, more transparent pricing, making AI credit usage easier to understand and control. Configurable environments Coding sessions now automatically adapt to each codebase's configuration, with broader out-of-the-box support for Python, Ruby, Go, and more. During a session, Linear detects and installs the toolchains and dependencies it needs to complete the task. Teams can go further by pinning runtime versions, adding setup scripts, and defining environment variables. To get started, create an environment in settings. Visit the docs for more details. Browser testing Once the application is running, Linear Agent tests its work where users experience it: in the browser. The agent opens the app, navigates through a flow, and verifies its implementation. It also captures before-and-after screenshots, making visual changes easier to review alongside the code. news.title: CMS List Field
news.body: You can now better manage repeating content like FAQs, product features, tutorial steps, and cases studies with the new List field in the Framer’s CMS. Rather than duplicating fields like Title 1, Description 1, Title 2, Description 2, you can group items in a single list and add or reorder rows as you would in a CMS table. Your content editors can spend less time juggling fields and more time keeping your site fresh. To migrate existing content, ask the Framer Agent to convert repeated CMS fields into a List. The Agent will also take care of reconnecting the CMS data on the Canvas. If you have a list that is not shown on the Canvas yet, you can easily add it from the Insert panel. Alternatively, select a card you’ve designed and use the newly added Repeat property to repeat it for each list item. Watch the video to learn more. We’ve also added features, fixed bugs, and made improvements across the CMS. See a complete list below. Added Added the List field in the CMS, including API and Agent support Added a new video component to insert in CMS rich text fields Added support for reordering the Status field in the panel Added support for editing content inline for content editors Add

news.title: Agents: 3D Transforms
news.body: Framer’s Agent now supports all 3D Transform properties like Rotate XYZ, Perspective, Origin, Depth, Backface, and many more. This lets you design and iterate on all sorts of creative effects at an incredible pace. Unique to Framer, all 3D layers remain selectable and customizable on our Canvas. For example, this very logo animation was made in Framer using Agents, and consists only of fully editable Frames and Effects. It was made with Opus 5 Fast with Light reasoning.

news.title: Agents: Reasoning and Fast Mode
news.body: The Agent model picker now includes reasoning, letting you choose how much thinking a model does before it starts building. Light reasoning is ideal for quick edits and refinements, while higher reasoning gives Agents more room to plan. We’re also adding Fast mode for models that support it, like Opus 5, for noticeably quicker generations and responses. Fast mode uses more tokens per task. Combined, reasoning and fast mode give you more control of Agents in Framer.

news.title: Branching and Publishing APIs
news.body: Plugins 4.1 brings two of our most requested capabilities to plugins: Branching and Publishing. Together, they unlock new plugin workflows, from experimenting on a branch to shipping your site. We’ve also rebuilt our API docs with search, improved content, and better linking. For the complete technical rundown, read the changelog. Find an overview of what’s new below. Branching Added createBranch to create and switch to a new branch Added the Branch class to switch, merge, and delete branches Added getBranch and getBranches to look up branches by ID Added subscribeToBranches to react to branch changes live Publishing Added publish to ship a project’s changes from a plugin Added deploy to push a published version to a custom domain Added getUnpublishedPageChanges to list changes since publish Added getDeployment and getDeploymentIssues to track deploys Plugins Added a url property to Font for its source file Added PathNode and ShapeGroupNode for imported vectors Added createdAt and updatedAt timestamps to collection items Added ShapeContainerNode and BooleanShapeNode node types Notion: Relation fields now support up to 100 references Notion: Added faster, clearer sync error reports

news.body: Procedures are now generally available in ElevenAgents. A procedure contains task-specific instructions and a trigger that determines when they apply. During a conversation, the agent loads the relevant procedure, allowing one agent to handle distinct tasks without placing every instruction in its system prompt. Use free-form procedures when the agent can adapt the wording or order of instructions. Use structured procedures when steps must run in a defined order. Both types can be used alongside workflows on the same agent.

news.title: Music v2
news.body:

news.title: App User Connectors
news.body: Lovable apps now work with each user's connected tools. Ship one app; each user connects their own account and gets a personalized app based on their data, workflows, and role-based permissions, for example, a team assistant that pulls from the user's Drive and Calendar. Lovable manages the credentials, security, monitoring, and availability so you just build.

news.title: Status-Aware Favicon
news.body: Lovable added a little something for working across multiple projects: your browser-tab favicon now reflects status, showing when Lovable is building, when your input is needed, and when a task is completed, so you can tell at a glance without switching tabs.

news.title: Use Lovable Apps Inside ChatGPT and Claude
news.body: Lovable apps can now be used directly within ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI tools. Enable agent integrations on a published app and Lovable reads its logic, generates an MCP server listing its actions, and hosts it for you, protected by OAuth by default with security checks at publish time. Your assistant can then run the app's actions in conversation.

news.title: Sonnet 5 in Lovable
news.body: Lovable now supports Claude Sonnet 5 — benchmarks show it gets more done for less and excels at catching risky requests, with improved security capabilities over the previous Sonnet model.

news.title: Automated Project Monitoring
news.body: Lovable introduced automated project monitoring — it checks your app on a schedule and alerts you when something breaks, fails silently, or looks wrong, before anyone notices. In beta now.

news.title: Text-to-Speech & Speech-to-Text
news.body: Your app talks back — Lovable now supports text-to-speech and speech-to-text, so you can seamlessly add AI voice features to your projects. Make a voice assistant, a hands-free tool, or an app you can literally speak to.

news.title: Build in Lovable, from Claude
news.body: New native integrations via the Lovable MCP server — chat to Claude, export from Claude Design, and ship with Claude Code, directly to Lovable. To start, go to Claude → + → Connectors → Browse Connectors → Lovable.

news.title: Lovable Shopify Integration
news.body: Introducing the Lovable Shopify integration — build online stores by chatting with AI. To show how it works, Lovable built and launched its first merch store.

news.title: TanStack Start
news.body: Lovable rebuilt its foundations on TanStack Start for server-side rendering — better discoverability from search engines and AI answer engines like ChatGPT and Perplexity.

news.title: Security Scan
news.body: Lovable now automatically runs a security scan before you publish — checking for database misconfigurations, missing RLS policies, and authorization gaps in 10–15 seconds.

news.title: Granola Connector
news.body: The Granola connector is live on Lovable — pull your meeting notes straight in and start building.

news.title: Subagents in Lovable
news.body: Lovable can now spin up helper subagents behind the scenes to research, review, and QA in parallel. Subagents appear in the activity log alongside the main build, so you can trace any decision back to its source.

news.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash in Lovable Apps
news.body: Add Gemini 3.5 Flash to the apps you build with Lovable — works well for agentic features.

news.title: Lovable's Google Connectors Are Live
news.body: Lovable's Google connectors are live. You can now build full-stack apps that talk directly to data from Google: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Maps, Gemini Enterprise, and BigQuery.

news.title: Introducing Skills in Lovable
news.body: Lovable introduced Skills — a markdown-based system for reusable instruction sets the AI remembers across sessions. Encode workflows once, then load them contextually as personal or team playbooks. Five built-in skills available now; ask Lovable to make a skill or call a specific one with /.

news.title: Skills in Lovable — Ground-Up Explainer
news.body: Tyler Bruno wrote a ground-up walkthrough of how Lovable Skills (and Skills in general) actually work and how to write a good one. Worth a read for anyone building with Lovable or any AI tool using Skills.

news.title: Server-Side Rendering + Semrush for SEO/AEO
news.body: Your Lovable apps are now built to be found. New apps are server-side rendered and discoverable through search engines like Google and AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity — existing apps get prerendering. Plus Semrush search intelligence in-app: chat with your SEO data, understand how you're performing, run SEO reviews on demand, and fix all suggestions in one click.

news.title: Aesthetics — Design Control in Vibe Coding
news.body: Lovable launched Aesthetics — a new design control layer inside vibe coding. Specify typography, layout, and color preferences, then preview design concepts before Lovable builds anything.

news.title: Built for Moms (with Wispr Flow)
news.body: Lovable kicked off a 'Built for Moms' contest with Wispr Flow — build a tool for the moms in your life.

news.title: Lovable MCP Server (Research Preview)
news.body: Lovable released its MCP server in research preview — create projects, send messages, inspect code, and deploy apps directly from your terminal or AI agent.

news.title: Wiz Findings Now in Lovable
news.body: Lovable integrated Wiz security scanning natively — vulnerability findings surface alongside built-in checks, with unified visibility for security teams in their Wiz dashboard.

news.title: GPT Image 2 in Lovable
news.body: Lovable added GPT Image 2 to its image generation stack.

news.title: Telegram Integration
news.body: Lovable now integrates with Telegram — build, ship,and trigger your apps from a Telegram bot.

news.title: $1 Custom Domains (3-Day Promo)
news.body: For 3 days only — buy a custom domain inside Lovable for just $1.

news.title: Lovable Mobile App
news.body: Introducing the Lovable mobile app. Your ideas won't wait — now you can build them anywhere.

news.title: Opus 4.7 Now in Lovable
news.body: Lovable now supports Claude Opus 4.7. Benchmarks show it completes tasks in 40% fewer turns. Discounted rates through April 30 — your credits go even further.

news.title: Lovable Desktop App
news.body: Lovable now has a desktop app. Access local MCPs, build across multiple project tabs, and use native keyboard shortcuts.

news.title: Introducing Lovable Payments
news.body:
Describe what you want to sell. Test it securely. One conversation to go live.
Integrate with Stripe, Paddle, or Shopify seamlessly from Lovable.

news.title: Introducing Lovable Academy
news.body:
Your guide to building real apps with AI. Templates, tips for prompting, and learning paths for everyone from first-time vibe coders to experienced devs.
We'll help you come up with ideas of what to build, tailored to your role and existing problems.

Learn more → academy.lovable.app

title: Luma AI
description: Scan real objects and scenes with a phone camera into photorealistic 3D models using NeRF, or generate 3D assets and video with Dream Machine.

news.title: GPT-Image 2.5 in Luma Agents
news.body: GPT-Image 2.5 is now live in Luma Agents. Use Flare for speed and volume, or Sunburst for precise edits and maximum fidelity—bring a reference, change what is off, keep the rest, and take it into video.

news.title: Live Text Extraction in Layers
news.body: Luma Layers can now extract baked-in text as editable live text, matching it to the closest library font. Select a layer, hit Extract, then retype, swap the font, and recompose without regenerating the image. Powered by Uni-1.

news.title: Seedance 2.5 on Luma
news.body: Seedance 2.5 has landed on Luma. Create up to 30 seconds of multi-shot, high-definition video in a single generation using up to 50 references across text, image, video, and audio. With Luma Agents, control scenes, camera angles, and pacing to produce your next masterpiece.

news.title: Layers in Luma Agents
news.body: Layers is now live in Luma Agents. Ask the agent to extract layers from any image, generated in Luma or uploaded, then keep chatting: swap the product, restyle the background, rewrite the headline. Change one element, preserve everything else. Powered by Uni-1.

news.title: Seedance 2.0 Mini in Luma
news.body: Seedance 2.0 Mini is now available in Luma — generate video fast enough to keep up with how you actually work. Storyboard a concept, test a dozen directions, and land on the cut before the idea cools. Powerful output with a lighter footprint.

news.title: Luma Connectors
news.body: Luma Connectors is live — plug Airtable, Dropbox, and Google Drive into Luma and pull files into any board on demand.

news.title: Seedance 2.0 Joins Luma Agents
news.body: Luma Agents can now generate with Seedance 2.0. Point your next project at it, see what it produces, keep moving. Same workflow, more to work with. Open Luma Agents at lumalabs.ai/app.

news.title: Kling Omni in Luma Agents
news.body: Luma Agents can now generate with Kling Omni — more models, more range, same workflow.

news.title: UNI-1 Inside Envato
news.body: Luma's UNI-1 model now powers Envato's image generator and image editor — sharper visual styles from reference and natural single-element edits.

news.title: Uni-1.1 API
news.body: Luma launched the Uni-1.1 API — first-pass results across fashion, architecture, manga, and cinematic verticals.

news.title: Innovative Dreams — Hybrid Filmmaking Studio
news.body: Announcing Innovative Dreams, a new production company by Luma and Wonder Project. Building a new Hybrid Production process — actors, artists, and generative AI working together in real time.

title: Luminar Neo
description: One-click AI sky replacement, object removal, portrait and lighting fixes, plus layer-based compositing — standalone or as a Lightroom plugin.

title: Moment
description: Marketplace and community for photographers — expert-tested camera gear and mobile lenses, video courses from working pros, and guided photo trips.

title: OpusClip
description: Turns long podcasts and webinars into short vertical clips for TikTok, Shorts, and Reels — AI picks the moments, adds captions, and reframes.

news.title: OpusClip in ChatGPT
news.body: OpusClip is now available in ChatGPT. In one conversation, you can analyze footage, create clips, write captions, and publish across platforms. OpusClip says the plugin is free to try.

media.alt: OpusClip demonstration inside ChatGPT

news.title: OpusClip Is Now a Claude Connector
news.body: OpusClip is now an official Claude connector, so you can edit videos and grow your social accounts directly inside Claude — no API keys or settings digging required. Connect OpusClip from Claude’s Connectors menu, then prompt it to work with your content.

news.title: Introducing AI Producer for ChatGPT
news.body: AI Producer is now available in ChatGPT. Drop in raw footage and chat with AI to add captions, B-roll, motion graphics, music, and SFX — powered by GPT-6 Astra.

news.title: Brand Vocabulary: Names Transcribed Right, Every Clip
news.body: Everybody has a word an automated transcript keeps getting wrong: a brand name, a cofounder's last name, a product mentioned forty times an episode. Brand Vocabulary lets you save names, terms and proper nouns once in the Asset Library, and every clip after that transcribes them correctly. Select the wrong word, correct it, and click Add to Brand Vocabulary; the fix applies to the clip you are in and carries forward to the next one.

news.title: AI Producer Is Available Now
news.body: The gap between raw footage and a produced video just disappeared: AI Producer is available now. Drop in your raw footage, chat with it to get exactly the edit you want, and it builds smart, dynamic motion graphics that land on your exact words, maximizing retention.

news.title: Detect Retakes
news.body: OpusClip can now find and remove bad takes and filler words. Hit Detect Retakes and every retake, restart, and self-correction gets flagged inline, so you see exactly what it found and where. It flags, you approve, and the timeline stays yours.

news.title: Auto Headline in Brand Templates
news.body: Auto Headline is now part of your OpusClip brand template. Set your headline style once (font, color, position) and every clip generated with that brand template comes out with the headline already styled and burned in. Turn it on right from Auto Import, no extra setup, for consistent branding across all your videos.

news.title: Introducing Auto SFX
news.body: The hardest part of editing is finding the right sounds. OpusClip's Auto SFX finds the moments that need sound and places the effects for you: upload your video and hit auto generate, or hit generate by prompt and type what you hear ('typing on a keyboard,' 'background chatter in a noisy bar') to get 3 variations. Available now on all Pro and Business plans.

news.title: Introducing Video Dubbing
news.body: OpusClip launched Video Dubbing: clone your voice from a video you already made, translate your content into 25 language markets (Spanish, Japanese, French, Korean, Portuguese, and more), and sync the dubbed audio to your timeline in minutes. Voice cloning is automatic with no separate training, you can fix translations by editing the transcript inline without re-dubbing, and you can dub multiple videos in bulk. Available on all Pro and Business plans.

news.title: Introducing the OpusClip MCP
news.body: The #1 AI video clipping product is now agent friendly. The OpusClip MCP gives your AI agent social media superpowers: connect it to Claude, ChatGPT, or any MCP client and clip, caption, and repurpose video from inside the conversation.

news.title: OpusClip on Android
news.body: OpusClip is now on Android — paste a YouTube link or upload a video and its AI turns your long video into 10+ short, vertical, ready-to-post clips. Every clip gets a Virality Score from 0 to 99 based on hook, flow, and trend, plus animated captions and auto-reframing. Live now on Google Play.

news.title: AI Upscaler
news.body: OpusClip launched an AI Upscaler — feed it low-res footage, hit "upscale", and it automatically makes your video sharper and cleaner so your clips look professional on every screen.

news.title: Custom Thumbnails on OpusClip Posts
news.body: Your thumbnail is the first thing people see. You can now set custom thumbnails on your OpusClip posts — pick any frame from your video, or upload your own image, then apply it across every platform with one click.

news.title: OpusClip API in Beta on Every Pro Plan
news.body: The OpusClip API is now in beta, included on every Pro plan. Pair it with Claude Code and agent workflows: bulk ingest top moments from long-form content, scan and adjust clips at scale, and schedule posts across TikTok, Reels, and YouTube Shorts automatically.

news.title: Scheduler API
news.body: OpusClip rolled out a Scheduler API — programmatically queue and post AI clips to social platforms straight from the OpusClip pipeline.

news.title: 4K Support
news.body: OpusClip now supports uploading and exporting in 4K — your highest-quality footage stays that way through the editing process.

title: Restream
description: Broadcast one live stream to 30+ platforms at once — YouTube, Twitch, Facebook, LinkedIn, X — with merged chat, overlays, and a browser studio.

news.title: Slack Is Now a Streaming Destination
news.body: Restream can now stream to Slack. Your team can watch town halls, demo days, and company-wide announcements right where work happens. Restream is hosting a live demo and Q&A on X on August 12 at 12 PM NY time.

news.title: 3 Million Clips Generated
news.body: Restream crossed 3 million clips generated, with its clipping feature turning creators into one-person content machines. The pace is accelerating: the first million took 8 months, the second 5, and the third about 3.

news.title: Manual Clipping Joins AI Clips
news.body: Automatic clipping is great until you want one specific moment. Now you choose in Restream: let AI pick your best clips, or select any part of the timeline and clip it yourself.

news.title: Control Who Comments on X Live Streams
news.body: When you stream to X via Restream, you can now decide who joins the conversation — controlling who can comment on your live streams.

news.title: Ask AI in Analytics
news.body: Ask AI in Restream Analytics reads your stream transcripts and live chats, then tells you what worked and what to do next in plain English. Grow your audience with data.

title: VEED
description: Browser-based video editor with AI auto-subtitles, screen and webcam recording, background removal, AI avatars, and team collaboration.

news.title: Clone Yourself in VEED
news.body: VEED launched a feature for making social videos from a photo, a voice recording, and a script, without filming each video.

media.alt: VEED demonstration of its Clone Yourself feature

news.title: The New VEED
news.body: VEED's rebuilt editor turns one prompt into a post-ready video, then leaves the pieces editable: swap characters, change camera angles, restyle subtitles, or switch the music without starting again.

news.title: OpenEdit on Windows
news.body: OpenEdit, VEED's open source agentic video editor, now runs on Windows. It builds complex motion graphics from a single prompt, and the announcement video was made in OpenEdit itself. Available from the veedstudio/open-edit repository on GitHub.

news.title: Introducing OpenEdit
news.body: VEED introduced OpenEdit, an open source agentic video editor. Install it with npx skills add veedstudio/open-edit, and VEED will DM the source code to anyone who retweets and comments 'Edit'.

news.title: Multi-Shot Characters
news.body: VEED introduced Multi-Shot Characters: create AI videos from multiple camera angles to boost viewer retention, cut out hours of editing, and get realistic results.

news.title: VEED Lip Sync 2.0 API
news.body: VEED launched the Lip Sync 2.0 API: one video, endless versions. Change the hook, fix lines, or dub, at scale, built on VEED's most powerful model to date. It handles objects blocking the face, low lighting, fast camera movements, and multiple angles, and launches with Magnific as a partner.

news.title: VEED MCP Is Here
news.body: VEED launched its MCP — use VEED inside AI workflows like OpenClaw, Hermes, Claude, and Cursor for video creation at scale with your agents. A free guide and skill file help you get started.

news.title: VEED Fabric + Subtitle API / Melius
news.body: VEED Fabric and Subtitle API now power Melius — a creative canvas for AI agents that generates talking videos with polished subtitles at scale.

news.title: Customisable Avatars Mobile
news.body: VEED's Customisable Avatars are now on the VEED mobile app — change clothes, hair, and vibe, add script, and generate in one flow.

news.title: Introducing VEED's Subtitles API
news.body: The world's most powerful subtitles, now available via API. 100+ languages, highest fidelity, 28 style presets. One integration. Endless engagement. Free fal API credits for the first 300 users who retweet and comment 'Subs'.

news.title: VEED Subtitles API — Launch Partners
news.body: VEED Subtitles API is live with launch partners: Figma Weave, Arcads, GIMI, BigMotion, PolishedAds, Creative Fabrica, and Clara — first to ship the API in their platforms.

news.title: VEED Fabric MCP Live in Make
news.body: VEED Fabric MCP went live inside Make — open MCP server that lets agents generate video with VEED's Fabric 1.0 model as a native step in 100+ workflow use cases.

news.title: VEED × Epidemic Sound
news.body: VEED partnered with Epidemic Sound — 55,000+ royalty-free music tracks now available inside the editor.

news.title: VEED ChatGPT MCP App
news.body: VEED launched its ChatGPT MCP app — turn chats intovideos right inside ChatGPT.

news.title: 4K Background Remover API
news.body: Background removal just hit a new bar. VEED's Video Background Remover API delivers true 4K resolution, studio-grade cutouts, and handles talking heads and fast-paced motion.

news.title: Multi-Shot Characters in VEED
news.body: Get multiple camera angles in one click. Skip hours of editing, keep retention high, post in minutes instead of days. Introducing multi-shot characters on VEED.

news.title: Customizable Avatars on Mobile
news.body: Introducing Customizable Avatars on VEED's mobile app. Make your AI avatars reflect your brand — pick any character, change clothes, hair, and vibe, add script and generate in one flow.

title: Capsule
description: AI video editor for marketing teams — works from your brand assets, templates, and motion design systems so videos come out on-brand and editable.

news.title: Introducing Video Skills
news.body: Capsule introduced Video Skills: make a video in Claude or ChatGPT that follows your exact video workflow, uses your assets and motion systems, and stays fully editable. Not slop.

title: Riverside
description: Remote recording studio for podcasts and video interviews — records locally on each device in up to 4K with separate tracks per participant.

news.title: Cinematic Zoom Effects in Riverside Editor
news.body: Riverside added cinematic zoom effects to its editor, letting creators pan, zoom, and add movement to videos.

media.alt: Riverside demonstration of cinematic zoom effects

news.title: AI Image and Video Generation in Riverside
news.body: AI image and video generation with world-class models is now in Riverside. Seedance 2.5, Veo 3.1, Nano Banana: take your pick. Generate b-roll, intros, guest cards, cover art, and more, right where you already edit your content, for a more professional look.

news.title: Riverside Rebuilt Its Mobile App
news.body: Riverside rebuilt its mobile app. Record high-quality video content, review your latest edit, and post clips straight from your phone. Inspiration doesn't happen exclusively at your desk, and now you can create content from literally anywhere.

news.title: Motion Graphics in the Riverside Editor
news.body: Motion graphics are now on Riverside. Generate and customize them right in the editor to make your videos look more professional and expensive.

news.title: Publish Video to Apple Podcasts
news.body: You can now publish video to Apple Podcasts directly from Riverside. Your podcast has somewhere new to show your face.

news.title: In-Person Multicam Recording
news.body: In-person multicam recording is now on Riverside. Capture multiple cameras in the same room, so you get the chemistry of a live conversation, not just the audio, in a single synced recording.

news.title: The First Agentic Editor That Understands Your Conversation
news.body: Riverside launched what it calls the first agentic editor that understands your conversation. Instead of manual cuts, the editor comprehends what was actually said in your recording and edits around the content, turning a raw conversation into a finished piece.

news.title: Social Scheduling on Riverside
news.body: Riverside now supports social scheduling — schedule your content to publish across social platforms and log off, all from inside Riverside.

news.title: Riverside 2.0
news.body: Riverside launched Riverside 2.0 — pitched as the first AI Producer that creates authentic content while you sleep, turning your recordings into ready-to-post content rather than generic AI slop.

news.title: VideoDub Roadmap (Post-Pipio)
news.body: Riverside laid out the VideoDub roadmap following the Pipio acquisition — sharper lip sync, motion, and identity edits without reshoots or AI avatars, rolling out over coming releases.

news.title: Riverside Acquires Pipio (EditYourself)
news.body: Riverside is welcoming the Pipio team — builders of EditYourself, a model that lets you edit your own footage without reshoots or avatars. Better, faster AI editing on Riverside is on the way, starting with improvements to VideoDub.

news.body: Shotbase 1.5.0 adds three local AI model choices for different Mac capabilities, an option to dismiss Quick Access automatically after a capture, and a shortcut to open the latest capture in the editor. It also improves motion framing and camera behavior, and fixes recording, annotation, timeline, and model-download issues.

title: Screen Studio
description: Mac screen recorder that turns raw captures into polished demo videos — smooth cursor motion, auto-zoom on clicks, and custom backgrounds.

news.title: Screen Studio Can Automatically Mask Sensitive Data
news.body: Screen Studio can now scan every frame of a recording and automatically mask sensitive information such as email addresses, credit card numbers, and API keys. The team says analyzing a 20-second recording takes about six seconds on an M3 Mac. Face masking is coming soon.

news.title: Screen Studio Projects Now Preview in Finder
news.body: Screen Studio now integrates with Finder preview, so you can see a project preview before opening it. This makes it easier to find the right recording when you have many projects in one folder.

news.title: Screen Studio 4.0 Upscales macOS Screen Recordings
news.body: Screen Studio 4.0 introduces a custom AI model for upscaling macOS screen recordings. The team trained it using screenshots from 5,000 randomly generated SwiftUI apps, downscaled to teach the model how to restore screen content.

news.body: An articulation of the creative principles that define Squarespace — grounding the brand in what they've always believed: that taste, human creativity, and a clear point of view matter more than ever, especially for entrepreneurs and creators building something that lasts.

news.title: Suno Studio: Improved MIDI and more
news.body: We’ve made improvements to Studio’s MIDI performance, and now working with MIDI in Studio is much more accurate and creatively inspiring. Specifically, transcription from MIDI to audio is faster, has more musical context, and is more accurate to the original. For example, you can ask the chat bar to create new audio stems based on a MIDI clip and get super accurate results. Another benefit of the new update is that prompting MIDI from scratch using the chat bar yields much better and more expected results. These improvements open up a whole new world of creative possibilities that are unique to the Suno experience. Upload MIDI files from long-lost compositions made outside of Suno, then breathe new life into them in Studio. Ever wondered what your synth parts would sound like as a guitar solo... or gamelan orchestra!? Now you can find out, and we hope these discoveries inspire you to take your creativity further. Aside from the MIDI improvements, we have also fixed some bugs and made some general usability updates. For example, you can now rename clips either individually (right-click on the clip and select Rename) or using the chat bar, with a prompt like “ rename all my clips to

news.title: Updates to Suno Studio
news.body: It’s been a couple of weeks since we launched Studio 2.0 , the biggest ever update to our browser-based DAW. We’re constantly working on making improvements, and we’re excited to announce a couple of updates that we hope will make your Studio experience even better. Here’s what’s new: Chat improvements We've updated the chat bar performance, and the latest improvements make it aware of bpm, so now it can process tempo changes. It’s also more reliable and more rational with its responses, and you can now undo prompt edits. Copy and duplicate plugins You can now move and copy plugins from one track to another by dragging and dropping. (Previously you needed to copy and paste in separate steps.) You can also use cmd-D (Mac) or ctrl-D (PC) to duplicate plugins on the same track, and you can also drag-and-drop while holding the option key to duplicate from one track to another. Wavetable fidelity We improved the performance of the wavetable synth, so now you no longer experience aliasing at high frequency. This should result in cleaner and more detailed synth sounds, and smoother frequency shifts. Overall responsiveness Audio playback is faster and projects load more quickly, so Studio

news.title: Free credit incentives for pay-per-use accounts
news.body: Pay-per-use accounts can now earn free X API credits two ways: a one-time \$20 when an account saves its first eligible payment card, and a one-time match of the first successful auto-recharge, up to \$50. A new account that earns both receives \$70 in free credits. Credits are applied automatically with no code or form, appear in the Developer Console within about a minute, are spent before purchased credits, and expire 3 months after they are granted. The incentives are rolling out now. See Free credit incentives for eligibility rules, examples, and FAQ.

news.title: Real-time reply moderation guide now uses Grok
news.body: We rewrote the Manage replies in real time integration guide. It now receives replies through the X Activity API post.reply.create event, classifies each reply with Grok through the xAI API using structured outputs, and hides high-confidence violations with the Hide Replies endpoint. The previous version relied on the deprecated Perspective API and the Account Activity API. The guide includes complete Python and Node.js webhook examples, guidance on writing the moderation policy, and recommendations for keeping users in control of what is hidden.

news.title: Broadcast chat removal events for X Activity API
news.body: Today, we added the broadcast.chat.remove event to the X Activity API. Subscribe by User ID with the broadcast.read scope to be notified in real time when the host or a moderator removes a chat message from a broadcast the user owns. The payload carries the broadcast_id and the message_id of the removed message. See Event payloads for a sample delivery.

news.title: X Rebuilds Livestream API
news.body: X rebuilt its Livestream API to support the full broadcast workflow: going live, scheduling broadcasts, managing and moderating chat, and receiving live events for alerts and overlays. The API is available now.

media.alt: X Developers announcement of the rebuilt Livestream API

news.title: Migrate OAuth 1.0a user tokens to OAuth 2.0 with token exchange
news.body: Apps with existing OAuth 1.0a users can now exchange each user's stored OAuth 1.0a access token and secret for an OAuth 2.0 access token and refresh token, with no consent screen or re-authorization. Send grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange to POST /2/oauth2/token; the granted scopes are derived from the permissions the user originally authorized, and offline.access is always included. See Migrating OAuth 1.0a user tokens to OAuth 2.0 for the request format, permission-to-scope mapping, rate limits, and error handling.

news.title: Conversion API Google Tag Manager server-side template
news.body: Advertisers can now send website conversions through the official X Ads Conversion API (Official) tag in a Google Tag Manager server container, without writing Conversion API request code. See Set up the Conversion API with Google Tag Manager for Pixel ID, access token, event mapping, and Pixel + Conversion API deduplication steps. The template is published in the Google Tag Manager Community Template Gallery.

news.title: REGIONS segmentation for Analytics
news.body: Asynchronous analytics jobs now support REGIONS as a segmentation_type. The country parameter is required when requesting a regional breakdown. See Metrics and Segmentation for the full list of enabled segmentation types.

news.title: Lead Generation API
news.body: We documented the Lead Generation API for Lead Gen campaigns. You can now create and manage native lead forms, attach a form to a card with the LEAD_FORM destination, and export submitted leads as JSON, CSV, or XLSX. POST /12/accounts/:account\_id/lead\_forms creates a form (introduction, fields, privacy policy, and optional thank-you page) POST /12/accounts/:account\_id/cards accepts destination type LEAD_FORM POST /12/accounts/:account\_id/ad-export/api/v1/exports with entity_type=leads exports submissions for a form and time window The Leads API requires the Campaign user permission. Lead exports are restricted to account administrators.

news.title: Media upload and Post-create size and duration limits
news.body: We documented the size and duration limits that apply when uploading media and when attaching it to a Post. Upload and POST /2/tweets are separately enforced. Limits follow the authenticated user's X Premium / verified status and media_category, not your developer API plan. Default accounts: Post video up to 20 minutes and 8 GB (tweet_video / amplify_video) X Premium / verified: Post video up to 125 minutes and 16 GB Direct Message video is unchanged: 140 seconds / 512 MB default, 10 minutes / 1 GB Premium Exceeding the posting user's duration cap returns 403 This user is not allowed to post a video longer than N minutes. The chunked upload quickstart now uses the v2 paths (POST /2/media/upload/initialize, /{id}/append, /{id}/finalize) instead of the previous command-style POST /2/media/upload flow.

news.title: Updated video_total_views definition
news.body: We updated the definition of the video_total_views metric in the VIDEO metrics group of the X Ads API Analytics endpoints. It now reports views that are 100% in-view for at least 3 seconds, plus any view where a user manually clicks the play button. The previous definition (at least 50% in-view for 2 seconds, per the MRC standard) no longer applies. The prior "100% in-view for 3 seconds" definition remains available as the video_3s100pct_views metric, and you can continue bidding on it via the VIEW_3S_100PCT bid unit.

news.title: Platform MCP Server
news.body: fal's second MCP server — the Platform API MCP — is now available at https://api.fal.ai/v1/mcp/platform. Where the Run MCP lets your AI assistant *build with models*, this one lets it *operate your fal account*: connect Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible client with your API key and ask *"why did my last request to my-app fail?"* — your assistant walks the same debugging steps you would. 15 tools: eleven first-class serverless debugging tools covering requests, logs, error analytics, deploy and revision history, runner and queue state, spend, and persistent storage — plus a four-tool discovery gateway that opens up the rest of the Platform API (compute, workflows, keys, account, organization, storage) without bloating your assistant's context. bash theme={null} claude mcp add --transport http fal-platform \ https://api.fal.ai/v1/mcp/platform \ --header "Authorization: Key YOUR_FAL_KEY" Read-only — it can observe your account but never change it; write operations are listed in the catalog but refuse to execute Stateless — your key is sent per-request and never stored, and normal permission and ownership scoping applies Free — tool calls are the same Platform API calls you co

news.title: New Serverless Observability APIs
news.body: A batch of endpoints rounds out programmatic access to what the dashboard shows about your serverless apps: GET /v1/serverless/apps — list your deployed apps with live state: active runners, queue size, machine types, and environment. Add expand=endpoints to include each app's route-level endpoint ids, in the exact form the requests and analytics APIs accept. GET /v1/serverless/apps/{owner}/{name}/events — operational event history: deployments, configuration changes, and runner lifecycle transitions — the "what changed around this time?" API. Also surfaced in the dashboard's events timeline. GET /v1/serverless/apps/{owner}/{name}/revisions — revision history with deployment status, who deployed, and deploy messages and annotations (the API behind the August 3 entry above) — line revision boundaries up against your error timeline to spot a bad deploy. GET /v1/serverless/apps/{owner}/{name}/runners/history — historical runner counts by state (running, idle, pending, draining) for capacity analysis and incident forensics. Together with the existing requests, logs, analytics, metrics, and usage APIs, these power the new Platform MCP server — and they're plain REST endpoints you can ca

news.title: GPU Utilization in Runner Telemetry
news.body: Runner telemetry now includes a dedicated GPU Utilization chart alongside the existing CPU, memory, and VRAM charts, so you can see how much compute your GPUs are actually doing -- not just how much memory they hold. GPU Utilization reports the average compute utilization across a runner's GPUs over time, surfaced both as a current stat and a time-series chart in the runner side sheet. Pair it with VRAM Usage to tell a memory-bound runner apart from a compute-bound one, making it easier to right-size machine types and spot under-utilized GPUs. Open any runner from the Runners page (Dashboard → Apps → \[your-app] → Runners) to view its telemetry. See Runner Analytics for details.

news.title: Deploy Messages and Annotations
news.body: You can now attach a freeform message and custom annotations to each revision when deploying: bash theme={null} fal deploy my_app.py::MyApp --message "Deploying new version" --annotation GIT_SHA=a1b2c3d4 Messages and annotations are set at deploy time and stay with the revision. View and search them on the app's Versions page in the dashboard, or fetch them via the revisions API. Also available in the Python SDK: client.deploy(..., message=..., annotations={...}). See Annotating Deployments for details.

news.title: Fibo Edit 1.5 on fal
news.body: Fibo Edit 1.5 from Bria is live on fal. It now accepts up to four reference images, so you supply the actual product, garment or character rather than describing it and the identity carries through. It is built for catalog and ad production: product placement, virtual try-on and consistent characters.

news.title: Muse Image from Meta
news.body: Muse Image, Meta's agentic image model, is live on fal. It plans the composition, uses tools and self-corrects before returning anything, which is aimed at complex briefs that usually fall apart partway through.

news.title: Gemini Omni Flash 1.1 on fal
news.body: Gemini Omni Flash 1.1 is on fal, processing text, image and video together rather than in sequence. It brings Gemini's real-world and physics knowledge to generation, and edits through conversation while holding character and scene consistent across turns.

news.title: H3 Max
news.body: H3 Max is a post-trained video model from fal Research. fal says it ranks first for overall quality, prompt understanding and aesthetics against leading video models on both its own and third-party independent evaluations, while generating a 5-second 720p video in under three seconds. It is 50% off for a week from launch.

news.title: H3 Max Live
news.body: fal has H3 Max generating video faster than real time. The demo is an infinite broadcast where every frame is generated on the fly and each scene is directed from chat: type !prompt and it is on screen within seconds.

news.title: MiniMax H3 on fal
news.body: MiniMax H3 is now available on fal. The physics are insane: water that lands with real weight, cloth that clings once it's soaked. A slow push-in on the face holds up too.

news.title: Mirage Avatar X API on fal
news.body: The Mirage Avatar X API is live on fal. Build expressive avatar experiences with Mirage's most advanced generation model yet, with identity preservation across AI video. Get started with audio and an optional visual reference.

news.title: Introducing fal Agent
news.body: Following a week of frontier video model launches, fal is opening early access to something it's been building: fal Agent, a creative partner for working across the best image, video, and 3D models.

news.title: Seedance 2.5 on fal
news.body: Seedance 2.5 is live on fal. In fal's demo, the input is a still image with a red squiggle, and the output is a continuous FPV run through the torii gate with a full lap around the monorail. Nobody keyframed anything.

news.title: Veed Lip Sync 2.0 on fal
news.body: Lip Sync 2.0 from VEED is now live on fal. Swap the audio on any video and automatically match the lips, emotion, style, and timing, no training or fine-tuning required. Process footage up to 4K, clips up to 10 minutes, with controllable sync strength.

news.title: LTX-2.3 Reframe on fal
news.body: LTX-2.3 Reframe is now live on fal, from LTX. Convert any video to a new aspect ratio: landscape to vertical, square, and back (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5, 5:4). Newly exposed areas are generated to match the original scene, with up to 60 seconds of input and 720p or 1080p outputs.

news.title: Seed Audio 1.0
news.body: ByteDance's Seed Audio 1.0 is now available on fal — generate natural speech, sound design, and music from text. Try it today.

news.title: Open-Sourcing 3DREAL
news.body: fal open-sourced 3DREAL — a render-to-real IC-LoRA for LTX-2.3 that turns any 3D, CG, or game render into photorealistic, film-quality video while keeping your exact composition and camera move from the first frame.

news.title: LTX 2.3 Video Effects
news.body: A new set of LTX 2.3 video effects is live on fal — apply an effect to any video in a single pass with in-context effect LoRAs: water simulation, cross-eyed, day to night, colorization, deblur, decompression, and instant shave.

news.title: The Figma agent is generally available

news.title: Post riffs to Figma Community

news.body: Motion becomes more reusable, expressive, and portable this release, giving teams a faster path from first keyframe to polished, handoff-ready animations.

news.title: Smoother design collaboration and navigation on mobile
news.body: New improvements to Figma’s mobile app for smoother collaboration and navigation.

news.title: Vertical wrap available in auto layout

news.title: Figma and Handshake Launch AI Skills Missions
news.body: Figma partnered with Handshake’s AI Skills Studio and announced four creative missions: design and animate an icon set, build a looping animation, illustrate a sticker pack, and turn a mood board into app mockups. The Handshake partner page lists the missions currently available.

news.title: Updated iOS and iPadOS 27 UI Kit, Now with Duo

news.title: Publish Weave tools to the Figma Community

news.body: Starting today, Org Admins on the Enterprise plan can set a public link sharing policy for Design and FigJam files at the workspace level.

news.title: Visual customization for workspaces

news.title: Little Big Updates Week 4: Visual improvements to how you work in Figma
news.body: Week 4 of LBU includes small tweaks to the visual experience of designing in Figma.

news.title: Collaborate on Figma or FigJam files - directly in Google Meet
news.body: No more tab switching, no more missed comments, and way more interaction and collaboration with your team.

news.title: Control opacity at scale
news.body: Opacity can be updated at scale in the variables modal and applied on top of any color without detaching.

news.title: Download Payout Statements in Community

news.title: Autogenerated passwords (Professional & Organization plans)

news.title: Password protection options (Enterprise plan)

news.body: The final week of LBU includes a number of updates to Figma’s design editor, our collaboration tools, and the prototyping experience.

news.body: Give your team jams a boost with 3 new AI features in FigJam.

news.title: Updated Corner Radius UI
news.body: We updated the corner radius UI so that it's easier to bind a variable to each individual corner.

news.title: Updated naming convention for paid seats

news.body: Figma now allows you to create one additional Figma or FigJam file while offline, so you can keep your ideas flowing.

news.body: Variables can now be bound to new fields in Figma.

news.body: Org admins on enterprise accounts can now designate workspaces as “hidden” for more control over their sensitive content.

news.title: Billing groups

news.title: New Community pages layout

news.title: Updates to managing team and project access
news.body: Updates to create a clearer and simpler experience when granting or managing access to teams and projects. These updates will be rolling out from now through early March.

news.title: In file videos and images can now be localized to the EU
news.body: We’ve expanded our EU file hosting capabilities to support localization of videos and images in addition to previously supported assets.

news.title: Approved libraries
news.body: Starting today Org and Workspace admins on the Enterprise plan can mark libraries as approved for the organization or for workspaces they manage

news.title: Sections and Branch Review compatibility!
news.body: Reviewers now have the ability to inspect each individual change within a section during branch review. This offers a more comprehensive review process when content is nested within sections.

news.title: Updates to the Figma for Jira App, now in GA
news.body: We’re introducing the new Figma for Jira app in general availability. Since the beta launch, we've shipped fast follows to help you increase productivity in Jira.

news.title: Check network settings
news.body: Searching for "check network settings" in quick actions will open a network settings modal, which indicates whether any of these services are blocked.

news.body: Last year we launched Dev Mode in open beta as a better way for teams to go from idea to code. Today, Dev Mode is officially out of beta and will require a paid seat to use.

news.title: Variable modes are now always selectable
news.body: In the past, incompatible modes were disabled. Now, they will be selectable. When a variable with an incompatible mode is selected, it uses its default value.

news.title: FigJam for Google Meet Hardware
news.body: We’ve launched the ability to create a FigJam board from Google Meet Series One Board 65 and Desk 27 devices.

news.title: Simpler way to manage team resources
news.body: Managing your team's community resources just got simpler.

news.title: AI-powered mindmaps and timelines in FigJam
news.body: Now you can use the power of AI to generate and expand mindmaps, and create visual timelines in FigJam.

news.title: Update to Library Updates Notification
news.body: Over the next few weeks, we are replacing the bottom right notification button for library updates and replacing with a new library icon for faster entry to library management.

news.title: Use a mouse? It's now easier to navigate in Figma
news.body: Now you have more options for navigating the Figma and FigJam canvases.

news.title: New ways to search for files
news.body: Now you can filter your search results. Constrain your search by using a filter keyword (by:, in:, type:) or selecting a filter from a dropdown at the top of the full results page.

news.title: Meet multi-edit

news.title: Gradient tool improvements
news.body: Creating beautiful gradients in Figma just got easier. Now you can flip and rotate your gradient with new controls, enjoy smarter defaults, and simply hold Shift to snap.

news.title: Sharing & Access Changes in Figma
news.body: We are rolling out changes to sharing and access settings to create a more consistent sharing experience and give you clearer visibility into and control over content permissions.

news.title: Figma design files now load dynamically by page
news.body: To ensure even the largest Figma design files can be used as efficiently as possible, Figma dynamically loads pages.

news.title: Mark frames ready for dev straight from the canvas
news.body: We are starting to roll out an easier way to mark frames ready for dev.

news.title: Improvements to page organization
news.body: Create dividers between pages in Figma to add another layer of organization to your files.

news.title: Select multiple pages for reordering, renaming, and deleting

news.title: Set variable mode for prototypes
news.body: We’ve added a new “set variable mode” interaction for prototypes which allows a user to switch between modes in their collection.

news.title: Improved project transfer

news.title: 10 improvements to Figma Slides
news.body: You asked—we listened. We shipped 10 updates to Figma Slides in 10 days based on your feedback:

news.title: Edit your billing and shipping address
news.body: You can now update the addresses that appear on your invoice directly from admin settings. Use “Invoice details” to update your shipping address and “Payment details” to update your billing address.

news.title: Now presenting: Figma Slides
news.body: Figma’s new presentation tool enables everyone to craft stunning, interactive presentations to engage any audience.

news.title: Allowing text style overrides
news.body: Applying italics, bolding, and underline to text on top of a text style will now override the text style to apply the decoration.

news.title: Billing group admin dashboard
news.body: Starting today, billing group admins on Figma Enterprise accounts can now view and act on upgrade requests from users in billing groups they manage from the dashboard in their admin console.

news.title: We continue to improve variables in Figma
news.body: Typography variables now include scoping, a follow up from Framework

news.title: Create a Figma Slides outline from a FigJam board with AI
news.body: Convert FigJam content, like team brainstorms or user research sessions, into deck outlines in Figma Slides. Start from an entire FigJam board, a specific page, or a select group of stickies.

news.title: Introducing Embed Kit 2.0

news.title: PDF & JPEG export quality selector

news.title: Improved file move enhancements
