news.title: Google Fonts update
news.body: We've added 450 new Google Fonts to Figma.

news.title: Publish a library to a workspace
news.body: Starting today, users in Enterprise organizations with workspaces set up can now publish libraries to a workspace, in addition to a team or the whole org.

news.body: Figma is making it easier for admins to find and manage draft folders of members and guests who have been removed from their organization, now known as "unassigned drafts."

news.body: We're introducing annotations and measurements, rich text formatting for component description, and advanced prototyping in the Plugin API.

news.title: Manage Figma Slides templates styles in Design mode
news.body: You can now manage your Figma Slides template styles in Design mode, not just Slides mode.

news.title: Move your slide frames into Figma Slides
news.body: Creating slide frames in Figma Design? You can now copy them over to Figma Slides with one-click.

news.body: Figma Enterprise customers using SCIM provisioning on Okta can now leverage Okta's Group Push feature to assign users to Workspaces and Billing Groups efficiently at scale.

news.body: We've made some updates to the Billing tab in Admin settings, including a tab structure to make it easier to navigate:

news.body: Find Community resources faster—no more endless scrolling!

news.title: New Export Setting: Detailed or Basic Image Sampling
news.body: "Designers now have the option to select between Basic or Detailed image resampling in advanced export settings.

news.title: Aspect ratio, locked
news.body: You can now lock the aspect ratio of almost any object in Figma – including frames, shapes, images, videos, vectors, and text – so that the proportions of that object are respected as you scale the object or its parent container.

news.title: New additions to Figma AI (beta)
news.body: These features are part of Figma AI's limited beta and are currently rolling out gradually.

news.body: 10 new design system updates for a faster and more controlled workflow.

news.title: Improvements to File Browser
news.body: We updated the file browser to create a more consistent and seamless experience as you use Figma products.

news.title: Updates to Figma Slides
news.body: Last year we launched Figma Slides in open beta, setting the new standard for telling visual stories.

news.title: Smart symbols for all fonts
news.body: Figma now transforms common character combinations into smart symbols in all fonts.

news.body: As we shared in December 2024, Starting on March 11 2025, and rolling out over the course of a few days, we will be making the following changes to our pricing, seats, and billing experience.

news.title: Updates to scrubbing inputs in Figma
news.body: We've made the scrubbable area to the left of input fields larger to make it easier to start scrubbing.

news.body: Figma admins can now approve seat requests directly in Slack, with a new notification center that lets Slack users customize which Figma notifications they receive.

news.title: File View History
news.body: Starting this week, see when teammates and invited guests last visited your Figma files, helping you track engagement and keep projects moving forward.

news.body: At Config, we launched the ability build your own custom generative plugins and shaders by prompting the Figma agent. Now, you can do more with those generative plugins and shaders with animations and interactions, publishing capabilities, and access to the code.

news.title: Hug and fractional units for grid

news.title: Embed your Figma Make prototypes

news.title: See your organization’s AI credits usage history

news.title: Updated left navigation bar in Figma Design

news.body: Through the Figma MCP server, AI agents can now write directly to your Figma files.

news.body: Whether you're refining a complex illustration, iterating on an interactive prototype, or opening that massive product file for the tenth time today, your workflow stays smooth.

news.title: ChatGPT Images 2.0 now available in Figma
news.body: OpenAI's newest image model, ChatGPT Images 2.0, is now available to use with Make Image and Edit Image in Figma Design, Draw, Slides, Buzz, and FigJam. Also available in Figma Weave.

news.title: Introducing Figma Weave workflow templates on the Figma Community
news.body: Meet the newest resource type available on the Figma Community: Figma Weave workflows.

news.body: Make kits give design system teams a way to bring together code with design system guidelines to help Make properly use your design system inside new prototypes.

news.title: Do more with grid
news.body: Grid is generally available and now makes it easier to reorder columns and rows, auto-position items into empty cells, and auto-add or remove rows to fit so you spend less time on manual fixes.

news.body: Figma Slides now has sections, making it easier to organize and navigate your presentation.

news.body: To get started, install the extension and sign in with your Figma account. This feature is currently in beta and available only on paid plans.

news.body: Admins on the Professional plan can now purchase additional AI credits on a pay-as-you-go basis.

news.title: Visually edit your codebase with Make
news.body: Make now lets you visually edit your product and codebase, opening up prototyping workflows on production code or allowing you to ship changes to users. This is a closed beta and we will roll out access over the coming weeks.

news.title: Design closer to CSS with the updated auto layout option
news.body: Auto layout now works more like CSS, so what you design lines up more closely with what actually gets built.

news.title: Bring code-backed screens onto the canvas with variables attached
news.body: Bring coded or legacy screens back into Figma and spend your time refining the work, not rebuilding it.

news.body: To get started, open the model picker in the Figma Make chatbox and choose GPT-5.6. The model is available on all plans.

news.body: Text wrap makes your text responsive with two new options: Balance and Pretty. Set either on a text layer, a text style, or an individual paragraph in text settings.

news.body: We've added more ways to discover, create, and share skills for the Figma agent.

news.title: AI credit user limits and credit requests

news.title: Get organized with nested folders
news.body: As work grows to more people and platforms, files inevitably get harder to find. We've introduced folders, so your team can add structure to files that flexes as project work evolves.

news.body: The new properties panel brings a more direct way to build in Figma Make. Click any element to adjust its properties by hand, or annotate a spot on the screen and let the agent make the change.

news.title: Code on the Figma Canvas

news.title: Agent: Custom Tools, Context & Skills
news.body: The Figma design agent gets more powerful: prompt it to build reusable custom plugins and shader effects, bring in context via attached files, web search, and MCP connectors (GitHub, Slack, Atlassian), and save frequently-used prompts as shareable Skills that codify your team's workflows.

news.title: Introducing Figma Motion
news.body: Figma Motion brings animation to the design canvas with a native timeline — create, preview, and hand off animated components without leaving your file. Includes AI-assisted keyframes, motion variables, and Dev Mode export to CSS, JSON, React, or motion.dev code. Now in open beta.

news.body: A treat before the Config keynote: the Figma design agent beta is now rolled out to 100% of Pro, Org, and Enterprise plans.

news.title: Design Agent Gets Web Search
news.body: The Figma design agent now has web search — prompt the agent or paste a URL, review results with linked citations, and insert content directly into your file.

news.title: Figma MCP Server Updates
news.body: Updates to the Figma MCP server — generate and edit decks in Figma Slides, build data-backed boards in FigJam, and roundtrip from code to canvas in Figma Make. Now with custom font support and image exports.

news.body: Quality-of-life updates to Figma Make for more control — Plan mode, a messaging queue, web search & fetch, and pinned comments.

news.body: Figma introduces pay-as-you-go AI credits and a new Professional plan tier.

news.title: Plan Smarter with More Context in Make
news.body: Figma Make now surfaces more context when planning — helping the agent make better decisions before it starts building.

news.title: Check Designs: Catch What's Off, Ship What's Right
news.body: Check Designs keeps every file synced to your design system — variable and style suggestions, color contrast, library mismatch detection, and detached component detection. Now GA for Full seat, Organization, and Enterprise plans.

news.title: Omni 1.1 Flash in Flow
news.body: Omni 1.1 Flash is in Google Flow with more control over a clip's shape. End frames on desktop direct where a video finishes as well as where it starts, which helps hold characters and narrative steady across a transition. Drafting in 360p costs fewer credits and works from the mobile app, and 720p generations upscale to 1080p or 4K for final clips.

news.title: MusicFX Winding Down for Flow Music
news.body: Google Labs is retiring MusicFX and MusicFX DJ on July 31, 2026 to focus on Google Flow Music — its tool for creating, sharing, and remixing original music. Everything learned from the MusicFX experiments carries into Flow Music as a long-term home for musical projects.

news.title: Create Bespoke Tools with Natural Language
news.body: With Google Flow Tools, you can now use natural language to create bespoke tools and workflows. Explore and try the Tools within Flow, remix one to fit your workflow, create your own from scratch with a prompt, or share with a friend. Image editors, video resizers, custom shaders — no coding experience required.

news.title: Gemini Omni Available for Everyone
news.body: Gemini Omni is now available for everyone to try in Google Flow. Earlier this week Flow introduced Gemini Omni, the new model that lets you edit videos using natural language — like Nano Banana, but for video.

news.title: Your Agent + Gemini Omni Land in Flow
news.body:
Introducing your agent and the all-new Gemini Omni model in Google Flow.

Think of your agent as a creative partner — it reasons through complex tasks and helps you brainstorm, create, and edit, all while under your direction.

Gemini Omni is where Gemini's intelligence meets our generative media models. Think of it as Nano Banana but for video. A major leap forward in world understanding, multimodality, and editing.

news.title: Gemini Omni for Creatives, Unlocked in Flow
news.body: The full potential of Gemini Omni for creatives, unlocked in Google Flow. Combine real-world inspiration with generated content and iterate with ease — through natural conversation. Available now for all Google AI subscribers.

news.title: Introducing Tools in Google Flow
news.body:
Image editors, video resizers, custom shaders… if you can think of it, you can now build it. Introducing Tools in Google Flow.

news.title: Midjourney’s First Acquisition
news.body: As a kid, all I wanted was a cool-place to work on cool-projects with cool-people. Projects to help people and push the world towards beauty, awe, and splendor. As an adult I find myself in the unusual position of having everything I wanted and two questions come to mind next: How can I use this opportunity to make baby David proud? And what the heck did Baby David know anyway? The answer will look like the slow blossoming of a very unusual research lab. The beginning of which you’re starting to see with Midjourney Medical. The maturation will look like the announcement of half a dozen similarly ambitious projects over the next 6 months. Frankly, it’s exciting, and scary, and the only thing I know for sure is I’m gonna need help. So this is why we’re announcing our first acquisition today which is: Co–Star. Click "Vary" on images you'd like to render at full-quality and full-resolution Draft jobs use half as many fast hours as V8.1 SD jobs (even though they generate 24 images!) Turn on draft mode by clicking the ⚡ button in the menubar Use --preview to test new features We're trying something new today to let you test early versions of new models. Use --preview in your prompt to test the latest. Images that you create with --preview might be a little unpolished and the jobs are not guaranteed to run consistently over time. In this first test, you'll notice differences across all images, especially those with personalization and moodboards. We'd love to hear what you think in #ideas-and-features

news.title: V8.1 is now the default model on Midjourney!
news.body: Hi everyone, After your testing and feedback, we've updated the default model from V7 to V8.1! A reminder of what's new in V8.1: The model is smarter, more coherent, better adheres to detailed prompts, and renders text better than ever With HD mode enabled, V8.1 renders at twice the size and 4x the resolution of V7 images V8.1 is incredibly fast. Your images appear in only 4 seconds in SD, and 12 seconds in HD Style references, personalization, and aesthetics remain consistent between V7 and V8.1 Note: V7 omni-reference is available to use while we finish training the improved version for V8 Now that V8.1 is the default, we will be deprecating our V8.0 alpha model in two weeks

news.title: Web Updates
news.body: Conversational mode has been improved across text and voice input: When a voice session starts, it has access to your Image Prompts, Style References, sidebar settings, and recent jobs. Image Prompts now work from the tray and sidebar. Tray images persist across voice submissions until you remove them. You can add references without exiting voice. A new Rerun as HD button makes it easy to rerun any V8.1 image generated in Standard Definition (SD) as High Definition (HD). Folder views on the Create and Organize pages now show a hidden-item count so you can see how much is filtered out. The filter reset button has moved from the bottom to the top of the filter bar. On mobile web, the settings menu now groups Profiles, Moodboards, and Liked Styles together. The More Options panel is available in the mobile lightbox. Improvements and bug fixes: Search on the Create and Organize pages now works for signed-in members without an active subscription. Upload error message now shows the correct 20 MB limit. Failed jobs no longer show Vary or Upscale buttons that can't run. Rate-limit message now appears when an upload is throttled. Prompt scrolling on the Create page no longer traps the scro

news.title: V8.1 Updates
news.body: Hi everyone, we have a few V8.1 related updates today: V8.1 is now available on Discord as well as midjourney.com We've improved sharpness and image quality for V8.1! This is most noticeable for SREFs and Moodboards but you should notice across all images (especially HD) To save compute during a server transition, we're making SD default for a bit. You can still switch to HD under settings panel or add --hd after your prompt. The rating data you've giving us is continuing to help us improve quality for V8.2. If you want to keep helping us do ranking we've updated the images here: midjourney.com/rank-v8-1 Thank you and have fun! ❤️ Examples of the image quality improvements in crops taken from HD images

news.title: High-res rating
news.body: Hi everyone! We're preparing some major aesthetic updates for v8.1/8.2 and we want your help doing some image ranking to improve the model Basically, we never did any ranking parties at full 2K resolution and in order to get the best possible HD pixels for everyone it would really help for us to rank some 'raw' images at the resolution from scratch This will help tune the model to be more 'natively' HD/2K 'beautiful' and we think you'll all appreciate the difference soon Rank images here. Tell us which one you think is more 'beautiful'. midjourney.com/rank-v8-1 Pro-tip: You can press the 1 key for the left image and 2 for the right image and 3 to skip. Thanks again! ❤️

news.title: V8.1 Alpha
news.body: Thanks for testing our V8.0 model over the last month! Today we're releasing our next version of V8 - V8.1 What’s new in V8.1? V8.1 has a consistent and familiar aesthetic in the spirit of V7. Moodboards and srefs are now super stable and will be everything you love. HD mode is now 3x faster and 3x cheaper. It’s so cheap we’re making it default for V8.1 Standard resolution is now 50% faster and 25% cheaper. Standard resolution in V8.1 at full quality is as fast as V7 draft mode! It’s great for exploring and iterating *fast*. We’ve also added a button called “Run as HD” which will rerun any SD job as HD. We’ve also brought back some community favorite features Image prompts and even image weights are now available in V8.1 New Prompt Shortener, which will kick in anytime you go over the prompt length limits Updated Describe that gives longer more detailed prompts and matches the prompting style of V8 Please Note: Our V8 series of models are still only available on alpha.midjourney.com and are in an early testing phase. Things will change! Perhaps without notice! But good stuff is on the way. It is likely that we will decommission our V8.0 model after V8.1 has been out for a few weeks

news.title: Relax mode for V8 Alpha
news.body: Hey everyone! We have some quick V8 Alpha related updates to make today Relax mode is now available! V8 Relax is now up for all Standard/Pro/Mega subscribers Supports all commands (except using --hd and --q 4 at the same time) There is a chance we run out of servers. If we do, we may change availability or speed of relax mode (until we get more servers online hopefully mid-late next week) Two Versions of SREF / Moodboards now available We have a new version of SREF/Moodboards that is less accurate but is 4x faster/cheaper and also supports --hd and works better with --p and --stylize and --exp This version is now 'default' You can use the old version by putting --sv 6 (style version 6) after your prompt Our guides/mods are split between which is 'better' but certainly in my (David's) opinion, this new version is more 'fun' - so please enjoy! Update on V8 Development We REALLY appreciate everyone's feedback so far! We are now working on a big training run for a new version of V8 (it might even be called V8.1) This new version will (probably) take 1-3 weeks to be ready When the next V8 comes out, we will likely remove the 'present' version of V8. So remember everything you're using n

news.title: V8 Alpha
news.body: Hi everyone! Today we’re letting the community test an early version of our V8 model on alpha.midjourney.com. We want your feedback and your help. Let’s explore what this new model can do. V8 is an incredible model. It’s much better at following detailed directions and will still surprise you when you ask. Its ability to understand your aesthetics through personalization, style references (srefs) and moodboards is amazing. Images are more coherent and detailed. Text rendering works better than ever (when specified in “quotes”). And image generation is ~5x faster than before. We’ve upgraded our web interfaces to support this speed. And more is coming. We have an improved conversation mode so you can just ‘talk’ in flow, a “Grid Mode” so you can focus on a single big set of images, and we’ve moved our settings into ‘sidebars’ so you can tweak settings without blocking your view. V8 launches with support for multiple aspect ratios, --chaos, --weird, --exp, --raw. We support backwards compatibility with your V7 personalization profiles, moodboards, and srefs. V8 brings a new --hd mode which natively renders images at 2K resolution and a --q 4 mode if you need a little bit of extra cohe

news.title: 🎛️ Performance Improvements and Auto Model
news.body: We made several memory and performance improvements. Raycast's host process now uses about 50% less memory. Each extension process uses about 30% less memory at startup and less CPU when launching, which helps menu bar commands, background refreshes, and AI tools. We also fixed a memory leak that grew the longer Raycast stayed open. More details are below, and further improvements are coming in the next updates. 🤖 Auto Model We reworked our Auto model, and you can now choose how it picks a model for you. It comes with three different preferences: Lightweight, Balanced, and Flagship. Balanced is the default and uses about 70% fewer credits than Flagship to help you get more out of your credits. Lightweight responds in about 70% less time than Flagship and works well for quick questions. Flagship uses the most capable models for harder tasks and requires a Pro+ or Max subscription. ✨ New AI: Added Claude and ChatGPT subscription usage in /usage in AI Chat and in Settings AI: Added Show AI Credits/Claude/ChatGPT Usage commands Clipboard History: Added a Paste as PNG action for TIFF images Root Search: Added direct search results for more settings, including Accessibility settings and

news.title: 🔌 External Model Providers
news.body: Extensions can now provide their own AI models to Raycast. Just install a compatible extension from the Store, complete its setup, and choose its models in AI Chat. It’s an easy way to bring even more models into your everyday workflow. We updated a few extensions: Ollama AI, AI by Vercel, Cerebras, Groq, LM Studio, etc.. Developers, check out the API changelog for more information. 💎 Improvements AI Chat: Rename a chat by double-clicking its title in the top bar. Press Enter to save or Esc to cancel, and the window can still be dragged by the title AI Chat: Dictation with Ctrl + M in the AI Chat and Quick AI composers now uses the same processed transcript as the Dictate command. The text shows up once you stop recording instead of streaming into the editor while you speak Applications: Added support for finding apps by alternate names and Spotlight keywords, such as “Codex” for ChatGPT and “Preferences” for System Settings Diagnostics: Added a warning in Settings → About when another app’s Secure Input may interfere with Snippet Expansion or Hyper Key, with guidance on resolving it Script Commands: Added line wrapping to full output so long lines are easier to read 🐞 Fixes AI:

news.title: ✨ New In Raycast AI
news.body: We rebuilt the core of Raycast AI. You can now give AI Chat a task and it works out a plan, uses your extensions, writes and runs code, checks the results, and keeps going until it's finished. When something fails, it tries a different approach. And when it needs a decision from you, it stops, asks you, and then continues where it left off. Tasks like these cost more to run than a single question, which is why this release also changes how we charge for AI. Our plans move from rate-limited to usage-based, all subscription prices stay the same, and there's a new Max plan for heavier usage. Read the full reasoning on our blog. But there is more… 🔁 Bring Your Own Subscriptions You can now connect your Claude or ChatGPT account to any paid Raycast plan and use those models in AI Chat, Quick AI, and AI Commands. This lets you run the heaviest tasks without worrying about additional costs. We plan to add other providers in the future, turning AI Chat into your single interface to get the most out of your subscriptions. You can enable models from your subscriptions in Settings → AI → Models & Providers. 📁 Projects Projects keep conversations about the same topic together. They have thei

news.title: 🦙 Bring Your Own Model
news.body: Bring Your Own Model brings three familiar ways to use your preferred AI models back to Raycast v2. Connect any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with Custom Providers, run models through Ollama with Local Models, or add your OpenRouter API key to choose from its catalog. Once configured, your models are available across Raycast AI alongside Raycast’s built-in options. In v2, Custom Providers, Local Models, and Bring Your Own Key require a Raycast Pro subscription. We know this is a meaningful change compared to v1 and want to be upfront about it. You can read more about our thinking and where we’re heading on the BYOAI article in the Manual. ✨ New AI: Added support OpenAI-compatible custom providers, local models via Ollama, and OpenRouter API keys, using their models across Raycast AI Quick AI: Added a Paste Formatted Response action Window Management: Added Resize Window and Move Window commands that take exact pixel dimensions and coordinates as arguments Window Management: Added Create Layout From Current Windows command allowing for quick capturing custom layouts from the windows currently on screen. The layout editor can also add any visible window, and a layout can place several w

news.title: 🎉Raycast 2.0 is out of Beta!
news.body: Raycast 2.0 is out of Beta! 🎉 Thank you so much for being a part of it! We would not be at this point without all of your feedback and support. With this release, Raycast v2 replaces v1. You will be guided through the update in Raycast, and your existing v2 beta data will remain unchanged. If you have not imported your v1 data yet, you will have the option to do so during the update. Some permissions may need to be authorized again after the migration. During the beta, Dictation and AI Chat were available for free while we tested and improved the experience. With this release, these features will now be part of Raycast Pro. To help with the transition, signing in gives you a 7-day free trial of Pro. No credit card is required. For more information on the update process, see our FAQ. ✨ New AI: Added a Clear Chat action, which resets a chat's messages while keeping its model, agent, and other configuration AI: Added support for mentioning AI extensions when replying to a question asked with the Ask User Question tool AI: Ask User Question tool can be collapsed to make browsing conversation easier while questions are unanswered MCP: Added loopback OAuth redirects so MCP providers tha

news.title: 💻 Screen Awareness
news.body: The best chats start with the right context. Screen Awareness brings context from your focused app or window into AI Chat or Quick AI, so you don’t have to copy text, attach screenshots, or explain what you’re looking at. Use the Send Focused Window to AI command, choose Screen Awareness from the @ menu, or simply ask “summarise this” or “reply to this”. The first time you use the command, a short onboarding guide helps you set a hotkey. Our team likes to double-tap the right Command key. ✨ New AI: Send Focused Window to AI command includes richer app and window context AI: New Ask Screen Awareness AI Extension to quickly give context to Raycast AI: Added compaction and context management support Quick AI: “Send Message” AI setting is now respected by Quick AI as well which allows submitting queries on Command Return Dictation: Added a way to import your vocabulary and hotkeys from other apps Dictation: Added a new “Add Word to Vocabulary” command to add a selected word or entered argument into your vocabulary Feedback: New Ask Feedback AI Extension to contact the Raycast team Hotkeys: Added support for chords using a modifier held on both sides of the keyboard (e.g. left ⌘ + right

news.title: Workflow Support in Runway MCP
news.body: All Plans Agents can now list workflows in your workspace, open one in the web app editor, tweak it, and run it from chat. Built for advanced, re-runnable pipelines you don't want to put together by hand.

news.title: Runway Ruby
news.body: Pro+ Plans Transform any SDR video into true HDR with Runway Ruby, a native color grading model available in Tool Mode, Workflows, and Runway Dev. Convert outputs from any model, first or third party, or your own existing video files, and get updated brightness and color range for professional-grade HDR results.

news.title: Seedream 5.0 Pro Layers
news.body: Paid Plans Split images into layers with a new tool that lets you toggle and transform each layer independently. Ideal for fine-grained image editing and asset extraction.

news.title: Compositing Nodes
news.body: All Plans Compose and blend images and video together with new compositing workflow nodes, now available to all customers.

news.title: SD2.5 1080p
news.body: Paid Plans Seedance 2.5 now generates in 1080p across all surfaces. Get sharper, higher-resolution results wherever you create.

news.title: Introducing Solaris
news.body: Runway introduced Solaris, the first of its Interface World Models. Instead of code sitting between a design and a running app, one model generates every frame of the interface, and every response to your input, live as you use it: click a button and the model paints what happens next. Runway reports Solaris was preferred 61% of the time on instruction following and 71% on natural behavior against coded interfaces, by its own evaluation. It is not a public product yet: Runway is launching with key partners and taking early-access requests, and says legible text, coherence over long sessions, and screen-reader support are still open problems.

news.title: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash on Runway
news.body: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash is on Runway, alongside the other image and video models it hosts.

news.title: Seedance 2.5 on Runway

news.title: MiniMax H3 on Runway
news.body: MiniMax H3 is now available on Runway. Access it alongside every other frontier model on one platform.

news.title: Workflows in Runway Agent

news.title: Introducing Runway Media Router
news.body: Runway introduced Media Router, the first preference-optimized router for generative media. Instead of hand-picking a model for every request, you define what 'best' means once, cost, quality, or latency, and the router selects the right video, image, or audio model for you.

news.title: Runway Opens Paris Office
news.body: Runway announced the opening of its first office in France — a new research hub in Paris anchored by an initial team of ten. Runway called France one of the world's strongest AI ecosystems and is hiring in Paris and across Europe.

news.title: HyperFrames v0.8.137
news.body: Compositions with large inline images or scripts use far less memory while they load for preview. Whisper transcription detects the spoken language and can report progress. Fixes Studio: Audio clips that reach the export ceiling now say “Too loud”, with the exact peak on hover or keyboard focus (4905b4dbc, #5099). Catalog previews now load under the docs site's script policy, with safer script encoding. Fixes Studio: Keyframed animations keep their ease through every Studio edit (0d5e395cd3, #5051). Studio: Undo takes back the last edit, even right after a resize or a nudge (98fe011699, #5048). Studio: Layers rows show a kind icon, and only a group row has a caret (f7d6734761, #5067). news.title: HyperFrames v0.8.46
news.body: Engine motion blur picks its own sample count per frame now, instead of one fixed count for a whole render. Features Engine: The sub-frame motion blur added in v0.8.45 used a fixed sample count for every frame of a render (16 by default). That undersamples fast or hard-edged motion and oversamples content that barely moves. The engine now measures how much a frame actually moved before choosing how many samples it gets, between 16 and 64, so quality goes up where it was undersampled instead of being spent evenly on every frame. Frames that need the extra accuracy cost more to render; a frame whose only change is a fade or a colour shift skips the measurement step and stays at the old cost. Nothing changes if samplesPerFrame is set explicitly (2ab7b8686, #4031). View the full commit range.

news.title: HyperFrames v0.8.45
news.body: Motion blur arrives twice in this release, as two separate mechanisms for two different jobs. The catalog component reproduces the After Effects look, while the render engine computes the real shutter integral. Features Producer: motionBlur on a render configuration turns on sub-frame multi-sample blur. An empty object takes the defaults: 16 samples per frame, a 180 degree shutter angle and a shutter phase of -90. samplesPerFrame accepts up to 64. Setting it forces PNG frame capture, because the samples are averaged pixel by pixel and JPEG samples would be averaged after a lossy step. Whether a render captures lossless frames now has one owner instead of being decided in three places from a different fact (b64a7a3a6, #4020). Engine: Each output frame can be the average of several captures taken across the shutter window. Because each sample re-renders the page, this integrates whatever the composition actually does inside the window: rotation, scale, opacity, filters and child animation, not translation alone. It is off unless asked for, and a static frame still costs one capture (0a1c6f5a4, #4019). Producer and CLI: A render can output an HLS VOD package. It is the same H.264 and

news.title: HyperFrames v0.8.44
news.body: The root_dimensions_mismatch false positive from v0.8.43 is fixed, so lint and check --strict stop flagging sub-compositions. The streaming encoder gains an opt-in locked keyframe interval, which no existing render turns on. Features Engine: The streaming encoder accepts lockGopForChunkConcat and gopSize, which force a keyframe at a fixed interval so encoded output can be cut and joined without re-encoding. It already existed on the disk encoder and now emits identical arguments on both paths. The flag defaults to off and an existing render produces the same FFmpeg arguments as before (b4f1929cf, #3973). Fixes Lint: root_dimensions_mismatch no longer fires for sub-compositions. A sub-composition's own and html, body CSS never reach the live rendering document, because the runtime mounts only its matched subtree, so the warning was drift that could not clip anything. v0.8.43 shipped the warning with this known false positive and this is the promised follow-up. A top-level mismatch is still reported, and a viewport-meta-only mismatch now says so in its own words rather than warning about clipping (2229d0d6a, #4012). View the full commit range.

news.title: Cygwin build inputs and matching source for Windows voice
news.body: CI-only build tools for native Windows voice releases. These archives are not included in Codex user packages. cygwin-build-inputs.tar.gz: 103 pinned Cygwin binary packages and the signed package index used by the offline build installer. cygwin-build-sources.tar: all 83 corresponding source package archives at the exact versions named by that index. news.body: Updated the left-hand navigation of the Plaid Dashboard for improved ease of use. Added connection_availability field to the Institution object. It is NOT_SUPPORTED when Plaid does not support new connections to the institution (which can only occur on /institutions/get\_by\_id responses), and SUPPORTED otherwise. Added optional roll_dates_forward field to the custom Sandbox user configuration object. When set to true, when the Item is created, the most recent transaction activity date will always be the current date and other transaction activity will be rolled forward to match. For Link: Released iOS SDK v7.1.2 , fixing a bug where onLoad was not called for Identity Verification sessions. Released iOS SDK v7.2.0 , fixing security issues, adding automatic session handoff for Embedded Link and delivering the Embedded Link start-failure onExit callback on the main thread. With this release, Safari Web Inspector can no longer attach to production Link sessions on iOS; WebView inspection is now limited to Sandbox. Released iOS SDK v6.5.2 , adding security improvements. Released Android SDK v6.2.2 . This fixes a static-initialization crash in LinkAccountVerificationStatus and other pub

news.title: Enhanced Sandbox capabilities with the launch of Sandbox Studio in the Dashboard
news.body: Enhanced Sandbox capabilities with the launch of Sandbox Studio in the Dashboard. Customers can now make Sandbox API calls directly via the Dashboard, create custom Sandbox profiles based on a text description, and save institutions to Sandbox profiles for testing Layer and the Returning User Experience. Improved user experience for accessing Fidelity Investments. New customers on Custom and Growth plans will get Fidelity access within 4 weeks (reduced from 8 weeks), and customers on Pay-as-you-go plans can request access via the Dashboard OAuth institutions page rather than having to file a support ticket. Improved user experience for accessing Charles Schwab. New customers will get Schwab access within 5 business days (reduced from 6 weeks), and customers on Pay-as-you-go plans do not need to explicitly request access. Removed unused account subtypes installment (loan) and charge card (credit). These subtypes were never returned by the Plaid API. Announced that effective October 11, 2026, the the home equity and commercial account subtypes will be sub-divided to more accurately reflect the accounts they describe. home equity will now correspond to HELOCs only; home equity loans w

news.title: Added a Billing page to the Dashboard for customers on negotiated rates
news.body: Added a Billing page to the Dashboard for customers on negotiated rates, providing visibility into invoice and payment history. For Link: Released React Native SDK v13.0.5 , adding an explicit Identity Verification session API that creates and returns the native Link session without waiting for the onLoad callback. The behavior of the existing createPlaidLinkSession is unchanged. Bundles Android SDK v6.1.0 and iOS SDK v7.1.0. Released React Native SDK v13.1.0 . New features include improved migration diagnostics and troubleshooting for the usage of removed methods; adding a named sdkVersion export and deprecating the raw native-module default export; and included guidance for AI coding agents. For Auth and Transfer: Announced upcoming Chase consent and Tokenized Account Number (TAN) expiration. Chase has begun rolling out a new OAuth consent experience in which the end user must choose a consent duration of 6 months, 1 year, or "always". When consent expires, the Item will break and any TAN associated with the account will expire along with it, causing payments made using that TAN to fail. The consent prompt appears on new Items only, and existing Chase Items default to "always", b

news.title: Improved behavior of Identity endpoints when called on non-depository Capital One accounts where identity…
news.body: Improved behavior of Identity endpoints when called on non-depository Capital One accounts where identity data is not available. The failure to fetch identity data in this scenario will no longer cause the Item to enter an error state. Improved accuracy of Item consent expiration data at institutions that enforce expiration dates. Some Items may show a revised consent expiration date as a result of these changes. Items will also now reliably enter an error state when they expire, regardless of whether Plaid is attempting to fetch new data from the institution or not. Redesigned the UI of the Settings page in the Dashboard to display a full-page view with a link to each setting, rather than the navigation being entirely within the left nav bar. For Link: Released Android SDK v. 6.2.1 , including a bug fixes for OAuth flows when linking multiple institutions. For Auth: Pushed out the date on which limited-purpose checking accounts for existing institutions will be omitted from Link by default. Originally, this change was scheduled to take effect August 7th, 2026. It has been extended to October 6, 2026. To opt in to allowing limited purpose checking accounts, see Enabling limited pur

news.title: Added support for returning Annual Percentage Yield (APY) data on accounts via the new apy field
news.body: Added support for returning Annual Percentage Yield (APY) data on accounts via the new apy field. Added /sandbox/user/fire\_webhook for firing test webhooks associated with a user (primarily Income and Plaid Check Consumer Report webhooks) rather than an Item. Added /user/items/associate for associating Items with a user id (Early Availability only). For Link: Released iOS SDK v7.0.5 , preventing SwiftUI Link sheet interactive dismissal so Link cannot be dismissed without triggering onExit, and deprecating PlaidLinkView and PlaidLinkUIViewControllerRepresentable in favor of PlaidLinkSheet or session.sheet(). Released Android SDK v6.2.0 , fixing a bug in which document uploads during the Link flow would sometimes fail, reducing minimum supported Android SDK version from 26 to 25, narrowing ProGuard rules to improve stack trace readability in minified apps, and removing the unused okhttp3 logging-interceptor dependency. news.title: 250+ AI-Native Video Tools in Tesseract

news.title: Introducing Tesseract for AI Video Editing
news.body: Mirage launched Tesseract, a video creative suite that gives AI agents direct access to tools for editing footage, motion, and sound. Agents can make precise revisions and render results from prompts. Mirage demonstrated it with GPT-6 Astra and Sol and offers a ChatGPT plugin.

media.alt: Mirage launch video made with Tesseract

news.title: Introducing Mirage Avatar X
news.body: Mirage Avatar X is the new standard for AI avatar models — industry-leading identity preservation, the most expressive AI avatars available, and support for both vertical and horizontal video. It looks like you, moves like you, and sounds like you. Create your AI twin from just 10 seconds of video, with no quality degradation across long-form, continuous generations.

news.title: AI Edit Library — 100+ Styles

news.title: AI Edit — Real Footage In, Edited Video Out
news.body: You're probably hearing a lot about generating videos with AI. Mirage built AI Edit to solve something different: post-production. For creators and business owners, the hardest part usually isn't filming — it's finishing. AI Edit closes that gap.

news.title: Meet Cappy — The First AI Video Editor You Can Text
news.body: Just text Cappy like a friend — if your friend happened to be a really good editor. No apps to download, no learning curve. Send an idea, some clips, or just say hi, then chat until it's exactly right. Free to try, on iPhone and Android.

news.title: Introducing Property Videos
news.body: Turn any listing into a beautifully-staged, professionally edited video with one click. No videographer. No staging. No editing. Available now on Captions web.

news.title: Auto-Fill Previous Stream Details
news.body: Creating another stream? You can now quickly fill in the title and description from your most recent stream. Click Fill Previous, make any updates, and go live faster. Available on all plans.

news.title: Vimeo Chat in StreamYard
news.body: Vimeo chat is now available in StreamYard. Vimeo comments now appear directly in your StreamYard chat, so you can respond and engage without switching tabs. Available on all StreamYard plans.

Available on paid plans.

news.body: New release adds WebGPU compute-powered effects — Fog, Smoke, and SmokeFill (which fills your logo with atmospheric smoke). Try it live in the collection.

news.body: CMYK Halftone just dropped. VHS too.

The way you build shaders just changed. Your agent now finds, tweaks, and ships the perfect shader preset — or designs one from scratch. Available for Pro users.

news.title: Freehand Brush Tools Are Live for Everyone
news.body: Rive's freehand drawing tools are out for everyone in Rive Editor 0.8.5879: Brush, Pencil, Eraser, Bucket, and Shape Bend. Brush paints filled shapes with a choice of tips such as Round, Tall Ellipse, Wide Bar, and Diagonal, plus size and other settings, so you can sketch and paint directly on the artboard and keep everything as editable vector shapes.

news.title: Introducing the Rive CLI and RML
news.body: Rive introduced a command-line tool and text format for building Rive files with an AI agent. The launch video was built by agents working with a person in the Rive CLI.

news.title: Rive CLI 1.0.3
news.body: Rive CLI 1.0.3 makes keyboard-driven workflows easier. Use readable key names in RML, press keys from the terminal with --key, move through focusable items with Tab and Shift+Tab, and get clearer errors and JSON output for agent-friendly workflows. The release also adds personal-file support for rive push, inspect --summary, safer project creation, and more useful RML validation.

news.title: Rive Editor 0.8.5376: Clip to Scripted Path Effects
news.body: Rive Editor 0.8.5376 is out. You can now clip to scripted path effects in Rive, extending what scripted paths can do inside your animations. Full release notes are on the Rive community.

news.title: Rive Editor 0.8.5321
news.body: Rive Editor 0.8.5321 introduces Global View Models — view models can now live at the file level instead of belonging to a single artboard. Create one from the Data panel's + menu under View Model → Global, and bind its properties from any artboard or component in the file.

news.title: Rive Editor 0.8.5275
news.body: Rive Editor 0.8.5275 is out, the latest release of the Rive editor, via the Rive community announcements.

news.title: Rive Editor 0.8.5134

news.title: Rive Editor 0.8.5113

news.title: Quiver Illustrations in the Rive Agent
news.body: The Rive Agent now supports Quiver AI illustrations on Voyager plans.

news.title: Rive Editor 0.8.5094 + Runtime Updates
news.body: Rive Editor 0.8.5094 ships with runtime updates — the latest editor improvements and fixes.

news.title: GPU Canvas — Early Access
news.body: Rive's new low-level GPU layer for 3D, shaders, and custom effects is now in Early Access.

news.title: Listener Action Scripts Tutorial
news.body: Rive's listener action scripts let you run custom logic when a listener fires in a state machine. One practical use case: distinguishing a double click from a single click, which is tricky to do with standard listeners alone.

news.title: Rive Editor 0.8.4858
news.body: Apply timeline values to design mode (Early Access), improved drag/drop from Assets panel to Stage, Stateful Components UI tweaks, and various fixes.

news.title: Fire Actions on States or Transitions
news.body: You can now fire Actions on a State or Transition in Rive. Use them to update View Model data that your runtime code reacts to.

news.title: Build Reusable Rive Components You Can Drive From Code
news.body: How to build reusable Rive components you can drive from code — web, mobile, and game engines.

news.title: Stateful Components Tutorial
news.body: A new way to reuse components in Rive without wiring up a separate view model instance for each one. Override properties directly in the inspector for faster iteration — significantly reduces complexity and enables quick design iteration.

news.title: Rive Editor 0.8.4840

news.title: Stagger Keys QOL + Shift+X to Swap Fill/Stroke
news.body: Rive shipped a Stagger Keys QOL update — collapsed keys are treated as a unit, expanded keys stagger individually. Plus Shift+X to swap Fill/Stroke.

news.title: Free Rive AI Agent
news.body: Starting today, the Rive Agent is available to everyone, including Free users. AI should make it easier for anyone to learn and build in Rive, regardless of plan.

news.title: Rive Editor 0.8

news.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 launch
news.body: We just launched Claude Sonnet 5.5, the second model in our Claude 5.5 family. Sonnet 5.5 is a faster, lower-cost complement to Claude Opus 5.5. For more information, see our blog post: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.5.

news.title: Build plugins for Claude
news.body: You can now submit plugins to the Claude directory through a new developer portal, track them through review, and see usage analytics once they’re live. For more information, see our blog post: Build plugins for Claude.

media.caption: Stylized view of review status and recommended changes for a plugin. Data is illustrative.

news.title: Claude Cowork comes to every conversation
news.body: We're rolling out a new Claude experience that makes everything Claude Cowork does available from any conversation. Ask a quick question or hand Claude a bigger task, like a report, spreadsheet, or presentation, without choosing a mode first. Your chats, Cowork tasks, projects, connectors, and skills carry over. The new experience is rolling out gradually to Pro and Max plans on web, desktop, and mobile. Learn more in Claude Cowork and chat are one Claude.

news.title: Create designs, decks, and docs in any conversation
news.body: You can now ask for a design, deck, or document in any conversation with Claude, including in Claude Code and the Artifacts tab, and edit it with Claude or directly as you work. Claude Design works inside your conversations with all of its features, including on-canvas editing and importing your design system. Claude Slides gives presentations their own starting point, and Claude Docs is a new way to write living documents with Claude and your team. Artifacts, including Claude Design, Claude Slides, and Claude Docs, are available on every plan, including Free. On Enterprise plans, Claude Design, Claude Slides, and Claude Docs are in beta and off by default until an owner turns them on. Learn more in What are artifacts and how do I use them? and Get started with Claude Docs.

news.title: Claude Opus 5.5 launch
news.body: We just launched Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in our new Claude 5.5 family. It performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5. For more information, see our blog post: Introducing Claude Opus 5.5.

news.title: Claude Marketplace Launches
news.body: Claude Marketplace brings together connectors and plugins, Claude-powered agents and products, and service partners. Browse integrations such as Slack and Notion, products from partners including Cursor and CrowdStrike, and implementation services from firms such as Accenture and Deloitte. Builders can also apply to list their tools, agents, or services.

news.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5.5
news.body: Anthropic introduced Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in the Claude 5.5 family. It targets agentic coding and knowledge work, with performance near Claude Fable 5.1 on most tasks. Anthropic says typical workloads cost 40% less than Opus 5 and output is generated over 30% faster. The model is available in Claude and through the Claude API.

news.title: Claude Cowork and Chat Merge Into One Claude
news.body: Claude Cowork and chat are merging into one Claude. Ask a quick question or hand over a report, and Claude takes it from there, even after you close your laptop. If something is unclear, Claude asks and you keep the final say. You can also now make decks, docs, and designs in your conversation: draft a one-pager in Claude Docs, turn it into a deck with Claude Slides, and mock up a matching visual in Claude Design, all from one place. Fix a line in the doc yourself, leave a comment for Claude on a slide, or select an element and move it. When it is ready, present the deck straight from Claude, export the doc in the format you already use, or share everything at one link. Rolling out to Pro and Max over the next few weeks.

news.title: Launching Salesforce in Claude (beta)
news.body: We've launched Salesforce in Claude, a plugin that brings a seller’s accounts, opportunities, and pipeline into Claude with 37 pre-built sales skills. Prep a call, review a deal, create a pipeline dashboard, and send your forecast all from Claude. It’s now available in beta on all paid plans for organizations Salesforce approves through its beta sign-up. For more information, see our blog post: Bringing Salesforce into Claude.

news.title: Claude Marketplace Adds Enterprise Listings
news.body: Claude Marketplace now includes CrowdStrike, Cursor, Factory, Gamma, and Vercel. Enterprises can use their Anthropic spend commitment to buy more Claude-powered products and agents.

news.title: Smart reports (beta)
news.body: We’ve launched smart reports, which analyze how a team uses Claude and report on the work getting done, what it costs, where sessions run into friction, and which repeated patterns are worth packaging as shared skills. Smart reports are available in beta on Claude Enterprise plans. Learn more in Get started with smart reports.

news.title: Write tools for the Microsoft 365 connector
news.body: The Microsoft 365 connector now goes beyond search. With write tools enabled, Claude can draft, send, and organize email, manage calendar events, update mailbox settings, and create and update files in OneDrive and SharePoint. Read and search tools work as before, and Teams remains read-only. Before members can use write tools, a Microsoft Entra administrator needs to consent to the updated permission set and an admin needs to enable them for the organization. For more information, see Set up the Microsoft 365 connector and Connect to Microsoft 365.

news.title: Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 launch
news.body: We just launched Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, the world’s most advanced models for coding and knowledge work. For more information, see our blog post: Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1.

news.title: Memory in Claude Cowork, editable topics, and a sensitive topics setting
news.body: Memory now works across chat and Cowork in the cloud. Everything Claude remembers is listed under Topics in Settings > Memory, where you can edit or delete any item. Topics such as health or beliefs stay out of memory unless you turn on Include sensitive topics in memory. Memory is on by default for Free, Pro, and Max plans and off by default for Team and Enterprise organizations. See Use Claude's chat search and memory to build on previous context.

news.title: Skill and plugin security scanning (beta)
news.body: Enterprise plans can now turn on skill and plugin security scanning to automatically check third-party skills and plugins for malicious content when someone uploads or edits them. For more information, see Get started with skill and plugin scanning.

news.title: Claude Opus 5 launch
news.body: We launched Claude Opus 5, a thoughtful and proactive model that comes close to the frontier intelligence of Claude Fable 5 at half the price. For more information, see our blog post: Claude Opus 5.

news.title: HIPAA configuration for your Claude organizations is now self-serve
news.body: You can now manage HIPAA readiness for your Claude organizations yourself. This applies to both Claude Enterprise and the Claude Platform (API). In each product, an eligible admin can review the Business Associate Agreement (BAA), download the implementation guide, and enable the HIPAA configuration in a single flow. For more information, refer to HIPAA-ready Enterprise plans and HIPAA readiness for Claude API.

news.title: Updated memory for Claude
news.body: Memory on Claude now works as a set of individual, categorized entries that Claude reads and updates during your conversations, replacing the previous daily memory summary. See Use Claude’s chat search and memory to build on previous context.

news.title: A new way to reflect with Claude
news.body: Your monthly recap is a new feature at Settings > Reflect that shows you the topics you spent time on, your most active day and peak hour, and observations about how you work with Claude. It's in beta on Free, Pro, and Max plans on the web and Claude Desktop, and requires memory to be on. Alongside it, Settings > Time and focus lets you set optional break reminders and quiet hours. For more information, refer to See your monthly recap and Set break reminders and quiet hours.

news.title: Claude Cowork on web and mobile
news.body: Claude Cowork is now available on web and mobile in addition to desktop. We are rolling this capability out over the next several weeks starting with the Max plan, with more plans to follow. Cowork runs your sessions remotely (in beta), so your sessions and files are saved to your Claude account and go where you go, on any device. Work continues when you close your laptop, and scheduled tasks run with no device online. Chat and Cowork also share one home now, with one place for your projects and artifacts across both. For more information, see Use Claude Cowork on web, desktop, and mobile.

news.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1
news.body: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, which it calls the world's most advanced models for coding and knowledge work. They are the same underlying model with different safeguards: Fable 5.1 is generally available, while Mythos 5.1 is limited to vetted professionals in cybersecurity and life sciences through Anthropic's access programs. Both carry a 1M-token context window, 128k max output and always-on adaptive thinking at $10 / $50 per million tokens, the same as Fable 5, with cache reads cut to $0.25 per million, about 25% cheaper in practice.

news.title: Claude Commerce Agents Go Open Source
news.body: Anthropic is open-sourcing Claude Commerce Agents: a blueprint for building shopping and merchant agents, with reference implementations across retail, travel, telecom and entertainment.

news.title: Claude in Chrome Generally Available
news.body: Claude in Chrome is out of preview and generally available.

news.title: Managed Agents Cookbook for the Vercel Chat SDK
news.body: A new cookbook connects a Claude Managed Agent to Vercel's Chat SDK, giving an agent a universal chat layer to sit behind. The code is in the anthropics/claude-quickstarts repository under managed-agents/chat-sdk.

news.title: Claude Team Plan for Scientists
news.body: Anthropic opened a Claude Team plan for scientists to 10,000 researchers across every field. Standard seats are free; premium seats with 5x usage limits are $15 a month for a year, an 80% discount. Principal investigators at academic and nonprofit research institutions sign up and add their group. It follows Claude Science in June and the AI for Science credit programme, and Anthropic plans to extend it well past the initial 10,000 seats.

news.title: Resume Terminal Sessions in the Desktop App
news.body: A session started in the Claude Code CLI can be picked up in the desktop app. Type /resume, choose the session, and it continues with the full conversation and context intact.

news.title: Weekly Limits in Claude Code Rise 25%
news.body: From 14 September, standard weekly limits in Claude Code go up 25% permanently for Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans. The temporary 50% increase stays in place until then, so measured against today the change works out to a 17% reduction. Anthropic says further changes are coming to give more visibility and control over usage.

news.title: Auto-Continue After Usage Limits in Claude Code Desktop
news.body: Claude Code desktop now has an auto-continue checkbox for usage limits. Turn it on and it picks up where you left off automatically once your limit resets.

news.title: The /design Skill in Claude Code
news.body: Claude Code can design now. The new /design skill, a research preview, brings Claude Design's artboard workflow into the CLI and Desktop, built on artifacts. Run /design to get editable artboards for your UI — pick one, tweak it, then have Claude implement it.

news.title: How Claude's Text Watermark Works
news.body: Anthropic explained the text watermark coming to future Claude models, added to meet EU AI Act requirements. When several word choices are equally valid, the model biases that pick using a hidden pattern that Anthropic can later detect, so Claude's involvement can be verified without changing output quality or spending extra tokens.

news.title: Improved Biology Safeguards in Claude Fable 5
news.body: Anthropic updated Claude Fable 5's biology safeguards, cutting biology-related fallbacks by about 85% across product surfaces. That means fewer legitimate requests, like everyday health questions, educational biology content, and clinical tasks for healthcare professionals, get redirected to the less capable Opus 5 model. Fable 5 still blocks requests in dual-use research areas such as virology, toxicology, and molecular design.

news.title: Session Budgets in Claude Managed Agents
news.body: You can now set a budget for Claude Managed Agents sessions to keep spend predictable. Sessions that hit the limit pause with a budget_reached event, and you can raise the budget to resume. One of four Managed Agents updates Anthropic shipped this week.

news.title: Claude Code Sessions Can Message Each Other
news.body: Your Claude Code sessions can now message each other. Instead of re-explaining yourself in another session, tell Claude to do it: it sends a summary (not your history or files), and the other session picks it up mid-task.

news.title: Auto Mode Becomes the Claude Code Default
news.body: Starting August 14, auto mode will be the default permission mode in Claude Code for Pro, Max, and Team users. Auto mode reviews shell commands and actions with a separate classifier: in testing it caught 89% of dangerous commands, while manual approval caught 14%.

news.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
news.body: Anthropic introduced Claude Opus 5, a thoughtful, proactive model with near-frontier performance at about half the cost of Claude Fable 5. It sets the state of the art on coding benchmarks, doubles Opus 4.8's Frontier-Bench score, beats everything but Fable 5 on OSWorld 2.0 at a third of the cost, and produces the strongest visual output of any Opus yet. Pricing stays at $5/$25 per million tokens. It's the new default on Claude Max, the strongest model on Pro, and available in the API, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork, with Fast mode support.

news.title: Managed Agents Gets New Features
news.body: Anthropic added several features to Claude Managed Agents: configure effort levels per agent, seed sessions with events, add up to 500 skills per session, use webhooks for environments and memory stores, and stream events for sub-agents.

news.title: Upgraded Voice Mode
news.body: Claude's voice mode now runs on Claude's more capable models and can reach the tools you've connected mid-conversation. Talk through the hard problems out loud, in many more languages.

news.title: Claude Security Plugin for Claude Code (Beta)
news.body: The Claude Security plugin for Claude Code is now in beta. Scan your changes for vulnerabilities before you commit, or run a full scan across your codebase, all from your terminal on the Claude inference you already run.

news.title: Record a Skill in Claude Cowork
news.body: New in Claude Cowork: teach Claude a skill by recording your screen while you do a task and talking through it as you go. Claude turns the recording into a skill it can run again. Find it under 'Record a skill' in the + menu of the Claude desktop app. Available on Pro, Max, and Team plans.

news.title: Economic Index Connector
news.body: Anthropic launched a connector that lets you query the Anthropic Economic Index directly in Claude. Ask natural-language questions about how AI is used across occupations, regions, and tasks (like which jobs use AI most, or what teachers use Claude for) and get answers grounded in real Index data with citations. It works across all Claude models, takes about a minute to enable from the connectors menu, and the full datasets stay free on Anthropic's site.

news.title: Claude for Teachers
news.body: Anthropic launched Claude for Teachers, a free AI tool for K-12 educators that automates planning and admin so teachers can focus on evidence-based practices like differentiation and mastery-based learning. It maps lesson plans to state standards, builds differentiated materials, analyzes class data, and connects to trusted curricula (OpenSciEd, Illustrative Mathematics) and nine edtech partners including Canva Education, MagicSchool, and Diffit. Free for verified US K-12 educators with full access through June 30, 2027.

news.title: Artifacts: Public Sharing + Multiplayer Editing
news.body: Claude Artifacts now support public sharing and multiplayer editing in Claude Code, and can be created with Claude Tag. Publish an artifact for anyone to open, and collaborate on it with others in real time.

news.title: Claude Code In-App Browser
news.body: Claude Code on desktop now has an in-app browser — Claude can pull up docs, designs, or any other site and read, click through, and interact the same way it does with your local dev servers. It is sandboxed and configurable, so you choose whether sessions persist.

news.title: Claude for Open Source Expands
news.body: Anthropic is expanding Claude for Open Source to more of the community — offering 6 months of Claude Max 20x free. Maintainers, core contributors, people landing PRs across the ecosystem, and those keeping critical packages alive can apply today.

news.title: Claude Cowork on Mobile and Web
news.body: Claude Cowork is coming to mobile and web — hand Claude a task at your desk and pick up the finished work from your phone. Close the laptop and Claude keeps going. The beta rolls out over the next several weeks, starting with the Max plan and more plans to follow.

news.title: Artifacts in Claude Code on Pro & Max
news.body: Artifacts in Claude Code are now available on Pro and Max plans. Ask for an artifact and Claude writes the code, publishes it live to claude.ai, and updates it in real time while it keeps working. Pages are private to your account and fully self-contained.

news.title: Higher Claude API Rate Limits
news.body: Anthropic raised Claude Platform API rate limits for all users and simplified the tiers, which are no longer based on API spend. The latest Sonnet and Haiku models now provide 5x higher rate limits at the highest tier.

news.title: Claude Sonnet 5
news.body: Anthropic introduced Claude Sonnet 5 — its most agentic Sonnet yet. It makes plans, uses tools like browsers and terminals, and runs autonomously at a level that until recently required larger, more expensive models.

news.title: Claude Desktop on Linux
news.body: Claude Desktop is now available on Linux (Ubuntu and Debian) in beta — alongside the browser and terminal, you get a first-class desktop experience with Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and chat on all paid plans.

news.title: Claude in Microsoft Foundry
news.body: You can now run Claude models in Microsoft Foundry, hosted on Azure. Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Haiku 4.5 are available through the Messages API with capabilities like prompt caching, thinking, and more.

news.title: Introducing Claude Tag
news.body: Claude comes to Slack as a collaborative teammate — tag @Claude in a channel to delegate tasks. It can access selected tools and data, learn from channel context over time, and work autonomously while your team focuses elsewhere.

news.title: Artifacts in Claude Code
news.body: Claude Code now supports Artifacts — interactive pages built from your full session, like a PR walkthrough or a living project dashboard, shared with your team at a private link. Available in beta on Team and Enterprise plans.

news.title: Two-Way Sync: Claude Code ↔ Claude Design
news.body: Claude Code and Claude Design now sync both ways. Run /design-sync to pull your design system into your repo and build against your real components, or push what you've built back into Claude Design and keep editing on the canvas.

news.title: Claude Design Updates
news.body: New in Claude Design: it stays on brand with your design system across projects, lets you edit directly on the canvas, syncs with Claude Code, and connects to more of the tools you already use.

news.title: Dynamic Workflows
news.body: New in Claude Code (research preview): dynamic workflows — Claude writes an orchestration script on the fly and spins up a large fleet of coordinated subagents in parallel.

news.title: /fork Update
news.body: /fork in Claude Code now runs a background agent with your exact context and prompt cache; the old /fork behavior is now /branch.

news.title: Introducing Claude Opus 4.8
news.body: Introducing Claude Opus 4.8 — sharper judgment, more honesty about its own progress, and the ability to work independently for longer. Available at the same price.

news.title: Claude Marketplace: Five New Partners
news.body: Augment Code, Bolt, CodeRabbit, Hebbia, and Legora join the Claude Marketplace. Apply your existing Anthropic spend commitment toward their Claude-powered products.

news.title: Security-Guidance Plugin for Claude Code
news.body: A security-guidance plugin for Claude Code is now available — helps identify and fix vulnerabilities as you write code. Available for all Claude Code users via the plugin marketplace (/plugins).

news.title: Self-Hosted Sandboxes + MCP Tunnels for Managed Agents
news.body:
We've added two security improvements to Claude Managed Agents.

Self-hosted sandboxes keep the agent's execution environment in your infrastructure or with a managed sandbox provider.

MCP tunnels let the agent connect to services inside your security perimeter.

news.title: Claude Design Token Limits Doubled
news.body: You can now create more with Claude Design. Token limits have been doubled across every plan.

news.title: "Extra Usage" Renamed to "Usage Credits"
news.body: Anthropic renamed 'extra usage' to 'usage credits' across Claude. Spending limits, auto-reload settings, and previously purchased credits carry over exactly as they were.

news.title: Why Usage Credits Now
news.body: Why the rename? 'Extra usage' originally meant paying when you hit a plan limit. Usage credits now power more — including features like Fast Mode directly.

news.title: Prompt Cache Diagnostics in Claude Console
news.body: Prompt cache diagnostics are now in Claude Console. When a request misses the cache, you can see exactly which part of your prompt changed and how many tokens it cost you.

news.title: Cache Diagnostics Docs + Dashboard
news.body: Check prompt cache diagnostics in the Claude Console usage dashboard and read the cache diagnostics docs for more on optimizing for cache hits.

news.title: Fast Mode Now Defaults to Opus 4.7 in Claude Code
news.body: Fast mode now defaults to Opus 4.7 in Claude Code. Try it with /fast.

news.title: How Fast Mode Works
news.body: Fast mode is identical Opus quality at ~2.5× the response speed, billed at a higher per-token rate. Use it when latency matters more than cost: rapid iteration, live debugging, time-sensitive work.

news.title: Claude for Small Business
news.body: Anthropic launches Claude for Small Business — 15 agentic workflows across finance, ops, sales, marketing, HR, and customer service. Integrates with QuickBooks, PayPal, HubSpot, Canva, Docusign, Google Workspace, and Microsoft 365. Plans payroll, closes books, tracks metrics, runs campaigns, chases invoices, and analyzes margins. Free "AI Fluency for Small Business" course with PayPal + a multi-city SMB Tour.

news.title: Claude Code Weekly Limits +50%
news.body: Claude Code weekly limits are increasing 50%, now through July 13. Live for all Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise users. Applies everywhere you use Claude Code — CLI, IDE extensions, desktop, and web. Nothing to opt into. Stacks with last week's 2× increase to 5-hour limits.

news.title: Dedicated Monthly Credit for Programmatic Usage
news.body:
Starting June 15, paid Claude plans get a dedicated monthly credit for programmatic usage — Claude Agent SDK, `claude -p`, Claude Code GitHub Actions, and third-party apps built on the Agent SDK. SDK and `claude -p` usage no longer share your subscription rate limits — interactive use gets its own budget.

news.title: AI Gateway adds confidence-based decision fallbacks
news.body: AI Gateway can now escalate a decision request to a fallback model when the primary model's answer trips a confidence condition you set. Conditions can be combined, so an escalation can depend on more than one signal. The plain model names you already list in models keep catching outright errors, so existing fallbacks are unaffected. Confidence conditions cover Choice and Score questions. Boolean questions escalate on a probability range instead. Set the fallback by adding one conditional object to providerOptions.gateway.models. Requests without it keep their existing behavior. Leave out question and the condition checks every question of the matching type, so { "confidenceBelow": 0.6 } escalates when any Choice or Score answer falls below 0.6. Because a triggered fallback runs a second decision, it bills both stages. Decision fallbacks are in beta. Learn more in the decision fallbacks documentation. Read more

news.title: Nano Banana 2.1 now available on AI Gateway
news.body: Nano Banana 2.1 from Google is now available on AI Gateway. It improves image generation and editing over earlier Nano Banana models. This release targets product recontextualization, mask- and ink-based editing, and factuality. Product recontextualization places an existing product in a new scene. Mask- and ink-based edits change only the region marked by a mask or by strokes drawn on the image. Factuality is how accurately images depict real-world subjects. The model renders photorealistic skin tones, intricate materials, sharp lighting, and coherent backgrounds at the latency and cost of a Flash-tier model. Call it through the AI SDK or the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API, or the AI CLI. AI CLI is an open-source command-line tool from Vercel Labs for generating text, images, video, and audio from your terminal. It runs on AI Gateway, so any Gateway model ID works with -m. Use google/gemini-nano-banana-2.1 as the model name. Generated images are returned in result.files: Try Nano Banana 2.1 in the model playground. news.title: CLI archive deployments are now up to 30% faster with split-tgz archive option
news.body: The archive option was introduced for CLI deployments hitting rate limits like the limit on the maximum amount of files. Prebuilt deployments commonly use archive uploads as they generate thousands of files at build time. Previously, archive deployments were always compressed into one large file with the only existing --archive option, tgz. Deployments using tgz may hit the file size upload limit. Additionally, uploading one large archive file is slower than uploading multiple file parts. The beta split-tgz format resolves these issues by splitting large archives into smaller parts. split-tgz avoids the static file upload limit and uploads large prebuilt projects up to 30% faster. Example usage: vercel deploy --archive=split-tgz Learn more about CLI deployments. Read more

news.title: Introducing Fluid compute
news.body: While dedicated servers provide efficiency and always-on availability, they often lead to over-provisioning, scaling challenges, and operational overhead. Serverless computing improves this with auto-scaling and pay-as-you-go pricing, but can suffer from cold starts and inefficient use of idle time. It’s time for a new, balanced approach. Fluid compute evolves beyond serverless, trading single-invocation functions for high-performance mini-servers. This model has helped thousands of early adopters maximize resource efficiency, minimize cold starts, and reduce compute costs by up to 85%. Read more

news.title: Vercel Functions can now run on Fluid compute
news.body: Vercel Functions can now run on Fluid compute, bringing improvements in efficiency, scalability, and cost effectiveness. Fluid is now available for all plans. What’s New Optimized concurrency: Functions can handle multiple requests per instance, reducing idle time and lowering compute costs by up to 85% for high-concurrency workloads Cold start protection: Fewer cold starts with smarter scaling and pre-warmed instances Optimized scaling: Functions scale before instances, moving beyond the traditional 1:1 invocation-to-instance model Extended function lifecycle: Use waitUntil to run background tasks after responding to the client Runaway cost protection: Detects and stops infinite loops and excessive invocations Multi-region execution: Requests are routed to the nearest of your selected compute region for better performance Node.js and Python support: No restrictions on native modules or standard libraries Enable Fluid today or learn more in our blog and documentation. Read more

news.title: ISR on Vercel is now faster and more cost-efficient
news.body: When Next.js introduced Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) in 2020, it changed how developers build for the web. ISR combines the speed of static generation with the flexibility of dynamic rendering, enabling sites to update content without requiring full rebuilds. Vercel has supported ISR from day one, making it easy for teams at The Washington Post, Algolia, and Sonos to serve fresh content while keeping page loads fast. Read more

news.title: Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) is now faster and more cost-efficient
news.body: Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) enables you to update content in the background without needing to redeploying your application. You can scale CMS or content-backed applications to millions of pages without having slow builds. We've optimized our infrastructure to make ISR faster and more cost-efficient: Smaller writes: ISR cache writes are now compressed by default, using fewer ISR write and read units (8KB chunks) per update and lowering Fast Origin Transfer (FOT) costs. Both reads and writes are now compressed. Region-aware caching: The ISR cache is now available in all regions and automatically aligns with your functions' region. If your project spans multiple regions, the most cost-effective location is chosen automatically. This improves performance, especially for traffic outside North America, and regional pricing applies. Redeploy your project to apply these updates or learn more about ISR. Update: The rollout of this change completed on February 5th, 2025 around 8am PST. Read more

news.title: Jev for Python engineers
news.body: It's simply impossible to not hear about Jev. Seemingly everyone is tinkering with it in some way, from using it to make trading decisions (what could possibly go wrong?) to generating UIs with it (maybe we're onto something here!). Jev is a new kind of AI model. You feed it data and ask it a set of multiple-choice questions, and it responds with its answers and how confident it is in each. Just like with any other model, Jev can and will make mistakes, but it will make them fast. ​ ​The bottom line is: Jev is built for making narrow decisions. Whether it's accurate enough for your use cases is something you'll need to test. The job of the Python team at Vercel is to make it easy for Python devs to tinker with Jev, among a few other things. So please welcome the latest release of the AI SDK for Python. Install it with uv add ai to use the new experimental evaluate() API, which talks directly to Jev's nervous system. Then create an AI Gateway key, set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, and try this complete example: Now, I'd like to explain what Jev is and how to make it work for you using a couple of examples. One is good and one is dumb. Ask Jev which is which. Let's have some fun! Jev ELI5 Jev

news.title: How Fluid compute works on Vercel
news.body: Fluid compute is Vercel’s next-generation compute model designed to handle modern workloads with real-time scaling, cost efficiency, and minimal overhead. At the center of Fluid is Vercel Functions router, which orchestrates function execution to minimize cold starts, maximize concurrency, and optimize resource usage. It dynamically routes invocations to pre-warmed or active instances, ensuring low-latency execution.
