title: Google Gemini
description: Google's AI assistant — write, plan, brainstorm, generate images, and analyze files with one of the most powerful multimodal models.

news.title: Gemini Nano Banana 2.1 generally available (GA)
news.body: : Released Gemini Nano Banana 2.1 (gemini-nano-banana-2.1), the latest high-efficiency image generation and conversational editing model. An update to Nano Banana 2 (gemini-3.1-flash-image), it maintains Flash-level speed and cost efficiency while delivering significant improvements in visual quality, prompt adherence, multi-turn character consistency, text rendering, and wide and panoramic aspect ratio generation (1:4, 4:1, 1:8, 8:1) across 1K, 2K, and 4K resolutions. See the Image generation guide to get started. Deprecation announcement: The gemini-3.1-flash-image model is deprecated and will be shut down on October 29, 2026. Migrate to gemini-nano-banana-2.1.

news.title: Ask Gemini Is Available in Google Chat
news.body: Ask Gemini in Google Chat is now available to help people set priorities, catch up on their work, and prepare for meetings from within Chat.

media.alt: Google Workspace demonstration of Ask Gemini in Google Chat

news.title: Six Ways Workspace Intelligence Offers Personalized Help
news.body: Google explains how Workspace Intelligence uses work context across Chat, Drive, Gmail, Docs, Slides, and Sheets to reduce prompting. Examples include daily briefings, answers from files, email drafts in your voice, citable document drafts, branded slides, and editable spreadsheets with formulas. Google notes that some features, including team knowledge search in Chat and AI Inbox, are coming soon to business users.

news.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS generally available (GA)
news.body: : Released our next-generation text-to-speech (TTS) audio models and the Gemini API Voices endpoint (/v1beta/voices): Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS (gemini-3.8-flash-tts): Flagship creative TTS model engineered for studio-grade voice fidelity, nuanced acting, regional dialects, and long-form multi-turn stability. Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS (gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts): Fast, cost-efficient TTS model built to replace gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview for high-throughput production and real-time voice agent cascades. Voice design, Voice replication, and the Extended Voice Library: Create persistent custom vocal personas from text prompts, replicate voices with consent verification, and query 150+ prebuilt and custom voices. See the Text-to-speech guide to get started.

news.title: New Connected Apps in Gemini
news.body: Google is rolling out new connected apps in Gemini. Productivity connections include Airtable, Linear, monday.com, PandaDoc, Wispr AI, and Zoho; creative apps include Adobe, Picsart, Squarespace, and Webflow; and lifestyle connections include Apartments.com, Experian, Peloton, and SeatGeek. Connect them in Gemini settings or invoke them in chat with an @ mention or a direct request.

media.alt: Gemini demonstration of its new app connections

news.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash and Flash-Lite TTS Launch
news.body: Google released Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Flash-Lite TTS for expressive text-to-speech generation. Flash focuses on voice fidelity and nuanced delivery, while Flash-Lite is designed for faster, higher-volume use. Both are available through the Gemini API and in Google AI Studio, alongside a Voices endpoint and voice design options.

media.alt: Google AI Studio demonstration of Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech models

news.title: Gemini 2.5 models access update
news.body: : To ensure reliable performance for everyone, we are limiting access to the 2.5 models to users who have actively used them in the past. These models are not deprecated and will continue to be served until further notice through the API. For any new projects, use our latest models: 3.5 Flash-Lite or 3.8 Flash. This helps us maintain sufficient capacity for both ongoing legacy workflows and new applications.

news.title: Antigravity Agent 09-2026
news.body: : Released antigravity-preview-09-2026, which replaces and deprecates antigravity-preview-05-2026. If you run on a remote sandbox (environment: "remote") and read only output_text or model_output steps, update the agent string and nothing else changes. If you run tools locally (local_environment) or parse function_call steps, the built-in tools changed. Parameters use PascalCase instead of snake_case, and file edits use line-range replacements instead of full rewrites. Capability 05-2026 09-2026 File creation write_file(path, content) write_to_file(TargetFile, CodeContent, Overwrite, Description) File editing write_file(path, content), full rewrite replace_file_content(TargetFile, StartLine, EndLine, TargetContent, ReplacementContent) File reading read_file(path, offset, limit), byte offsets view_file(AbsolutePath, StartLine, EndLine, ContentOffset) Directory listing list_files(path) list_dir(DirectoryPath) File and code search None, agents used shell commands find_by_name(SearchDirectory, Pattern, MaxDepth) and grep_search(SearchPath, Query, IsRegex) Shell execution code_execution(command, timeout_seconds) Unchanged Web search google_search(queries) Unchanged See the Antigravity A

news.title: Six Mini Apps You Can Build With Sheets Canvas
news.body: Google published a guide to Sheets canvas, a Gemini 3.8 Flash powered feature that turns spreadsheet data into custom, interactive mini apps described in natural language. Edits made on the canvas sync back to the underlying cells in real time. The six examples cover Kanban boards, executive dashboards, financial scenario models, event schedules, 2x2 priority matrices, and brainstorm workshop boards. It is available on Business and Enterprise Standard and Plus, Google AI Pro and Ultra, and Google AI Pro for Education via Insert > Create a canvas.

news.title: Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking generally available (GA)
news.body: : Released two new audio-to-audio models for real-time voice applications using the Live API: Gemini 3.8 Live (gemini-3.8-live): The default option for most low-latency voice agent experiences and real-time dialogue without reasoning delays. Features interleaved reasoning, default asynchronous function calling, and full session client content updates. Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking): High-reasoning audio-to-audio model supporting background reasoning during live audio interactions, recommended when higher background reasoning is required. To get started, see the Live API guide, the Capabilities guide, and the Thinking guide.

news.title: Lyria 3.5 generally available (GA)
news.body: : Released the next generation of Google's music generation model: lyria-3.5: Full-length song generation with improved musical coherence, natural vocals, and fine-grained duration and structural control. The model supports text and image inputs and generates high-fidelity 44.1 kHz stereo audio. See the Music generation guide for details and code samples.

news.title: The Gemini App Is Now Available for Windows
news.body: Google launched the Gemini app for Windows, with an Alt + Space shortcut for instant help over your active work. The desktop app also brings Gemini Spark, Google app context, and image and video creation into one workspace.

news.title: New Google AI Plan Features
news.body: Google added new capabilities across its AI plans: use voice in Gmail, Docs, and Keep; create and edit visuals with Google Pics; turn Sheets into interactive mini-apps; let Gemini Spark handle web errands and photo tasks; and give eligible college students a free year of a Google AI plan.

news.title: Less Switching, More Flow in Google Workspace
news.body: Gemini can now handle complex, cross-app tasks across Gmail, Drive, Docs, Slides, and Chat. Create presentations from Chat, build spreadsheets in Drive, draft emails in Docs, turn email threads into structured briefs, and convert Docs into editable branded decks without leaving the app you are using.

news.title: Lyria 3.5 in public preview
news.body: : Released the next generation of Google's music generation models: lyria-3.5-clip-preview: Optimized for 30-second clips, loops, and rapid experimentation. lyria-3.5-pro-preview: Full-length song generation with improved musical coherence, natural vocals, and fine-grained duration and structural control. Both models support text and image inputs and generate high-fidelity 44.1 kHz stereo audio. See the Music generation guide for details and code samples.

news.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash generally available (GA)
news.body: : Released gemini-3.8-flash, our most intelligent Flash model, engineered for long-horizon software engineering, autonomous agents, and complex enterprise workflows. To get started, see the Gemini 3.8 Flash model page and the Latest model guide.

news.title: Agentic video understanding
news.body: : Released agentic video understanding for Gemini 3.7 Flash, 3.6 Flash, and 3.5 Flash-Lite across the Interactions and GenerateContent APIs. The model dynamically navigates video timelines, requesting transcripts, frames, or audio tracks on demand. This approach uses up to 88% fewer tokens for long-form content compared to static processing. To get started, see the Agentic video understanding guide.

news.title: Gemini Omni Flash generally available (GA)
news.body: : Released gemini-omni-1.1-flash, the GA version of our fast, conversational video generation and editing model. This release includes significant new capabilities: Video extension: Seamlessly extend existing videos by generating continuations at the end of a clip using the extend task or directly with a prompt. Interpolation (first + last frame): Generate a video transitioning between two images using the image_to_video task with up to 2 images. Resolution control: New resolution parameter in video_config supports 360p, 720p (default), 1080p, and 4k outputs. 1080p and 4K outputs are generated using upscaling. The existing gemini-omni-flash-preview endpoint will be deprecated on September 30, 2026. To get started, see the Gemini Omni Flash model page and the omni guide.

news.title: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe generally available (GA)
news.body: : Released two dedicated speech-to-text models based on Gemini's audio understanding: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe (gemini-3.5-transcribe): High-accuracy, low-latency non-streaming speech-to-text with utterance-based language detection across 85+ languages, speaker diarization, word-level timestamps, and custom vocabulary biasing (up to 1,000 terms). Gemini 3.5 Transcribe Live (gemini-3.5-transcribe-live): Low-latency, bidirectional streaming speech-to-text over WebSockets using the Live API, supporting interim and finalized transcription events, Smart transcription mode, and multiple Voice Activity Detection (VAD) strategies. To get started, see the Audio transcription guide, the Live transcription guide, and the Gemini 3.5 Transcribe model page.

news.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash generally available (GA)
news.body: : Released our most intelligent workhorse model yet for coding and agents: Gemini 3.7 Flash (gemini-3.7-flash): Substantial improvements across software engineering, web development, and agentic workflows, available at an introductory price through December 31, 2026. To get started, see the Gemini 3.7 Flash model page and the Latest model guide.

news.title: Introducing Agentic Video Understanding with Gemini
news.body: Gemini models can now scan video dynamically, jumping between segments instead of processing every frame at a fixed rate, which Google says cuts token use by up to 88% and cost by up to 66%. It is available on Gemini 3.7 Flash, 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, with the Gemini app and YouTube's Ask YouTube feature to follow.

news.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber
news.body: Google released Gemini 3.8 Flash, a significant step up from 3.7 Flash for agentic tasks and software engineering at the same price ($0.75 per million input tokens, $3.75 per million output), and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, a variant with frontier-level vulnerability detection and patching that is available only to trusted defenders through Google's Fairwind Program.

news.title: Agentic Gemini Live
news.body: Gemini Live picked up agentic capabilities, so more can be done by voice alone: listen to your Daily Brief, triage email, or get help from Spark, all by talking to Gemini.

news.title: Scene Extension with Omni 1.1 Flash
news.body: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash can extend a video from where it left off, either to carry a story further or to branch it somewhere new. Create or upload a clip, then ask Gemini to extend the scene with whatever happens next. Select Create video in the tools menu to start. Available globally to Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers.

news.title: Everything New in the Gemini App
news.body: Google says the Gemini app became the fastest growing product in its history this month, and its 14th to reach a billion users. The roundup covers a free one-year student plan, a student hub and interactive study notebooks, Gemini 3.7 Flash in chat and Spark, Gemini in Waymo, a toggle for visible watermarks, clip extension with Omni 1.1 Flash, more app connections, and new agentic capabilities in Gemini Live.

news.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash
news.body: Google introduced Gemini 3.7 Flash, its most intelligent workhorse model yet for coding and agents. It arrives three weeks after Gemini 3.6 Flash, driven by developer feedback and algorithmic innovations Google says will carry into future models.

news.title: 10 Free Gemini Omni Video Edits
news.body: Level up your video editing with Gemini Omni — create up to 10 videos at no cost until 11:59pm PT on August 4, 2026. Change objects, add interactions between subject and space, and more.

news.title: Voice on Gemini for macOS
news.body: You can now create, edit, and summarize with Gemini on macOS using your voice. Long-press Fn to dictate clean text, or ask Gemini to transform highlighted content, analyze local files, and generate visuals right where your cursor is. Rolling out globally in English, with more languages coming soon.

news.title: Spark Auto-Browses Chrome + 160+ New Countries
news.body: Gemini Spark now integrates directly with Chrome to handle tedious web errands, like scheduling apartment viewings or researching flights, using your logged-in accounts and saved passwords, with protections against prompt injection and approval required for sensitive actions like payments. Chrome auto-browse starts in the U.S. Google AI Pro subscribers in 160+ additional countries also now have access to Spark.

news.title: Gemini Spark Rolls Out to AI Pro
news.body: Gemini Spark is now also starting to roll out to Google AI Pro subscribers in the U.S., with more countries coming soon. Spark is the personal AI agent that works in the background to get things done under your direction.

news.title: Real-Time Help in Gemini Live
news.body: Gemini Live can give you real-time assistance with whatever you see, whenever you see it. Tap the Gemini Live icon in the Gemini app, click the camera, point your lens at whatever you need help with, and ask, whether it's step-by-step repair instructions or help navigating a confusing error code.

news.title: Gemini in Chrome Launches in the UK
news.body: Gemini in Google Chrome launched in the UK, bringing its AI features to the desktop browser. Gemini can help regardless of which Chrome tab you are in, summarizing pages, comparing options, answering questions, and helping you multitask across tabs.

news.title: AI Overviews in Google Drive
news.body: Your Google Drive has lore, and now Gemini can help you explore it. AI Overviews let you find files and information by asking a simple question in natural language, so you spend less time searching and more time getting things done.

news.title: Avatars in Gemini (Nano Banana)
news.body: Placing yourself in different scenes, styles, or eras just got faster: set up your digital avatar in Gemini once, and create custom Nano Banana images of yourself without uploading a selfie every single time.

news.title: Gemini Spark Rolling Out to More Countries
news.body: Gemini Spark is now rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in more countries and languages. Spark is your personal AI agent that works in the background 24/7 to get things done under your direction.

news.title: Gemini Spark Real-Time Tracking
news.body: Gemini Spark can now intelligently track topics and react to events in real time — for example, set up a prompt to get tailored game analyses emailed to you after your favorite team plays.

news.title: Gemini Spark + Agent Updates
news.body: Gemini Spark is coming to the Gemini app for macOS, alongside updates to the 24/7 personal AI agent: custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, integrations with Canva, Dropbox, Instacart, OpenTable, and Zillow Rentals, connections to Google Tasks and Keep to turn brain-dumps into action items, and real-time tracking of topics like sports, stocks, and news.

news.title: Personalized Image Creation
news.body: More U.S. users can now create personalized images for free in Gemini. By connecting your Google apps in settings, Gemini grounds image creation in your preferences and fills in the blanks — and you can connect or disconnect apps anytime.

news.title: Take Notes for Me in Google Meet
news.body: "Take notes for me" in Google Meet is rolling out to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in select languages — let Gemini capture the details so you can focus on the discussion.

news.title: Study Notebooks in Gemini
news.body: At ISTE 2026, Google introduced study notebooks in Gemini — turning it into an interactive, adaptive learning platform with personalized lessons — plus no-cost ACT/GRE practice tests and Gemini in Google Classroom for students.

news.title: Create/Edit Images in Gemini Live
news.body: You can now create and edit images directly in Gemini Live — test room decor, get help with math, or create memes in real time using your camera.

news.title: Thinking Levels
news.body: Thinking Levels are now available on Gemini across Web, iOS, and Android.

news.title: Gemini Spark
news.body: Gemini Spark is now available to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in the U.S. — handles heavy lifting and connects across your digital ecosystem.

news.title: India Video Edit
news.body: Users in India can now upload and edit videos directly with Gemini Omni.

news.title: Gemini Connects to OpenTable, Canva, Instacart
news.body: Gemini can now connect to even more apps, including OpenTable, Canva, and Instacart. Whether you're booking a table, creating a flyer, or ordering groceries, Gemini doesn't just find info — it takes action via connected apps.

news.title: Daily Brief Rolls Out
news.body: Get a head start on your day with Daily Brief — Gemini proactively flags what matters most in an easily digestible to-do list. Now available to all Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra subscribers 18+ in the U.S. — open Gemini and select Daily Brief in the side panel.

news.title: SynthID Expands to OpenAI, Kakao, and ElevenLabs
news.body: Google is bringing the SynthID watermark to generative content from OpenAI, Kakao, and ElevenLabs — building on its earlier NVIDIA partnership. Industry-wide collaboration on content transparency is the whole point: a single watermark only works if everyone speaks it. Announced at Google I/O.

news.title: Introducing Gemini Omni
news.body:
We're dropping Gemini Omni: our first step towards a model that can create anything from anything — starting with video.

It combines Gemini's intelligence with our generative media systems — representing a leap forward in world understanding, multimodality, and editing.

news.title: Gemini Spark — 24/7 Personal AI Agent
news.body: Introducing Gemini Spark — our 24/7 personal AI agent designed to proactively manage tasks and help you navigate your digital life, all under your direction. Coming to trusted testers this week, and as a Beta for US Google AI Ultra subscribers next week.

news.title: Gemini Live Now Inline in the App
news.body: Gemini Live now opens immediately and inline in the Gemini app, so you can seamlessly switch between typing a quick question and diving deeper in a free-flowing conversation, and then back again. Smarter, faster, and less distracted by background noise.

news.title: Daily Brief — Your Morning Digest Agent
news.body: Introducing Daily Brief — an out-of-the-box agent that creates a personalized digest in the Gemini app to be your first stop every morning. Synthesizes inbox, calendar, and tasks into a skimmable briefing organized by topic with suggested next steps. Rolling out today to Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra subscribers in the U.S.

news.title: Voice Understanding Comes to macOS
news.body: Powerful new voice understanding technology is coming to your laptop — think aloud without worrying about all the 'ums' and 'what abouts.' Using context on your screen, Gemini turns free-flowing speech into precise drafts, instantly reformatting text to capture your intent right where your cursor is. macOS app available to download today.

news.title: Google AI Ultra Price Drop + New $100 Tier
news.body: We're reducing the price of our top-tier Google AI Ultra plan from $250 to $200/mo AND introducing a new $100/mo Ultra plan tier. The new plan unlocks 5x higher usage limits to the Gemini app than the Pro plan, plus early access to new features, 20 TB storage, YouTube Premium, and more.

news.title: Content Verification Tools Expand Across Google
news.body: As generative media becomes more advanced, it's helpful to know exactly where content comes from — and if it's been changed. Today we're expanding content verification tools across Search, the Gemini app, Google Chrome, and Made by Google.

news.title: Gemini Surpasses 900 Million Users
news.body: In just a year, Gemini app users have more than doubled, surpassing 900 million.

news.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash Drops at I/O
news.body: It wouldn't be a Google I/O without new models. Say hello to Gemini 3.5 Flash — frontier performance for agents and coding, excelling at complex long-horizon tasks that deliver real-world utility. Now available via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.

news.title: Gemini Intelligence Comes to Android
news.body: Google unveiled Gemini Intelligence for Android — proactive AI on the phone that automates complex tasks, summarizes web content, and fills forms. Launches on Samsung Galaxy and Pixel this summer, then expands to watches, cars, glasses, and laptops later in 2026.

news.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite GA
news.body: Google made Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite generally available — the fastest and most cost-efficient model in the Gemini 3 family, built for high-volume agent tasks, translation, and simple data processing. Already in production at JetBrains, Gladly, Astrocade, and others.

news.title: Introducing Nano Banana Pro
news.body: Google DeepMind unveiled Nano Banana Pro — an advanced image generation and editing model built on Gemini 3 Pro with superior multilingual text rendering, better creative control, and 4K output.

news.title: Generate files directly in Gemini
news.body: Gemini can now generate Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, PDFs, Microsoft Word/Excel, CSV, LaTeX, plain text, RTF, and Markdown files directly in chat. Download or export to Drive without leaving the app.

news.title: Personal Intelligence + Nano Banana 2
news.body: Personal Intelligence now gives Gemini an understanding of your preferences and interests when generating images, so you can spend more time creating and less time explaining.

news.title: Gemini in Google Slides
news.body: Available today, Gemini in Google Slides generates on-brand presentations in minutes using your own Google Docs, Sheets, and PDFs as context. Every single element stays 100% editable. Try it at slides.new.

news.title: Gemini Omni 1.1 Brings New Controls to Google Vids
news.body: Google Vids now uses Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash for AI video creation. Extend scenes while keeping characters, lighting, and style consistent; set exact clip durations; and generate or upscale scenes in 1080p. Anyone with a Google or Workspace account can try AI video creation at no cost on desktop at vids.new.

news.title: Gemini Omni Editing in Google Vids
news.body: Editing videos used to take hours. Now? Just ask. With Gemini Omni in Google Vids, you don't need to be a professional editor: type a prompt to swap backgrounds, adjust lighting, and clean up messy footage instantly.

news.title: Direct Avatars in Product Demos
news.body: In Google Vids you can now create product demos by directing avatars to walk, talk, and interact with objects from a single text prompt. Available on desktop.

news.title: Claude Opus 5 in Rork
news.body: Claude Opus 5 is now live in Rork: state of the art on coding benchmarks, stronger visual output than any previous Opus, and near Fable 5 intelligence at half the price.

news.title: Rork AI Cloud (150+ Models)
news.body: Rork launched Rork AI Cloud — one-shot apps using any of 150+ models from Kling to GPT-Image 2 to ElevenLabs, no API keys required.

news.title: Smart Event Creation in Notion Calendar
news.body: Notion Calendar now lets you create an event by pressing Space in a new event and describing your plan. Calendar fills in the event details from your description.

news.title: Model Controls for Notion AI
news.body: Workspace admins can now choose which models are available in Notion Agent and Custom Agents, and set a default model for Custom Agents, under Settings → Notion AI → General → Model controls.

news.title: Interactive Agent Calendar Tools
news.body: Notion Calendar gave your personal agent new calendar tools. On desktop, you now see rich, interactive UI when you ask it to do calendar things, so you can take quick actions like jumping into a meeting link without leaving the chat.

news.title: AI Meeting Notes for Outlook
news.body: Notion Calendar AI Meeting Notes now work with Outlook calendar — upcoming meetings in your sidebar, calendar-driven notifications, rich meeting note headers with attendee and event details, and AI-powered transcription and summarization.

news.title: Outlook Support
news.body: Notion Calendar now connects to Outlook — view and edit events, RSVP, search, check availability, and schedule right alongside Google and iCloud, with all your calendars together in one place.

news.title: No more tool-specific Notion MCP rate limits
news.body: notion-search and notion-query-data-sources no longer have their own rate limits. Calls to these tools now count toward the standard request limits, like other Notion MCP tools. See Supported tools.

news.title: Create teamspace root pages with Notion MCP
news.body: notion-create-pages now supports creating pages directly in a teamspace with parent.teamspace_id. Use a user-backed connection with permission to add top-level pages; see Teamspace root pages for details and an example.

news.title: Custom blocks in markdown
news.body: The markdown content API and Notion MCP now read custom blocks with inherited bindings as instead of . You can place existing definitions and preserve unchanged instances during page edits; see Working with markdown content. Definition creation remains in private alpha.

news.title: New SIEM event for the AI meeting notes consent setting
news.body: The SIEM and DLP event stream now sends workspace.settings.meeting_notes_consent_setting_updated when an admin changes whether a workspace requires consent before AI meeting notes transcription. The payload carries the final state, either enabled or disabled. See SIEM events. This is separate from the existing audit log entry for a person confirming consent in a meeting. The new event records a change to the requirement, not an instance of consent.

news.title: Completing the query tool update in Notion MCP
news.body: notion-query-database-view is no longer available. Call notion-query-data-sources instead, and pass the same view_url as {"data": {"mode": "view", "view_url": "..."}}. Calls to the old tool name now return a tool error that names this replacement.

news.title: Higher Notion MCP search and query limits
news.body: Notion MCP now allows 20 search calls and 20 data source query calls per connection every 10 seconds. Rate-limit tool errors also include their structured JSON in the text response for clients that read only text. See Supported tools.

news.title: Page writes return 504 when a request times out
news.body: Update a page's content as markdown and the notion-update-page MCP tool now return HTTP 504 gateway_timeout when a request runs past its deadline. Before, they returned HTTP 500 internal_server_error. The notion-create-pages and notion-convert-page-to-skill MCP tools already returned 504 in this case. A 504 does not mean the write was undone, so check whether the change was saved before you retry it. A write that runs out of its time budget still returns 503 service_unavailable, with additional_data.retry_guidance. See Request limits for when to retry each status.

news.title: Custom emoji icons are validated
news.body: A custom_emoji icon on a page, database, data source, or callout must now name a custom emoji in the integration's workspace. Otherwise the request returns a validation_error instead of saving an icon that reads back as null. See Emoji and icon. Notion MCP applies the same check to custom_emoji: page icons in notion-create-pages and notion-update-page.

news.title: Rate limit waits in the response body
news.body: Any 429 or 529 response that includes a Retry-After header now repeats the wait in the body as additional_data.retry_after, so clients that can't read headers, such as MCP clients, can still see how long to wait. Two new rate_limit_reason values identify an endpoint's own limit (public_api_endpoint_rate_limit) and a connection whose API access has been restricted (public_api_request_blocked). A workspace-limit 429 now says that the limit is shared by all of the workspace's connections. See Request limits.

news.title: GPT-6 Luna and Sol Join Notion’s Model Picker
news.body: Notion is rolling out GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6 Sol as two additional choices in its model picker.

news.title: GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash in Notion Agents
news.body: Notion added the open-weight GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash models to Personal and Custom Agents.

news.title: Notion icon URLs are validated
news.body: An external icon URL that points at Notion's built-in icon set, such as https://www.notion.so/icons/pizza_blue.svg, sets a native icon and reads back as type: "icon". A URL that names no real icon or color now returns a validation_error instead of saving a broken icon. In Notion MCP, the page icon parameter on notion-create-pages and notion-update-page now accepts the icons/pizza_blue identifier that notion-fetch returns, so an icon can be copied from one page to another.

news.title: File uploads accept CAD and 3D model formats
news.body: The File Upload API now accepts common CAD and 3D model formats, including .dwg, .dxf, .dwf, .rvt, .rfa, .3dm, .step, .stl, .obj, and .glb. They attach to pages as file blocks.

news.title: application/octet-stream resolves from the file extension
news.body: Many HTTP clients label files with application/octet-stream when they can't infer a MIME type from the extension. Create a file upload and Send a file upload now treat that generic type as unspecified and resolve the real type from the filename extension, or from the content type set at creation. Files with unsupported extensions are still rejected.

news.title: Check tool access with notion-get-tool-access
news.body: Notion MCP has a new notion-get-tool-access tool. Call it with {} to get the full connection-scoped current_tool_access map. It takes an optional tool_names array such as ["search", "ai_search"] to narrow the result. Call it before you use a tool whose availability depends on the plan: to choose between notion-search and notion-ai-search, for example, or to see which parameters the workspace's plan restricts. Those tools now say so in their descriptions, and each points to one call for the whole map that you can reuse across them. It doesn't grant access or change the workspace. Entries in the map can now include restricted_parameters, which maps a parameter path such as filters.title_only to the reason it's unavailable. A restriction applies even when the entry's status is available, so check it before sending the parameter. Read the reason against your requested value: a single teamspace remains supported even when filters.teamspace_ids lists a restriction on multiple teamspaces. When ai_search is exposed and available, the map omits search, even when requested by name. Otherwise, the map can include both an available search entry and an unavailable ai_search entry, depending on

news.title: Search drops unavailable options instead of failing
news.body: A notion-search or notion-ai-search call that asks for a filter or sort the workspace's plan doesn't include now runs the supported part of the search. These calls previously returned a validation_error. The response adds a notices array naming the dropped fields, with an upgrade link when available, and results can be broader than requested and use relevance sorting. On a plan without multiple-teamspace search, when teamspace_id and filters.teamspace_ids select different teamspaces, both are dropped. If dropping the options leaves an empty query with no supported constraint, the response returns no results and a notice asking for a non-empty query or a supported filter. notion-ai-search content search on a plan without AI access now runs a keyword search in Notion only rather than returning an upgrade error. It still reports type: "ai_search" and explains in notices that connected sources weren't searched. A workspace with a billing restriction, such as an unpaid invoice, still gets a permission error asking a workspace owner to manage billing.

news.title: notion-ai-search handles user lookup
news.body: notion-ai-search now takes query_type. Set it to user with a name or email to look up a workspace user, and the response reports type: "user_search", the same as notion-search. Omit query_type, or set it to internal, for a content search. Content filters and sorting aren't valid with a user lookup and return a validation_error. A user lookup doesn't need AI access, but both search tools need user information capabilities. Workspace-owned MCP connections must also expose notion-get-users. Choose an exposed search tool; switching tools doesn't bypass these permissions.

news.title: Introducing the Notion Skills API
news.body: Notion has introduced the Notion Skills API. Teams can edit their skills in Notion and use them in ChatGPT, Claude, and all of their agents. The API exposes skills stored as Notion pages as downloadable directories of files, following the Agent Skills and Agent Plugins standards.

news.title: Set Default Agent Instructions for Your Entire Workspace
news.body: Notion now lets you set default agent instructions that apply across your entire workspace. The company describes the feature as house rules for your agents, so teams can define guidance once instead of repeating it for every individual agent.

news.title: Custom Agents Can Now Call Sub-Agents
news.body: Notion Custom Agents can now call sub-agents, each with its own instructions, context, access, and model. The primary agent can hand off focused work to other Custom Agents, then bring the results back together to finish the job.

news.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Now Available in Notion Agents
news.body: A new open-weight model just landed in Notion: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now available in Personal and Custom Agents, alongside the existing model choices.

news.title: Notion 3.7: Agent skills for your whole team
news.body: You know how some people are really good at prompting AI? Or they’ve figured out the best way to handle repetitive work? Now they can turn that know-how into a skill and level up the whole team. Skills are reusable instructions that teach AI how your team works. Like generating a monthly business review in your team’s format. Or critiquing your doc in the same way your boss would. They’re like team shortcuts for getting repetitive tasks done.

news.title: AI Meeting Notes Can Draft Email Recaps
news.body: Notion AI Meeting Notes can now draft an email recap with attendees from your calendar already filled in. Give it a once-over and send without leaving Notion.

news.title: Notion Desktop waits before background refreshes
news.body: Notion Desktop can now wait until you are done working before applying background updates to an active tab. Visible refreshes dropped from 30%+ to under 3% on the new version, which should mean fewer interruptions and less lost work while reading, typing, uploading, or recording meeting transcripts.

news.title: Session URL shorthand for Custom Agent session tools
news.body: Notion MCP's Custom Agent session tools now accept the shorthand session:// and thread:// for session_url, resolving both in the connected workspace. The full form session:/// that session tools return still works, and a full URL whose workspace ID differs from the connected workspace still returns HTTP 400 validation_error.

news.title: Validation and conflict errors from Custom Agent session tools
news.body: Notion MCP's Custom Agent session tools now return HTTP 400 validation_error for malformed URLs, URLs for a resource other than a session, or full URLs naming another workspace, and notion-send-message-to-session returns a conflict error when the session already has a run in progress. Both cases previously returned a generic failure. Valid URLs for missing, inaccessible, or unsupported sessions return HTTP 404 object_not_found. Wait for the run to finish with notion-wait-session before sending another message.

news.title: AI search accepts filters, and notion-search routes content queries to it
news.body: notion-ai-search now accepts the exact filters and sort options that notion-search accepts, and it accepts an empty query for filter-only browsing. These options return Notion-only workspace results so the constraints are enforced exactly, and the response still reports type: "ai_search". Omit them to search Notion and connected sources together. Filtering by editor, last-edited date, multiple teamspaces, title only, or content status, and sorting by date, still require Business or Enterprise. User lookup remains on notion-search with query_type: "user". Content searches sent to notion-search now run AI search when the connection can use it. When notion-fetch with the id self reports current_tool_access.ai_search.status as available, a keyword content query sent to notion-search searches Notion and connected sources and reports type: "ai_search", so clients that haven't adopted notion-ai-search keep getting unified results. A call that passes an exact filter, an empty query, or a sort other than relevance stays on Notion workspace search. Routing respects the connection's tool list: a connection that can't use notion-ai-search keeps its content searches on workspace search, and the

news.title: Control which AI models your agents can use
news.body: What’s on your team’s model roster? That’s up to you. With model controls, workspace owners can choose which AI models are available in Notion Agent and Custom Agents separately, and set a default model for Custom Agents. Keep costs predictable and support your compliance needs while your teams continue building.

news.title: Faster retries and plan-based rate limits
news.body: The per-connection rate limit is now enforced over a fixed 60-second window: 600 requests per minute on Business and Enterprise plans, and 180 requests per minute on all other plans. Retry-After for this limit never exceeds 60 seconds, down from up to 15 minutes, and per-connection 429 responses now also include the wait as additional_data.retry_after in the body. See Request limits.

news.title: Icon names and database icons
news.body: When setting a native icon, name now also accepts the icon picker name, so values like "token" and "star circle" can set the same Notion icon. databases.retrieve now returns the icon set in the Notion UI, matching the icon surfaced by dataSources.retrieve.

news.title: Search the trash and query archived pages
news.body: Search accepts a new filter.in_trash option to list trashed pages and data sources (databases on API versions before 2025-09-03). Query a data source accepts a top-level is_archived body parameter to return archived pages instead of the default non-archived set. SDK support: @notionhq/client v5.23.2 adds filter.in_trash support to client.search(). v5.23.1 exports rich text annotation types and fixes pagination helper type compatibility with endpoint methods under strictNullChecks.

news.title: Longer-lived Notion MCP access tokens
news.body: Notion MCP access tokens now last about eight hours, up from one hour. Clients must continue to rely on the token response's expires_in value, but the longer lifetime reduces refresh frequency and makes connections more resilient to client-side refresh failures.

news.title: Verify webhook signatures with one call
news.body: The new verifyWebhookSignature() helper confirms that a webhook event really came from Notion, so you no longer need to hand-write the HMAC check. Pass the raw request body, the X-Notion-Signature header, and your subscription's verification_token; the helper compares signatures in constant time and returns false instead of throwing on malformed input. It works without configuration in Node.js 18+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Functions, and browsers. A companion signWebhookPayload() generates signatures for testing your handler.

news.title: Read every row in a large data source
news.body: A single data source query returns at most 10,000 results, so plain pagination can silently miss rows. The new iterateAllDataSourceRows() and collectAllDataSourceRows() helpers page past the limit using the windowing approach from the Query large data sources guide, de-duplicating rows along the way. Stream rows with the iterator, or collect them into an array when the full result fits in memory.

news.title: Start and poll async page writes
news.body: notion.asyncTasks.retrieve({ task_id }) adds typed support for the Retrieve an async task endpoint, and the page create and markdown update methods now accept allow_async: true. Together they let you run large markdown writes asynchronously: start the write without holding a request open, then poll until the task succeeds or fails.

news.title: Reliability and fixes
news.body: The client now automatically retries service_overload (HTTP 529) responses, respecting the Retry-After header as described in Request limits. Thanks to @RyanBillard for contributing this. The relevance sort in search parameters now has the correct type, { property: "relevance" }. Pagination parameters accept start_cursor: null, so you can pass a response's next_cursor straight through without a null check.

news.title: HTML blocks via the API
news.body: You can now create HTML blocks with the API. Upload an .html file with the File Upload API and attach it to an embed block via embed.file_upload when appending block children, creating a page, or updating a block. The Notion app renders the file's contents interactively in a sandboxed iframe — the same HTML block the app creates with the /html command and that agents create through Notion MCP.

news.title: Choose an expiration when creating a personal access token
news.body: When creating a personal access token in the Developer portal, you can now pick an Expiration of 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, 180 days, or 1 year. The default stays at 1 year, matching the previous behavior. The create dialog previews the exact expiration date, and the reveal step shows the same date next to the token value. The workspace admin view under Settings & members → Connections now also surfaces an Expired status and filter for PATs whose expiration has passed. Expired tokens stop authenticating and return an unauthorized error, and can still be revoked from the admin view or the Developer portal.

news.title: Notion MCP splits keyword search and AI search
news.body: notion-search is now keyword-only. It matches short, specific terms in Notion and no longer searches connected apps like Slack, Google Drive, and Jira. Use it for content search only when notion-fetch with the id self reports that current_tool_access.ai_search.status is not available. It remains the tool for user lookup by name or email. Semantic search moved to a new notion-ai-search tool. Use it for every content search when current_tool_access.ai_search.status is available, including searches that include specific terms. It takes one concise natural-language query and searches sources connected to the workspace, such as Slack, Mail, and Calendar, when they are available to the caller. Using it requires Notion AI; without it, calls return a prompt with a recovery link, and notion-fetch with the id self reports ai_search in current_tool_access so clients can route to notion-search. notion-ai-search does not accept the exact filters, the sort options, or the user lookup that notion-search accepts. Clients that still send the old content_search_mode parameter on notion-search keep working: workspace_search behaves like notion-search, and ai_search behaves like notion-ai-search. The

news.title: JavaScript SDK 5.24.0
news.body: We released @notionhq/client v5.24.0. It adds client.blocks.meetingNotes.create() for creating a meeting note, typed unsupported formula and rollup values, and APIErrorCode.InvalidBeta for handling invalid_beta responses.

news.title: Notion MCP supports MCP protocol version 2026-07-28
news.body: The Notion MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp now supports MCP protocol version 2026-07-28. Existing MCP clients that negotiate the earlier 2025-era protocol on the same endpoint continue to work unchanged, so no client updates are required.

news.title: Clearer per-tool access status
news.body: The current_tool_access status previously called limited_free_trial is now available_with_limit. The new name makes clear that a tool is available until the usage limit included with the workspace's plan is reached. This is a naming and description update only; it does not change tool availability or usage limits.

news.title: Fetch documentation resources with the fetch tool
news.body: The Notion MCP fetch tool now accepts notion://docs/* URIs (for example, notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec) and returns the same content as the MCP resource of the same URI. This gives MCP clients that cannot read MCP resources a way to load the specs referenced in tool descriptions.

news.title: Per-tool access map in notion-fetch self
news.body: The notion-fetch MCP tool's self response now includes a current_tool_access map, so clients can tell before making a call which tools will actually run on the connected workspace's plan and which would only return an upgrade prompt. Each entry's status is available, limited_free_trial (calls succeed via a free or metered trial allowance), upgrade_required (the entry also carries an upgrade_url into the workspace's upgrade flow), or not_enabled. See Integrating your own MCP client.

news.title: New identity fields in OAuth token responses
news.body: User objects now include an email_verified boolean next to person.email, indicating whether Notion has verified that email address. The field appears anywhere person emails do, including the owner in OAuth token responses and List all users results. Notion MCP token responses now include top-level user_id, workspace_id, and email_domain fields on successful authorization-code exchanges, so MCP clients can associate a connection with a Notion user and workspace without an extra call. See Integrating your own MCP client. New response fields like these are backwards-compatible additions and appear on every API version. Parse responses leniently: ignore fields you don't recognize rather than rejecting them.

news.title: Notion app links in API responses use the new app domain
news.body: As part of Notion's move from notion.so to notion.com, the links Notion generates for its own records changed in early June 2026: the url values returned for pages, databases, and data sources, and the href values for page and database mentions, now point at the Notion app domain with a page path prefix, https://app.notion.com/p/{page-id}, instead of https://www.notion.so/{page-id}. Existing notion.so links continue to open correctly. These values are links for people to open in Notion, not stable identifiers: their domain and path format may change again. To reference a record, use its id field rather than parsing the URL, and use a page's public_url to link to its published site. Links authored by users, such as link.url in rich text and URL property values, and links to sites published on notion.site or custom domains are unchanged.

news.title: JS SDK updates
news.body: @notionhq/client v5.25.1 fixes the isFullDataSource and isFullDatabase type guards, which previously accepted partial responses and narrowed them to the full type. Both now require the title field, the same structural check the other full-object guards use. isFullPageOrDataSource picks up the fix. v5.25.2 adds the does_not_equal condition to verification property filters in data source and database query request types, alongside the existing status condition.

news.title: prop() references in formula property writes
news.body: Formula expressions submitted through Update a data source now store prop("Property Name") references exactly as written. Previously, the API accepted some expressions but silently rewrote them — most visibly, a reference to a unique ID property dropped the ID's prefix from computed values, and a prop() reference inside an array literal emptied the array. Expressions the API can't store now return a validation_error instead. Formulas saved before this fix keep their old stored expression until you resubmit the update. Formula properties created through the API also now keep their result type, so number formatting options stay available in Notion and other formulas can reference them with prop().

news.title: Readable formula expressions in data source schemas
news.body: Retrieve a data source now returns formula expressions using the same prop("Property Name") syntax you write. Expressions that can't be rendered faithfully in this syntax continue to use the internal property reference syntax.

news.title: Admin API reference for agents
news.body: The Admin API reference now covers the endpoints for managing agents in a workspace: credit usage and limits, permissions, status, creation policy, and workflow metadata.

news.title: Filter properties on page writes
news.body: Create a page and Update page properties now accept the same filter_properties query parameter as Retrieve a page. Pass the IDs of the properties you want, and the write response includes only those properties. This keeps responses small and fast for pages with many properties. SDK support: @notionhq/client v5.25.0 adds filter_properties to pages.create() and pages.update().

news.title: Reorganizing query tools in Notion MCP
news.body: Use notion-query-data-sources for both SQL queries and saved database views. To query a saved view, set mode to "view" and pass the same view_url. Existing notion-query-database-view calls continue to work and now include migration guidance. We plan to remove this older tool in a follow-up change.

news.title: Truncation metadata on notion-fetch
news.body: The notion-fetch MCP tool response now includes truncated, unknown_block_ids, and unknown_block_count when a page is large enough that some subtrees could not be loaded. unknown_block_ids lists up to 50 omitted subtree root IDs, and unknown_block_count reports the total number of omitted subtree roots. Pass a returned ID back to notion-fetch to retrieve that subtree directly; treat an object_not_found error on retry as a signal that the caller does not have access to the subtree.

news.title: unsupported formula and rollup property values
news.body: The API can now return formula and rollup page property values and property item values with type set to "unsupported" and an empty unsupported object. This happens when a value depends on too many related pages or nested formulas and rollups. The response doesn't include a partial value. Treat the property as unavailable. Rollups still include the function field. To make the value available, reduce the number of related pages or simplify the nested formulas and rollups.

news.title: Fetch saved database views in Notion MCP
news.body: Notion MCP's notion-fetch now accepts view:// URLs to read saved view settings. Tool response text now names fetch instead of view, without changing page content.

news.title: Custom Agent session tools in Notion MCP
news.body: Notion MCP now supports finding and working with Custom Agent sessions. The new tools can query or search sessions, start a session, send a follow-up message, check or wait for its status, stop a run, and list or read session events. See Supported tools for the full tool list and examples.

news.title: Atomic batched content updates in Notion MCP
news.body: notion-update-page calls that use the update_content command now apply every content-changing replacement in the batch or none of them. Previously, when one old_str matched no page content and another one in the same call did, the matching replacements were saved and the call returned success — so a batch that removed content in one operation and reinserted it in another could drop that content. These calls now return a validation_error naming the old_str that wasn't found, and the page is left unchanged. Operations whose old_str and new_str are identical are ignored without checking for a match. See Supported tools for the tool's matching rules. old_str must also be a non-empty string. Empty values were previously ignored, which silently skipped the replacement; they now fail validation on both notion-update-page and Update a page's content as markdown.

news.title: Admin API reference for users and permission groups
news.body: The Admin API reference now covers listing workspace users and managing workspace permission groups and direct memberships. These endpoints require the new user:read, permission-group:read, and permission-group:write scopes and are available to eligible Enterprise organizations.

news.title: Notion Agent APIs in public beta
news.body: The Notion Agent APIs are now in public beta. Use sessions to start a chat with a Custom Agent, stream its reply, submit an action, and page through a session's event history, so you can bring Custom Agents into a Slack bot, an internal tool, or a mobile client. The quickstart walks through a first request end to end with a personal access token. The beta also covers managing Custom Agents programmatically: find the agents a token can reach with Query agents, read per-agent usage with Retrieve agent insights, and set credit limits, enable, disable, or delete agents — individually or in an asynchronous batch. If you built against the private alpha routes for agents, threads, messages, or chat, see Upgrading to public beta. The replacements take JSON request bodies instead of query parameters and return sessions and events instead of threads and messages. Migrate off the alpha routes by September 30, 2026.

news.title: More filters in Notion MCP view tools
news.body: The notion-create-view and notion-update-view tools now apply relation, person, status, created by, last edited by, unique ID, last visited, verification, and place filters. Previously, some calls succeeded but saved a view without the requested filter. Use a page URL or ID for relation filters and a user ID or "me" for person filters. Invalid values now return an error. See Supported tools for accepted values, and read the notion://docs/view-dsl-spec resource for the full configuration syntax. Verification filters now round-trip through view responses for both matching (status) and non-matching (does_not_equal) conditions. Data source queries accept the same conditions.

news.title: Updating the query tool list in Notion MCP
news.body: New tool-list responses no longer include notion-query-database-view. Use notion-query-data-sources with mode: "view" for saved views. Clients with a cached tool list can still call notion-query-database-view; those calls continue to work and return migration guidance. The current_tool_access map returned by notion-fetch with the id self no longer has a query_database_view entry, since the map describes the tools that a current tool list advertises. See Supported tools for the tool list.

news.title: Multi-source SQL on Business plans in Notion MCP
news.body: notion-query-data-sources SQL queries that span multiple data sources now work on Business plans with Notion AI, which previously required an Enterprise plan. SQL is unlimited on Business and Enterprise plans with Notion AI; other plans keep the metered single-data-source allowance, and saved-view mode stays free on every plan.

news.title: Page covers and icons in notion-fetch responses
news.body: The notion-fetch MCP tool now returns cover and icon metadata for pages and database items. Both use the same shapes as the REST API, so clients can inspect the current cover or icon before deciding whether to replace it.

news.title: Rich text in data source queries
news.body: The notion-query-data-sources MCP tool now supports mode: "rows" to keep rich text in data source results. This mode preserves mentions and link targets that SQL output can omit.

news.title: Typed databases in the REST API
news.body: Create a database now accepts an optional database_type of tasks, projects, or skills. Notion builds the database from its canonical schema and metadata for that type, so the result matches a database of that type created in the Notion app. database_type can't be combined with initial_data_source, and when title is omitted the database is named after its type. See Typed databases for the properties each type creates. Database and data source objects now include a read-only database_type field.

news.title: Free workspace block limits now apply to the REST API
news.body: Starting today, the REST API enforces the existing Free workspace block limit for internal connections and OAuth connections restricted to selected workspaces. This is not a new workspace limit. See Workspace block limits for the grace period, HTTP 403 response, and background template behavior.

news.title: Upgrade prompts for Custom Agent tools in Notion MCP
news.body: Notion MCP's Custom Agent tools — notion-list-agents, notion-search-agents, and the session tools — now return a prompt with a recovery link when the workspace doesn't have access to Notion AI and Custom Agents. They previously returned a generic permission error with no recovery link. notion-fetch with the id self also reports these tools as upgrade_required with an upgrade_url, or as plan_required with a landing_page_url and landing_page_action when Notion routes the user through a plan landing page. Clients can use this status to route around unavailable tools before calling. Workspaces with a billing restriction, such as an unpaid invoice, are treated separately: the tools return a permission error that asks a workspace owner to manage billing, and current_tool_access reports them as not_enabled rather than upgrade_required. A connection that lacks the "View threads and interact with agents" capability does not advertise these tools and must reconnect or re-authorize.

news.title: Capture ideas and draft content in Notion
news.body: Your agent can now capture ideas and draft content in Notion without choosing where the page belongs first. The page starts as a private draft, so you can review it and organize it later.

news.title: Save and reuse your preferred workflows with Notion Skills
news.body: When you ask your AI to save a workflow you want to reuse, it can now create a Notion Skill or turn an existing page into one. Skills are reusable instructions stored as Notion pages that you own and can edit. When you ask for that workflow later, your AI can find the right Skill and read its instructions before starting.

news.title: Find the right page more easily
news.body: Your AI can now narrow Notion searches by where a page lives, who created or edited it, when it changed, whether the title matches, and the page's status. It can also sort results and look through up to 50 matches. Search results now show more context, including where a page lives and whether Notion has verified it. This helps your AI choose between similar or conflicting pages before reading the full content. Every plan includes filters for creator, creation date, and a single page, data source, or teamspace. On Business and Enterprise plans, your AI can also filter by editor, last-edited date, multiple teamspaces, title, or content status, and sort by date.

news.body: Notion is now available in Spanish and Portuguese (beta)

news.body: Meet the new Notion Projects — with AI

news.title: Notion 2.35: Introducing Q&A by Notion AI (now in beta)
news.body: Q&A by Notion AI, gives you answers instantly by understanding all the information in your workspace.

news.body: Notion 2.33: Automate workflows in databases

news.body: Notion 2.48: Set up Notion in one click, Calendar updates, and more.

news.body: Notion 2.43: Suggested edits are here + new Notion AI features

news.title: Notion Calendar is now on Android
news.body: Product improvements, updates, and fixes.

news.title: Upcoming changes coming to our Plus plan
news.body: Product improvements, updates, and fixes.

news.title: Notion 2.40: Home with calendar, navigate content, and organize your sidebar
news.body: Find your most important notes, events, and to-dos. We also added features to help you navigate long content and organize your sidebar.

news.title: Agent can build forms
news.body: Collect requests, get feedback, send surveys, & more—no manual form building required.

news.title: Gemini 3 Pro is live
news.body: Your Notion Agent now has access to Google's latest model, alongside those from OpenAI and Anthropic. Pick your preferred model for each task, knowing your Notion Agent gets stronger with every model release.

news.title: Notion 3.1
news.body: Notion 3.1: Lots of Agent updates, new Meetings tab, more AI Connectors, and map view!

news.title: Page discussions in one place
news.body: It’s now easier to catch up on the latest comments when collaborating with your team. This simplified view of page discussions lets you navigate to recent comments, identify what's new, and mark comments to return to later.

news.title: Agent now reads CSVs
news.body: Notion Agent can now read CSVs to find insights in seconds. Drop in any CSV (up to 1,000 rows) and ask your Agent to create an analysis or visualize your data as a chart or board. Perfect for expenses, customer lists, or project trackers.

news.title: Notion 3.0: Agents
news.body: Notion 3.0 is here! We’ve rebuilt Notion AI from the ground up as Agents. Now, anything you can do in Notion, your Agent can do for you. Let your Agent handle the busywork, so you can focus on your life’s work.

news.title: Notion 2.53: Offline mode
news.body: We’re excited to finally say it: you can access pages, capture ideas, and keep work moving on the Notion desktop and mobile app offline.

news.title: Notion in Indonesian, Thai, and Vietnamese
news.body: Notion is now available in Indonesian, Thai, and Vietnamese.

news.title: Ask your agent to suggest edits
news.body: Your agents can now propose changes instead of making them directly. Ask your agent to suggest edits, then move top to bottom to approve each one. It’s great when you need line-level changes, like a pass for grammar.

news.title: Your Developer Portal, now in the sidebar
news.body: Manage your Workers, connections, and personal access tokens from the new Developer section of your Notion workspace. See an overview of deployed Workers and logs behind every run. Plus, the new developer bar makes it easy for anyone building with the API to find IDs for the page, database, block, workspace, or user. Copy any one of them, or the full API object, in one click.

news.title: Model selection, simplified
news.body: The model picker now leads with a shortlist of models made for your hardest tasks, and every model has a scorecard to compare speed, intelligence, and cost. Pin your favorites for easy access and dial up the effort when you need a more thorough answer.

news.title: Share context with Custom Agents from the Share menu
news.body: See a doc or database your agent would find useful? Now you can share it directly from the Share menu. No need to click over to the agent’s settings.

news.title: AI Meeting Notes can now trigger Custom Agents
news.body: Custom Agents can now run right after an AI Meeting Note is finished. No more need to manually update status trackers, post recaps to the project channel, or file tickets by hand.

news.title: Workers, now in your Notion credits dashboard
news.body: Now you can track your Workers’ usage in the credits dashboard, alongside your other spend.

news.title: New calendar tools for your agent
news.body: Your agent just got new calendar tools to show and manage your schedule. Join calls, send invites, and find times that work for everyone— all from the chat.

news.title: Share Notion Workers across your team
news.body: Build and iterate on Workers with your team. Or share one so teammates can connect it to their own Custom Agents.

news.title: Meet the Notion Agents iOS app
news.body: Find answers quickly from across your workspace or connected tools, capture ideas wherever they happen, or hand off tasks for your agents to finish by the time you get back to your desk.

news.title: Notion 3.6: External Agents, HTML blocks, and more
news.body: Your agents shouldn’t be stuck in one-off chats. Now you can bring multiple agents into a single UI with the rest of your team, so you can automate entire workflows end-to-end.

news.title: Merge cells in simple tables
news.body: Finally! Merge cells in simple tables.

news.title: 3.5: Notion Developer Platform
news.body: Now you (and your coding agents) can write code to sync any data and build any agent tool, all running on our infrastructure. You can also bring your favorite agents into Notion (like Claude, Codex, Decagon, or ones you’ve built yourself). It turns Notion into one shared canvas with all your data, for your team and agents to work together.

news.title: Plan Mode
news.body: When you ask your agent to make significant changes like rewriting pages or updating databases in bulk, results can drift off course if your intent is unclear. Plan Mode introduces a preliminary step where your agent asks clarifying questions and builds a detailed plan before acting. The result is fewer surprises and more confidence in complex, multi-step work.

news.title: New Custom Agent Directory
news.body: Custom Agents now have a dedicated place in your Library. Use the Custom Agent Directory to browse all your workspace’s agents, pin your favorites, and create new ones to automate your team's busywork 24/7.

news.title: New Custom Agent controls for admins
news.body: Two months ago, we launched Custom Agents in beta. Since then, teams have created more than a million of them and honestly pushed them further than we expected! One theme from admins was consistent: as Custom Agents scaled, so did the need for more control and visibility. Your feedback shaped what we built next, so here’s what's new.

news.title: A new home on mobile
news.body: Navigating Notion on mobile just got easier with the new home tab. Now your home, chats, meetings, and inbox are just one swipe away.

news.title: Add Custom Agents to private Slack channels
news.body: Custom Agents can now read and reply in private Slack channels.

news.title: Rollups now as currency, percent, and more
news.body: Rollups now support number formatting (USD, EUR, percent, etc.) and decimal places. Show budget totals, conversion rates, and more in your rollups without any formula workarounds.

news.title: Find pages faster from the breadcrumb
news.body: Hover over any item in the breadcrumb to see sibling pages, including pages inside databases. This makes it easier to find related pages and navigate your workspace.

news.title: Mail & Calendar, now in your settings
news.body: Connect your calendar and inbox from a new dedicated tab in your settings.

news.title: Schedule meetings with Notion Agent
news.body: Notion Agent now shows your calendar to help you find available time with teammates. See a ranked list of choices, compare schedules, and book. All without leaving the chat.

news.title: Notion 3.4, part 2
news.body: We launched Custom Agents a few weeks ago, and teams are building faster than we can keep up with. In Notion 3.4, your agents can take on even more of your day-to-day busywork.

news.title: Customize your tabs in databases
news.body: Keep your databases clean and easy to navigate by choosing how your tabs are displayed: Text and icon, Icon only, or Text only.

news.title: New page cover art from timeless collections
news.body: Choose page cover art from four new collections, sourced from museums and public archives.

news.title: Mute discussion replies
news.body: Keep your notifications clean by muting replies to discussions you no longer find relevant.

news.title: Share Notion AI chats as a link
news.body: You can now share your Notion AI chats as a read-only link.

news.title: Voice input on desktop
news.body: Voice input for Notion AI is now on desktop. Whether you are dictating a longer prompt, or just prefer talking over typing, voice input makes it easier to get things done with your Agent.

news.title: Keep pages tidy with tabs
news.body: Tabs let you split a page into clean sections so you can keep related content together without a long vertical scroll.

news.title: Archive outdated pages to keep your workspace fresh
news.body: Archive lets you mark pages as outdated to keep your workspace clean and improve your search results.

news.title: Notion 3.4, part 1
news.body: This month, we have a champagne problem: our engineers are shipping faster than ever, which means Notion 3.4 has too much to cover in a single email. So let’s start with the fundamentals, like a new dashboard view for your databases, a completely redesigned sidebar (opt-in to try it out!), presentation mode that turns any doc into a slideshow, and a lot more.

news.title: Custom skills for Notion AI
news.body: Custom skills let you turn any repetitive AI task into an easily accessible command.

news.title: Notion Academy & certifications, in 6 new languages
news.body: Notion Academy videos and certification programs are now live in 6 new languages— Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, French, and German.

news.title: Custom instructions for AI Meeting Notes
news.body: Custom instructions let you define exactly how AI Meeting Notes makes your summaries so they are as useful as possible after a meeting ends.

news.title: New consent controls for AI Meeting Notes
news.body: Workspace owners can now set a workspace-wide policy for AI Meeting Notes audio consent.

news.title: Search Salesforce accounts, leads, opportunities, and contacts in Notion
news.body: Notion AI can now search your Salesforce data (accounts, leads, opportunities, and contacts) right alongside everything else in your workspace.

news.title: Visualize progress with dashboard views
news.body: Dashboard views are a new database view for better visibility and context. This lets teams (and agents) easily assemble beautiful, glanceable overviews directly on top of their databases.

news.title: Generate images with Notion AI
news.body: Notion AI can now generate and edit images right on your page.

news.title: GPT-5.4 is now in Notion
news.body: GPT-5.4 is now available in Notion’s model picker.

news.title: New “can create pages” database permission
news.body: The new “can create pages” database permission lets users create new pages in a database, while still being restricted from viewing or editing other contents they should not have access to.

news.title: Run Custom Agents for less with MiniMax M2.5
news.body: Custom Agents now support MiniMax M2.5, an open weight model that’s up to 10x more cost-efficient for basic tasks.

news.title: Present any Notion page
news.body: Turn any Notion page into a fullscreen presentation.

news.title: Notion 3.3: Custom Agents
news.body: Big news today: Custom Agents are finally here! Give them a job, set a trigger or schedule, and they’ll get it done—24/7. They’re designed for teams and work across Notion, Slack, Mail, Calendar, and more. The work that used to require constant coordination now runs on its own.

news.title: A home for everything in Library
