news.title: Claude Opus 4.6, now in Notion
news.body: Claude Opus 4.6 is the strongest model Anthropic has shipped. For Notion users, it feels less like a tool and more like a capable collaborator.

news.title: Search your Asana tasks and projects from Notion
news.body: Your Notion Agent can now find Asana projects and tasks in seconds.

news.title: Notion 3.2: Mobile AI, new models, people directory
news.body: First round of 2026 updates is in! This release helps Notion fit into your world even better. Work on the go, choose your AI models, track what matters to your team.

news.title: Custom Agents API in Public Beta
news.body: The Custom Agents API is in public beta, with a Notion Agent SDK for reaching Custom Agents from outside Notion. You can hold a conversation with one and read back previous chats, or trigger an agent from another app or workflow.

news.title: Share Pages with Your Custom Agents
news.body: A small quality-of-life improvement in Notion: you can now share pages with your Custom Agents straight from the Share menu, making it easier to give them all the context they need.

news.title: Custom Blocks Early Alpha for Developers
news.body: Notion is opening up an early alpha for custom blocks, a new Notion primitive for building interactive blocks that can read your workspaces and databases. Very early, very experimental, and the team wants to learn from what developers build with it.

news.title: High Contrast Mode
news.body: Notion's muted design can make content hard to read, so a new high contrast mode is here for anyone who needs more contrast. Text, icons, and borders are much easier to see.

news.title: Claude Opus 5 in Notion
news.body: A new model today: Claude Opus 5 is now available in Notion.

news.title: Notion as Code (Beta)
news.body: Now in beta: Notion as code. Define an entire workspace in TypeScript, teamspaces, databases, custom agents, all of it, then deploy it through the API. Build workspaces with coding agents, version-control your setup in git, and reproduce the same setup anywhere you need it.

news.title: Open and Import Markdown Files
news.body: .md, meet Notion. You can now open Markdown files in Notion as a read-only preview, then import them as Notion pages, so notes and docs written in Markdown drop straight into your workspace.

news.title: Notion Agent Manages Your Inbox
news.body: It's a bad day to be a notification. Notion Agent can now manage your Inbox: from chat, it catches you up on what's important, then marks notifications read or archives them in bulk.

news.title: Notion Agents iOS App
news.body: Meet the Notion Agents iOS app — a team of agents in your pocket. Send a voice note, a photo of a napkin sketch, or a question at 11pm, and it's handled before you're back at your desk.

news.title: Notion 3.6
news.body: Notion 3.6 is here — more ways to work with agents, clearer meeting notes, HTML blocks, better file support, and a handful of fixes to make everyday work feel smoother.

news.title: Agent Now Uses Outlook
news.body: Your Notion personal agent can now use Outlook — view, manage, and schedule events in calendar, and search, triage, and respond to emails in mail.

news.title: HTML Block
news.body: Notion added a new HTML block — build interactive HTML right on your page. Ask AI to turn your content into interactive explainers, prototypes, diagrams, dashboards, or even a playable arcade, then share with your team to use and tinker together.

news.title: Winding Down Notion Mail
news.body: Notion is winding down the Notion Mail inbox across web, desktop, and iOS on September 22, going all in on agents to run your inbox — more than half of Notion Mail users already manage email without ever opening their inbox.

news.title: External Agents: Claude + Cursor
news.body: Introducing External Agents in Notion — your favorite agents collaborate like teammates. Assign Claude and Cursor tasks from a board shared with your whole team, @-mention them, and watch them run.

news.title: Claude Fable 5 in Notion
news.body: Claude Fable 5 is now in Notion — the model to put behind your most complex custom agents and workers, setting new highs on Notion internal benchmarks for the hardest multi-step work. Available on Business and Enterprise plans.

news.title: Grok 4.3 + Grok Build 0.1
news.body: Grok 4.3 and Grok Build 0.1 are now available for Notion Agent and Custom Agents.

news.title: Migration to app.notion.com
news.body: Notion has finished migrating from notion.so to app.notion.com — same workspace, new home.

news.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash for Custom Agents
news.body: Gemini 3.5 Flash is now available for Custom Agents in Notion.

news.title: Outlook + Notion Agents
news.body: Connect Outlook Mail to Notion Agents (alpha) — find threads, draft replies, send, sort, and archive.

news.title: Claude Opus 4.8 in Notion
news.body: Claude Opus 4.8 is now available in Notion.

news.title: Snapshot Diffs in Version History
news.body: Version History now shows exactly what changed — text, images, tables, database properties — without playing spot-the-difference. Snapshot Diffs are live.

news.title: Custom Agent Insights
news.body: No more guessing what your agents are up to. Custom Agent Insights makes every run fully visible — change a prompt or model and see if your agent got cheaper or smarter run by run, hunt down expensive runs and the patterns behind them, and pinpoint where a run broke (a tool call, a missing connection) so you can fix the root cause.

news.title: Notion Now in Italian
news.body: Ciao! Notion is now available in Italian. Finalmente!

news.title: Notion Developer Platform
news.body:
Introducing the Notion Developer Platform — new building blocks to sync any data source, build any tool, and orchestrate any agent:
• Notion CLI (ntn) — Notion in your terminal
• Workers — run code on Notion's infra
• Database sync — pipe any data source into Notion
• Agent tools — build any workflow
• Webhook triggers — trigger Notion from any app
• External Agents API — bring any agent into Notion
• Notion Agents SDK — use Notion Agents anywhere
…plus a bunch of API improvements. Soon you won't need to be a developer to build on Notion — your agent will be one for you.

news.title: Markdown API
news.body: The #1 requested dev feature is shipped: Markdown API. Plus a recap of the last year of API/MCP improvements — Database views API, Personal Access Tokens, 91% more token-efficient Notion MCP, root page creation, database locks for read-only, database templates, AI Meeting Notes API, OAuth scoped to your workspace, and the new Developer Portal.

news.title: Grok Now an MCP Integration in Notion
news.body: Notion added Grok as an MCP integration — your timeline and your workspace in the same chat.

news.title: Speaker Identification in AI Meeting Notes
news.body: Notion AI Meeting Notes can now identify who's speaking in 1:1s and video calls.

news.title: Notion AI Mobile Widgets (TestFlight)
news.body: New Notion AI mobile widgets designed by Andrew Ashen — available in TestFlight beta now.

news.title: Notion Agent Manages Your Email
news.body: Your Notion Agent can now manage your email! Ask it to search your inbox, draft a reply, or unsubscribe from lists you keep meaning to leave. It puts in the hours, you get your afternoon back.

news.title: Custom Agents in Slack Channels
news.body: Notion now lets you add Custom Agents to private Slack channels — invite them like any teammate, and they only see the channels you bring them into.

news.title: Mobile Homepage Refresh
news.body: Notion refreshed its mobile homepage — home, AI chats, meeting notes, and inbox are all one swipe away.

news.title: Notes Sharing to Slack 2.0
news.body: Notion AI rolled out Notes Sharing to Slack 2.0 — push AI meeting notes into Slack in two clicks with auto-formatted summaries.

news.title: Agent Instructions & Skills
news.body: Today's lecture in the Custom Agent series — learn how to turn your repeated prompts into reusable skills, get consistent outputs, and make your Notion Agent feel tailored to you.

news.title: Rollup Number Formatting
news.body: Rollups now support number formatting (USD, EUR, percent, etc.) and decimal places. No more formatting via formulas — your budget rollups finally look like money.

news.title: Class Is in Session
news.body:
Learn how to build your first Custom Agent, write clear instructions, and connect the right tools and triggers so it can handle repetitive work for you and your team.

Tomorrow's lesson? Agent Instructions and Skills!

news.title: GPT-5.5 in Notion
news.body: GPT-5.5 is now in Notion.

news.title: Breadcrumb Browser
news.body: Breadcrumbs now show sibling pages when you hover. Easier to explore related pages and navigate your workspace.

news.title: Autofill Agents (Renamed)
news.body: Database agents are back to being called Autofill. Basic for quick one-pass fills (Biz + Ent plans), Custom Agent for bigger stuff with workspace + web search and multi-step reasoning.

news.title: Custom Agent Directory
news.body: Your Library just got a new wing. The Custom Agent Directory is a full-page gallery for your and your workspace's custom agents. Browse, search, and manage them in one place. Go to Library → Agents tab.

news.title: Kimi K2.6 Now in Notion
news.body: Kimi K2.6 is now in Notion. The first open-weight model that plays like other top-tier models. Strong at tool use and carrying out tasks no matter how meticulous or ambiguous.

news.title: Image Gen is Here
news.body: If you can make a page, you can make a graphic for it too. Just hit /image and Notion handles the rest.

news.title: Mail & Calendar in One Tab
news.body: Mail and calendar connections now live in a single Settings tab. Once connected, Notion AI can schedule meetings and draft emails on your behalf across accounts.

news.title: Fresh Cover Art + AI Agent Permissions
news.body: New cover art from Texturelabs, Hudson River School, National Museum of Asian Art, and USDA Pomological Watercolors. Plus: add, remove, and edit page permissions for custom agents in the Notion AI app.

news.title: Opus 4.7 Now in Notion
news.body: Opus 4.7, Anthropic's most intelligent model, is now in Notion. A real step up for multi-step workflows — fewer tokens, about 3x fewer tool errors.

news.title: Notion AI Agent Connects to Your Calendar
news.body: Notion connected its AI Agent to your calendar — it can now find meeting times, create and update events, and display a real grid view right in chat.

news.title: Meet Canto, our first speech model
news.body: Flow now runs on Canto, the first speech model we've built ourselves. It's now rolled out for everyone, with nothing to switch on. Most speech models are trained and tested on clean audio recorded in quiet rooms with good microphones. That isn't where people use Flow. You're on a train, in an open office, walking between meetings, or talking quietly so you don't disturb anyone. Canto was built and measured against those conditions instead. On our evaluation of real-world English Flow recordings, 9.8 hours from more than 2,300 speakers, Canto had the lowest word error rate of every model we tested, including models from Google, OpenAI, AssemblyAI and Deepgram. On a separate set built to stress-test the hardest audio, with background conversation, music, traffic, wind and whispered speech, Canto was the most accurate of the real-time models we tested. We're already training its successor at more than ten times the scale, with better recognition in difficult conditions and broader language coverage ahead. Read the full research post here. ‍

It uses your personal dictionary to help capture names, acronyms, and technical terms correctly so you can: Catch up during a call: Ask “What did I miss?” for a recap of the discussion so far. Find answers across meetings: Ask “What follow-ups do I owe people from my calls this week?” or “Based on the calls I’ve led this month, how could I ask better questions?” Answers include citations back to the meetings. Draft from your notes: Turn conversations into follow-up emails, project updates, or briefs directly in Notetaker. Find it: Open the Notetaker tab in Wispr Flow. Connect your meetings to your other work Notetaker just added one-click setup for Gemini, alongside connections to Claude and ChatGPT. You can also connect to any other MCP-compatible AI tool. news.title: Wispr Flow Notetaker is here
news.body: Today we're launching Wispr Flow Notetaker, our first product beyond dictation. It records your meetings, gets your words, names, and speakers right, and turns the conversation into transcripts and summaries you can act on. No bot joins your call, and it works on every meeting platform. Where the accuracy comes from. Most notetakers hear a meeting cold. Notetaker walks in with context you've already built: The personal dictionary you've trained in Flow carries over, so your acronyms, product names, and industry terms come out spelled right. Speaker names come from the calendar invite, so "Biswaroop" doesn't become "Bishop" and the action item lands on the right person. You get a live transcript during the meeting. When it ends, Notetaker re-reads the entire recording with that context, which is where speaker names get attached and everything comes out sharper. Accuracy matters more now that meeting notes feed your other tools. Everything Notetaker produces is available over MCP to Claude, ChatGPT, or your own agents, and a wrong name in the transcript doesn't get caught downstream. It just travels. What it does: It works wherever your meetings happen: Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, even

news.title: Wispr Flow Raises a $280M Series B at a $2B Valuation
news.body: Wispr Flow raised $280 million in Series B funding at a $2 billion valuation, led by existing investor Menlo Ventures, taking total capital raised to $361 million. Alongside the round Wispr Flow previewed Canto, its first proprietary speech model, trained for the conditions people actually dictate in rather than quiet rooms — in the hardest settings, with background noise, wind, heavy accents or music, word error rates fall from more than 30% to between 5 and 10%, and across everyday use it should cut the dictations you need to edit by 30 to 35%.

news.title: Introducing Notetaker
news.body: It's no secret how Wispr Flow feels about typing, and they hate messy meeting notes too. Meet Notetaker, Wispr Flow's answer to cleaner meeting notes. Learn more at wisprflow.ai/notetaker.

title: Shopify
description: Build and run an online store — e-commerce platform with themes, payments, inventory, and AI tools for creators selling products.
features: AI product descriptions and image editing

news.title: Analyze purchase orders in Shopify Analytics
news.body: You can now review and export purchase order data in Shopify Analytics. Three new reports help you understand your purchase orders: Purchase order costs shows ordered items, quantities, supplier costs, estimated taxes, and purchase order costs. Purchase order transfers follows purchase orders through transfers, shipments, and receiving. Purchases on order shows open, ordered purchase orders that don't have linked transfers. The Purchase Orders page also shows purchase orders, on-order purchase orders, total items ordered, acceptance rate, and shipments due soon. Learn more about purchase order reports.

news.title: Pay suppliers internationally from Balance
news.body: We have released International Payments from Balance for the US. This gives merchants a more cost-effective way to pay their international suppliers, with transparent pricing and no extra setup. International payments from Balance will let eligible merchants pay recipients internationally from the Balance mobile app. Learn more about the International Payments from Balance in the Shopify Help Center.

news.title: Faster checkout, carts synced across devices via Shop
news.body: Shop can now verify who a shopper is while they're browsing your store, even before they make a purchase. For Shop users, this means checkout loads faster, carts sync across devices, sign-in is sped up with one-tap, and the Buy with Shop Pay button is pre-filled for a smoother, higher-converting checkout. Browsing activity also syncs to a shopper's Shop account, so Shop can resurface items they viewed and abandoned carts, helping you close the loop on conversions. What this means for you: * Faster checkout *- less friction, faster load times * *Carts follow shoppers - carts sync and stay up to date across a shopper's devices * Better-converting Shop Pay button - personalized to show the card a shopper last used * One-tap sign-in - for Shop users signing into their customer accounts * Built-in recovery - Shop reminds shoppers to finish carts they left behind * Two-way sync - carts started in the Shop app carry over to your storefront, and vice versa Now supported on all browsers. Learn more in the Shopify Help Center.

news.title: Admin now supports 3 new languages
news.body: We’ve released improved support for 3 right-to-left languages (Arabic, Urdu, and Hebrew) in both Admin and Storefronts, including checkout, customer accounts and the Horizon family of themes. Display language is determined based on the user’s device settings, if available. Product pages and other merchant-owned content will continue to be displayed in the languages that you have enabled. You can enable translations on your product details pages (PDPs) by using the Translate & Adapt app in the Shopify admin. Get started with right-to-left languages by adding them in your admin.

news.title: Schedule and test discounts with Rollouts
news.body: You can now include discounts in Rollouts to run coordinated campaigns and test different offers before launching more broadly. Schedule discount changes: Launch a new offer to a portion of online store traffic, then expand when you're ready. Compare offers: Test discount changes against your existing offers and review conversion results to help decide which offer to keep. Launch changes together: Schedule a discount to go live alongside your theme and checkout changes in a single rollout. Your discount’s existing customer eligibility rules still apply. You can also continue using discount start and end dates to schedule standalone promotions. Learn more about discounts scheduling and testing in our help documentation.

news.title: Design a fully bespoke store with Canvas
news.body: Canvas is a new design surface for your online store. Every page is laid out together in one interactive, infinite workspace, so you can see how your whole store feels and work on any part of it in context. In Canvas, you can: * Pan across every page of your store and zoom in on any detail * Click any element to edit it directly, or tell Sidekick what you want in the chat * See Sidekick's changes land in real time, from a single section to a store-wide redesign * Preview the real, working store, with interactions, animations, and different products, collections, and screen sizes * Canvas is rolling out to existing stores over the coming days. Go to Online Store > Themes to create a new theme in Canvas, or duplicate a Shopify theme or custom theme in Canvas. Your original theme stays in the current theme editor. At launch, Canvas doesn't support third-party themes from the Shopify Theme Store, Markets, rollouts, translations, or app blocks and app embeds. Themes edited in Canvas don't receive theme updates. Learn more about designing your store in Canvas in the Shopify Help Center.

news.title: Add your own notes to Shopify Analytics
news.body: Your reports show what changed. You know why. Now, you're able to capture that story directly in Shopify Analytics. Add annotations to supported time-series reports for the moments that shape your business, like a campaign launch, creator mention, supplier change, promotion, or operational improvement. Instead of leaving that context in memory, spreadsheets, or team threads, it stays beside the data where you expect to see shifts. When you return to a report weeks or months later, you and your team can quickly understand why performance changed without piecing the story back together. From the annotations panel, you can: - Add a title, description, date or date range, and annotation type - Use our auto-detected annotation categories or choose your own - Edit, delete, and see who created each annotation - Search and filter context from your team, installed apps, and Shopify Annotations are shared with staff who have Reports permission and appear alongside context from Shopify and installed apps. Together, they create one shared history of what changed, what your business did, and why it mattered. Learn more about annotations here.

news.title: Shop is now at shop.com
news.body: Shop's web experience has moved from shop.app to shop.com. Your store, products, and channel settings are unaffected — the change only affects the web address shoppers use to reach Shop. What's changing Shop's web experience now lives at shop.com instead of shop.app Existing shop.app links redirect automatically to shop.com What you need to do Nothing. Your store, products, and channel settings carry over exactly as they are. If you've linked to shop.app anywhere (social bios, ads, etc.), you can update those links to shop.com at your convenience, though the redirect will continue to work.

news.title: Return window overrides now available
news.body: You can now set return window overrides by market for specific collections, products, or variants. Overrides let you choose a different return period than your default return window - for example, 14 days for seasonal items instead of your standard 90 days. How it works * Overrides replace the default return window: If an item matches an override, that override's return window gets applied instead of your default or market-specific window. * The shortest override wins: If an item matches more than one override, the shortest matching return window applies. * Final sale still wins: Items marked as final sale can't be returned (or cancelled), even if they also match a return window override. * Default rules apply otherwise: If an item isn’t final sale and doesn’t match an override, your market-specific return window applies. If no market-specific rules are set, your default return window applies. Where to set it Settings > Policies > Return and cancellation rules > Select specific market rules to modify > You can then select a target collection, product, variant to apply a return window override to. Example Set a 14‑day window for your “Holiday 2026” collection while keeping your stor

news.title: Local delivery orders in Shopify POS
news.body: Staff can now create local delivery orders at checkout in Shopify POS. When a customer can't take an item home, you can arrange delivery in the same sale. You no longer need to ask them to reorder online or leave notes on the order. Local delivery uses the delivery zones and rates you already set up for your online store. When you add shipping to a cart and the customer's address is in one of your delivery zones, local delivery shows up with your other shipping rates. Select it, confirm the customer's phone number, add any delivery instructions, and check out. The delivery address and fee show in the cart, on the receipt, and on the customer-facing display. You can then prepare and fulfill the order in POS, the same way you handle local delivery orders from your online store. Things to know Staff permissions: Local delivery uses your existing POS permissions, with some updates to how they apply: * To create local delivery orders, staff need Create shipping and delivery orders (previously Ship to customer). * To fulfill local delivery orders, staff now need Fulfill shipping, pickup, and delivery orders (previously Fulfill shipping and pickup orders). Previously, staff could fulfill

news.title: Run stock counts in POS
news.body: Shopify POS now lets store staff run cycle and full stock counts directly in POS, making it easier to count inventory on the sales floor while keeping planning, review, and approval in Shopify Admin. In Shopify Admin, users with the required permissions can create and schedule a stock count, select the location where the count will take place, and choose the products to include. Once created, the count automatically appears under Products > Stock counts in POS at the selected location. In Shopify POS, staff with the inventory permission can open the count and record what’s on hand by scanning barcodes or entering quantities manually. When the count is complete, it is submitted for review in Shopify Admin. Submitting a stock count from POS doesn’t immediately update inventory quantities. Users with the required permissions can review the completed count and any discrepancies before approving it and applying the resulting inventory adjustments. Shopify also keeps a record of what was counted, when the count was completed, and who performed it, providing an audit trail for inventory adjustments . Running stock counts in Shopify POS requires POS Pro and Shopify POS v11.16 or later. Lea

news.title: Use metaobject fields in Analytics reports
news.body: If you attach a metaobject to a product, variant, customer, or order through a metafield, those fields can now be used in Analytics. A designer country, a warranty term, or a loyalty tier can group and filter a report the same way a custom metafield can. Merchant-owned metaobjects are already enabled. You can turn a definition off if you don't want it in reports. What you can do - Open a report and pick fields under Metaobjects, then the resource, the definition, and the field. For example, Designer, then Country. - Filter to a single value, like a designer in Italy. - Use the same fields in the query editor. - Turn a definition on or off in Settings > Metafields and metaobjects. Open the metaobject and use Filter or group data in Analytics. What stays the same - Your metaobjects, and the metafields that point to them, are unchanged. - Custom metafields and category metafields stay in the picker, in their own groups. - Metaobjects created by an app stay off until you or the app turn Analytics on for that definition.

news.title: Category metafields are now available in Analytics
news.body: Until now, the color, material, fit, and other attributes you set when you categorize a product stayed on the product page. To see which materials or colors actually sell, you had to export. Those category metafields now show up in Analytics as dimensions and filters, next to your custom metafields. If you already categorized products, there's nothing to turn on. The attributes your products use are there. What you can do - Group a sales report by Color, Material, Fit, Fabric, Size, Activity, or any other category metafield on your products. - Filter a report to a specific value, like organic cotton or a particular color. - Use them in Reports, Explore, and the query editor. What stays the same - How you categorize products hasn't changed. - Custom metafields still work the way they do today. - If a product has more than one value for an attribute, Analytics keeps those values together on one row so sales aren't counted twice.

news.title: Tax is now calculated on return shipping fees
news.body: Starting October 23, 2026, for merchants using Shopify Tax or Tax Platform in the United States, return shipping fees will be taxed like any other shipping charge. Shopify calculates and applies the tax automatically, so you don’t need to fix under-collection on returns. When you create a return, you’ll see the estimated tax. When you process the return, we record the final amount. These taxes flow into your tax reports automatically. This update applies to orders shipped to US addresses. Your existing shipping tax settings still apply — if you’ve set shipping to be untaxed in a state, return shipping fees in that state remain untaxed. *What you need to do: * - If you use a manual workaround today to calculate, collect, import, or reconcile tax on return shipping fees, review it before October 23 to avoid double-counting tax. - Otherwise, no action is required. Learn more

news.title: Filterable logs and health metrics for custom apps are now in the Developer Dashboard
news.body: The Developer Dashboard shows how your custom apps perform, not only how they are set up. Open any custom app to see its API request volume, error rates, webhook delivery health, and embedded admin page load speed. Each measurement has a clear threshold, so you can tell good from bad at a glance. A single filterable stream holds every API request, webhook delivery, and app event, so you can find the cause when an app stops working. A new home page shows what needs your attention across all of your apps. Agencies and developers who build your custom apps see the same data. Come see what's new: 1. Explore the new experience at dev.shopify.com/dashboard. 2. Read more in the docs.

news.title: Shop Pay Wallet Available in Muse
news.body: Shop Pay is now available as a wallet in Muse, enabling agentic checkout with Shop Pay.

media.alt: Shopify demonstration of Shop Pay checkout in Muse

news.title: Improved shipping and duty data in Analytics
news.body: We now provides a more complete and timely view of shipping costs and duties. What's changed: Profitability data includes both duties and other shipping costs when they apply to the same order & better supports orders in different currencies. What to expect: You might notice changes to shipping costs, duties, or profit values in custom or Shopify-created reports that use this data such as the "Average profit margin by market" & "Profit margin by order" reports.

news.title: Shop Pay Installments can now be enabled on multiple business entities
news.body: Shop Pay Installments, Shop Pay’s built-in buy now, pay later solution, is available for merchants and buyers located in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Merchants who operate multiple business entities in these supported countries can now enable Shop Pay Installments on all entities, not just the primary entity. Enable Shop Pay Installments for eligible entities from your Shopify Payments payment method settings. Learn more about Shop Pay Installments.

news.title: Plan launches, events, and tests with clearer and more granular controls in Rollouts
news.body: Rollouts has a redesigned setup experience that makes it easier to plan a launch, run a temporary event, or test changes to your store. Reflect your intent: Choose the timing and traffic percentage for your rollout. Rollout settings will adjust to reflect your intent as a launch, temporary event, or an experiment. Combine multiple changes: Make changes to your theme, checkout and customer account pages in a single rollout. Understand your audience: See what percentage of traffic your rollout reaches and how it’s split between test versions. Review conflicts: See conflicting settings directly in the setup flow so you can address them earlier. Learn more about the new Rollouts configuration in our help documentation.

news.title: Shopify Analytics session measurement improvements
news.body: Starting September 21, 2026, Shopify is improving the sessions experience in Analytics to give merchants a cleaner view of real shopper activity. As a result, sessions, conversion rate, and other session-based metrics might look different after this update. This doesn't necessarily mean that your traffic, orders, or customer behavior changed. This update gives you a cleaner session baseline by focusing the default sessions experience on human visitors where the Human or bot filter is available, classifying bot/system traffic more consistently, and keeping valid shopper journeys visible even when they don't include a standard pageview. Session-based metrics that might look different include: * Sessions * Conversion rate * Add-to-cart rate * Reached checkout rate * Checkout conversion rate * Bounce rate * Pageviews per session * Online store visitors * Searches Orders, sales, and customer counts aren't changed by this session measurement update. When you compare reports before and after September 21, 2026, treat this as a new baseline for session-based metrics. Learn more about Shopify Analytics session measurement improvements.

news.title: Payouts page redesign: see all your payouts in one view
news.body: Your payouts now appear in a list on the left with the selected payout's details beside it, so you can move between payouts without leaving the page or losing your place. What's new: * A date-led view of paid and pending payouts, so you can see at a glance what you've been paid and what's on the way. * Expandable breakdowns for the selected payout, so you can see what makes up the amount without navigating away. * Simpler traceability for payout failure Availability: The new look rolls out gradually to all merchants in the Shopify admin on web and mobile.

news.title: A new look for the Shopify admin
news.body: On September 15th, we began rolling out a new look for the Shopify admin: new color, type, spacing, and icons across every page, inside a new frame. Search, notifications, and the store picker have moved into the side navigation, which collapses for more room on the page. Sidekick has moved from a side panel to a floating chat at the bottom of every page, so it’s in reach from wherever merchants are working. The new look rolls out gradually and will arrive to your admin on its own with no setup needed. Learn more about the admins new look in Shopify Help Center.

news.title: Keep the cart in view on mobile POS
news.body: Shopify POS v11.15 introduces a persistent cart button on phones that keeps key details about the active cart visible as staff move through POS. The cart button shows recently added items, item count, and running total, so staff can confirm what’s in the cart without leaving the screen they’re working from. It also provides confirmation when changes such as discounts, customers, staff, custom sales, or fees are added. Staff can tap the cart button to open the full cart from Home, Products, Orders, or Search. When they close it, they return to where they left off, making it easier to move between selling tasks without losing context. What’s new * Keep the cart in view: Recently added items, item count, and total remain visible as staff move through mobile POS. * Open the cart in one tap: Tap the persistent cart button from Home, Products, Orders, or Search to access the full cart. * See cart updates as they happen: Staff get confirmation when items and other changes are added to the cart. * Updated mobile navigation: The persistent cart button replaces the Cart tab in the bottom navigation and the previous “Go to cart” bar.

news.title: Multi-currency payouts now available in Australia and France
news.body: We've expanded Multi-Currency Payouts for eligible Shopify Payments merchants to Australia and France. Merchants in Australia can now receive payouts in 13 currencies: AUD, NZD, USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, NOK, SEK, DKK, CHF, JPY, SGD and HKD. All 13 can be paid into an Australian bank account, or you can add an account in the US, New Zealand, the UK, Canada or the eurozone for those currencies. Merchants in France can now receive payouts in 18 currencies: EUR, AUD, CAD, CHF, CZK, DKK, GBP, HKD, HUF, JPY, NOK, NZD, PLN, RON, SEK, SGD, USD and ZAR. EUR remains your default payout currency, and other currencies are paid into additional bank accounts you add. Multi-currency payouts are available to stores on the Advanced and Shopify Plus plans. More info in help docs

news.title: Collect WhatsApp marketing consent at checkout
news.body: Now you can collect WhatsApp marketing consent at checkout. Capture opt-ins when customers make a purchase, expanding your subscriber list and helping you convert new leads through WhatsApp. Enable WhatsApp marketing consent in your Checkout settings.

news.title: Tailwind Labs Is Joining Shopify
news.body: Tailwind Labs is joining Shopify to give Tailwind CSS a stable home and develop the framework alongside real commerce products. Tailwind CSS and the team’s other open-source projects will remain MIT-licensed, with the same team continuing to lead maintenance. Existing customers will retain access to Tailwind Plus and ui.sh, but new customer signups are closing as the team focuses on Tailwind CSS at Shopify.

news.title: Meta is now an AI channel in your admin
news.body: Meta now appears alongside your other AI channels in Agentic Storefronts in your admin. Your products are shared with Meta by default through Shopify Catalog. You can manage acess for Catalog and direct checkout, and view performance for Meta in your agentic settings. Learn more about selling on Meta.

news.title: Product variants now support multiple barcodes
news.body: Until now, a product variant could hold one barcode. That's a problem when the same item arrives with a manufacturer's UPC on the box, your own private-label EAN on the shelf tag, and an ASIN on a marketplace listing. You had to pick one and keep the rest in a spreadsheet. Now you can add up to 20 barcodes to a variant, and any of them identifies the product. What you can do Add, scan, and remove barcodes right on the variant details page, or from the Shopify app on your phone. Give each barcode a type: UPC, EAN, ISBN, GTIN, or ASIN, and we'll check the value against that standard's format, so a mistyped digit gets caught as you enter it. You can also select Custom for internal codes that don't follow a standard. Update barcodes across many variants at once in the bulk editor. Import and export the full set using the Variant Barcodes column in your product CSV. Find products by any barcode on a variant, not just the first one. Channels continue to read the first barcode provided. What stays the same Your existing barcodes are already in place, so there's nothing to migrate. The first barcode on a variant is still the one used wherever a single barcode is expected, which means your

news.title: Microsoft Advertising now available in Campaign Autopilot
news.body: Get more reach with Microsoft Advertising Microsoft Advertising is now available as a channel in Campaign Autopilot. Autopilot can help create a Microsoft Advertising account for you or connect to an existing one, then run Performance Max campaigns alongside your other channels. Budget is allocated automatically based on performance across all your connected channels. Campaign Autopilot is available in early access. Head to the growth tab to sign up or get started.

news.title: Permitted store staff can now see an identified customer's online cart in POS
news.body: Authorized staff can now view items from an identified customer's abandoned online checkout in Shopify POS. When a known customer shops in store, store staff can look them up in POS and see if they have any items in their online cart. Using this information they can offer to assist the customer with sizing or by answering product questions, and help complete the purchase in person. This update is available in Shopify POS v11.14 and requires permissions to be turned on. Enable "View abandoned checkouts" in Shopify Admin under Settings > Users > Roles > POS Role(s) > Customers. In order for an online cart to be displayed the customer must be identified, have an email address, have an eligible abandoned checkout, and the POS session must have location context. Only the products in the customer's online cart is viewable, not their browsing history. Learn more about viewing abandoned checkouts in POS.

news.title: Recommended changes to checkout field settings are now available
news.body: Eligible stores can now get personalized recommendations for customer information settings from the Checkout settings page in Shopify admin. These recommendations help you collect more complete customer details at checkout so you can reconnect with past shoppers more effectively and personalize your marketing. New stores already use these recommended settings by default. Recommendations may include setting customer contact method to email-only, requiring first and last name, or optionally collecting shipping address phone number. You can review recommendations and apply any changes directly from Checkout settings. Existing store settings won’t change unless you apply the recommendations.

news.title: Taxes now recalculate when you change an order's shipping address
news.body: Update: Tax rates vary by destination. Previously, the original destination tax stayed on the order even after you updated the shipping address, so your financials and tax reporting could drift out of sync. Now the order reflects the taxes for where it's actually shipping, which keeps your records accurate. Taxes are recalculated for the new shipping address, and you’ll see a preview of the updated amounts before saving. If the change creates a payment difference, you'll see it before you save, so you can choose to send an invoice to the customer. Learn more about editing a shipping address in the Shopify Help Center.

news.title: DHL Express is now available in the UK, Germany, France, Italy, and Spain
news.body: DHL Express is now available in the UK, Germany, France, Italy, and Spain. Merchants in these markets can buy domestic and international shipping labels from their Shopify admin, with no third-party app or separate DHL account required. What's included: * Competitive DHL Express rates * Domestic and international label buying, right from your admin * Customs documentation generated automatically for international orders * DHL On Demand Delivery, so customers can reschedule a delivery, redirect their shipment to another address, leave it with a neighbor, or collect from a DHL service point * Available on any Shopify plan, with no app, no monthly fee, and pay per label To buy a label, go to any order in your admin and select Create shipping label. Learn more about buying shipping labels on Shopify.

news.title: Managed Markets is ending Delivered Duty Unpaid (DDU) support
news.body: On August 24, 2026, Shopify Managed Markets will stop supporting delivered duty unpaid (DDU) in every country and region where it supports delivered duty paid (DDP). What's changing Markets that use or inherit DDU automatically move to DDP wherever Managed Markets supports it. Customers in those markets will now pay duties and taxes at checkout, not to the carrier or customs on delivery. Collecting duties and taxes at checkout helps avoid surprise costs on delivery and makes international shopping more predictable. What you need to do If you want your customers to keep paying on delivery, turn off Shopify Managed Markets before August 24, 2026. Otherwise, no action is needed. Learn more about Managed Markets in the Shopify Help Center.

news.title: Enhanced printed receipt editor
news.body: We've updated printed receipts in Shopify POS so you can manage sale, return, exchange, gift, and gift card receipts in one place. Return and exchange receipts now print as a single section with one amount summary at the bottom, instead of two separate sections with two subtotals. What’s new? The new content editor in the POS channel applies your branding, header, and footer across every receipt type, lets you override by location only when you need to, and includes built-in fields for return policy, signature line, and regional tax IDs (VAT, GST/QST, ABN). Gift receipts no longer show line items so you can print multiple at once, and you can choose whether gift card receipts print automatically. For everyday changes that used to require the Liquid editor, you can now do it directly in the editor with a real-time preview. Migrating from Liquid customizations If your shop uses a customized Liquid receipt template, you have until January 1, 2027 to move to the new editor. Preview and configure your new template in the content editor while your existing Liquid template keeps printing. When you're ready, flip the shop-level switch to make the new format live. Note that switching is irr

news.title: See Shop Campaigns performance in your analytics tools
news.body: Shop Campaigns performance data, including ad spend, sales, ROAS, and customer acquisition cost, is now available through ShopifyQL. This means your analytics and reporting apps can pull Shop Campaigns data directly, so you can see campaign performance alongside your other marketing channels. What this means for you If you use an analytics app like Triple Whale, Northbeam, or Elevar, your provider can now integrate Shop Campaigns data into their dashboards. Check with your provider on their timeline. If your team builds custom reports in tools like Power BI, Tableau, or Looker Studio, you can connect to this data through ShopifyQL. You can also view Shop Campaigns directly in the Analytics or Advertising tab in your admin. What's available Campaign-level performance by customer segment and time period: ad spend, sales, orders, return on ad spend, average order value, and average customer acquisition cost. Learn more about Shop Campaigns reporting

news.title: Collect WhatsApp marketing consent on Shopify Forms
news.body: Now you can collect WhatsApp marketing consent on Shopify Forms. Capture opt-ins when customers fill out a form on your store, expanding your subscriber list and helping you convert new leads through WhatsApp marketing campaigns. To learn more about enabling WhatsApp marketing consent on Shopify Forms, visit the Shopify Help Center.

news.title: Scan and search variants with multiple barcodes
news.body: Shopify POS can now identify a product variant using any barcode associated with it, making it easier for staff to find the right product when items have different barcodes across suppliers, channels, or packaging. What’s new? Staff can now scan or search for a product variant using any of its associated barcodes, including identifiers such as GTIN, EAN, ASIN, or SKU-based codes. Regardless of which associated barcode is used, Shopify POS will pull up the correct variant. This reduces the need to manually look up products when the barcode on an item differs from the primary barcode your store typically uses, helping staff find the right item faster during checkout, receiving, and inventory tasks. This update is automatically available in Shopify POS v11.14. Additional barcodes must first be associated with the product variant in Shopify Admin.

news.title: Check connectivity status from POS Home
news.body: You can now check your device’s connectivity status directly from POS Home. A new status icon makes it easier for staff to confirm that their device is connected and ready to sell before starting checkout. What’s new? Connectivity status has moved from the POS side navigation to POS Home, where it’s visible at a glance. Staff can select the status icon to open a popover with more details about their connection. By making connectivity easier to find, staff can identify and troubleshoot issues sooner instead of discovering a connection problem in the middle of a sale. This update is automatically available to all staff on Shopify POS v11.14. No setup or action is required.

news.title: Shopify Payments in the United Arab Emirates now available on the Advanced plan
news.body: Merchants on the Advanced plan in the United Arab Emirates can now accept payments through Shopify Payments, with no third-party gateway required. Shopify Payments was previously available only to merchants on the Plus plan. Set up Shopify Payments in your Shopify admin. Review eligibility and onboarding requirements for Shopify Payments in the United Arab Emirates.

news.title: US tax calculation accuracy improvements based on fulfillment location
news.body: Tax accuracy has improved for orders shipping to customers in the United States. Tax is now calculated using the fulfillment location that your order routing settings select for each order. For local pickup orders, tax is calculated from the pickup location. Now, if you fulfill orders from multiple locations, tax reflects where each order actually ships from, and your order records show the ship-from location used in the calculation. This is beneficial because tax rates can depend on where an order ships from, and your records are more accurate for reporting and filing. Learn more about order routing in the Shopify Help Center.

news.title: Review Shopify Payments balance activity with the new activity report
news.body: The Shopify Payments activity report gives you a clearer way to understand how money moved through your Shopify Payments balance over a selected date range. You can open it from Finance > Documents > Shopify Payments activity report or from the Payouts page, then generate a report that brings together your starting balance, gross activity, fees, payouts, and ending balance in one place. Use the report when you're closing a month, checking why your Shopify Payments balance changed, or reviewing activity before payouts reach your bank account. The report is organized around balance activity and transaction dates, so it gives a different view than payout-by-payout exports from the Payouts page. You can also export the report as a PDF for your records or finance workflows. The activity report helps you review balance movement across a period, while the Payouts page remains the place to review individual payout deposits. Learn more

news.title: Checkout now defaults to last used payment method for signed-in customers
news.body: Checkout now remembers a signed-in customer's last-used payment method and pre-selects it on future purchases. This feature is only enabled for checkout flows where saved payment methods are enabled on D2C and B2B.

news.title: Bulk staff setup with CSV import
news.body: You can now create, suspend, and reactivate staff accounts in bulk by uploading a CSV file in Shopify admin. This update helps reduce manual setup for larger teams by letting you bulk create admin or POS staff accounts with assigned PINs and suspend or reactivate existing users in one upload. It’s especially useful for seasonal hiring, store expansion, and fast offboarding, when teams need to make staff changes quickly and accurately. To use this feature, go to Settings > Users > Import in Shopify Admin. Download the sample CSV template there to get started. Learn more about importing users in bulk using a CSV file.

news.title: A redesigned Point of Sale channel page with an easy entry point to the POS editor
news.body: We've redesigned the Point of Sale channel page in your Shopify admin so your in-store setup and performance are right where you start. The page now opens with a Customize the in-store experience section that previews your store's actual lock screen, customer display, and receipts, so you can see what your staff and customers see and open the POS editor for any of them in one click. You can still open the editor from Point of Sale > Settings > Customization as well. 🛍️ You can also read your in-store performance from the same page. A new Analytics section shows gross sales, orders, discounts, and returns for today, the last 7 days, or the last 30 days, and you can filter by location if you sell from more than one store. Each metric links through to the full report. Managing your retail setup is quicker too, with direct links to manage your staff and locations. If you haven't set up a POS device yet, you'll see a QR code to download the Shopify POS app and start selling in person. The new page is available to everyone using the Point of Sale channel, and staff need analytics permissions to see the analytics section. Learn more on https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/ge

news.title: WhatsApp Marketing in Shopify Messaging
news.body: WhatsApp marketing is now part of Shopify Messaging — a new channel to engage your customers.

news.title: DoorDash in the Shopify App Store
news.body: DoorDash is now in the Shopify App Store. Connect your store to get discovered by local shoppers looking for on-demand delivery, adding same-day local fulfillment to your Shopify storefront.

news.title: Sidekick Works with Your Apps
news.body: Shopify Sidekick now works with your apps — get answers and take action in apps like Klaviyo and Checkout Links, right from your conversation.

news.title: Campaign Autopilot
news.body: Your store runs 24/7 — now your marketing does too. Meet Campaign Autopilot: automate everything from paid ads to email right from the Shopify admin.

news.title: Build a Shopify Store with v0, Replit, or Manus
news.body: Three new places to spin up a Shopify store: build with v0, Replit, or Manus — then sell with Shopify. Part of Shopify's push to let you build, manage, and scale your store with the AI tools you already use.

news.title: Universal Commerce Protocol Live for All Merchants
news.body: Universal Commerce Protocol is now live for all Shopify merchants. Teach your agent to search billions of products with Shopify Catalog, build carts, and check out with the new UCP skill.

news.title: Manage Your Shopify Store in ChatGPT or Claude
news.body: Shopify now lets you manage your store directly inside ChatGPT or Claude — get insights, add products, look up orders, and more, all without leaving the chat.

news.title: The Shopify AI Toolkit Is Here
news.body:
Manage your store with your favorite agent.
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, and more.

Learn more → shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/ai-toolkit

news.title: Interactive Learning Overviews for Everyone
news.body: Gemini Notebook made Interactive Learning Overviews available to all users. Under Reports, they bring source summaries and Studio artifacts together in an interactive hub for studying or exploring a topic.

news.title: Live Chat on Mobile for All Ultra Users
news.body: Gemini Notebook has fully rolled out Live Chat to Ultra users on mobile. Have real-time voice conversations with your notebooks in around 100 languages, ask questions about your sources, and get step-by-step guidance with minimal hands-on interaction.

news.title: Short Video Overviews in 70+ Languages
news.body: Short Video Overviews are now available in 70+ languages, plus three new English variants. Turn sources into roughly 60-second vertical videos in your preferred language. Rolling out on web and mobile for Ultra and Pro.

news.title: Flexible Usage Limits in Gemini Notebook
news.body: Gemini Notebook is introducing flexible usage limits for more control over your workflow, rolling out deferred artifact generation, and moving limit resets to every 5 hours instead of daily so you can keep creating throughout the day.

news.title: Expert Intelligence
news.body: Expert Intelligence is a cross-Google initiative for working with sources you already trust, starting with eligible Google Play ebooks in Gemini Notebook. Books can be combined with your other sources rather than read on their own.

news.title: Meet Collections
news.body: We heard you loud and clear: you want a way to organize your notebooks. Meet Collections — a brand new tab that works like photo albums or playlists: zero rigid folder structures with maximum flexibility. Add notebooks to as many collections as you want, or skip them entirely.

news.title: Drive Sync, Pinning, and Slide Deck Editing
news.body: Gemini Notebook shipped a batch of features: sources uploaded from Google Drive now auto-sync when you edit them, you can pin notebooks to the top of your homepage (web), reorder or delete slides in Slide Decks (web), share specific artifacts from phone or web, download slide decks on mobile, and search for notebooks on mobile. More is on the way.

news.title: NotebookLM Is Now Gemini Notebook
news.body: NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook. Three years after starting as a tiny experiment (Project Tailwind), the app grew from a passive workspace into a research companion with audio, video, and interactivity, and an ecosystem reaching the Gemini app and soon Google Search. Same app, same mission (helping you learn faster), updated name reflecting its role in Google's AI portfolio. Big things to come, including folders.

news.title: Short Video Overviews

news.title: In Python SDK 1.10.0, TypeScript SDK 0.130.0, C# SDK 12.52.0, Go SDK 1.77.0, Java SDK 2.67.0, PHP SDK 0.53.0
news.body: In Python SDK 1.10.0, TypeScript SDK 0.130.0, C# SDK 12.52.0, Go SDK 1.77.0, Java SDK 2.67.0, PHP SDK 0.53.0, Ruby SDK 1.75.0, and version 1.37.0 of the ant CLI, the Admin API methods for organization info, members, invites, workspaces, API keys, rate limits, service accounts, workload identity federation, customer-managed encryption keys, and compliance settings are out of beta: call them under client.organization and ant organization. These releases also keep client.beta.organization and ant beta:organization. We announced the deprecation of the Claude Sonnet 4.5 model (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929), with retirement on the Claude API scheduled for November 30, 2026. We recommend migrating to Claude Sonnet 5.5. Read more in Model deprecations.

news.title: We've added capabilities.thinking.types.disabled to the Models API
news.body: We've added capabilities.thinking.types.disabled to the Models API. GET /v1/models and GET /v1/models/{model_id} now report whether each model accepts thinking: {type: "disabled"}, which turns thinking off. See Using the Models API.

news.title: We've added a line field to the Models API
news.body: We've added a line field to the Models API. GET /v1/models and GET /v1/models/{model_id} now return the model line each model belongs to. Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 both report opus, for example. Use line to group models without parsing their IDs. line is null for a model that belongs to no line. See Using the Models API.

news.title: We announced the deprecation of the Claude Sonnet 4.5 model (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929)
news.body: We announced the deprecation of the Claude Sonnet 4.5 model (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929), with retirement on the Claude API scheduled for November 30, 2026. We recommend migrating to Claude Sonnet 5.5. Read more in Model deprecations.

news.title: We've launched Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5)
news.body: We've launched Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5). It's available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude on Google Cloud, and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. For its context window, output limits, and prices, see the Claude Sonnet 5.5 model page. Code written for Claude Sonnet 5 can break on Claude Sonnet 5.5 in five ways. To turn off up-front thinking, send thinking: {"type": "between_tools"} instead of "disabled", at high effort or below. Forced tool use (tool_choice types any and tool) returns a 400 error. Thinking blocks are tied to the model and the conversation. On the Claude API and Google Cloud, the earlier computer_20251124 computer use tool isn't accepted. The advisor tool rejects Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, and Claude Sonnet 5 as advisors. See What's new in Claude Sonnet 5.5 for each change and the migration guide for before-and-after requests. For model-specific prompting patterns, see Prompting Claude Sonnet 5.5. Thinking blocks that Claude Sonnet 5.5 produces work only in the account that produced them, or in an account linked to it. When another account sends one of these blocks, the API drops the block before the model sees

news.title: We're resuming billing for refusals that arrive before any output when stop_details.category is "bio"
news.body: We're resuming billing for refusals that arrive before any output when stop_details.category is "bio", "frontier_llm", or "reasoning_extraction", the categories where we measure low volumes of false positives. Mid-stream refusals were already billed. Refusals billed under this change are charged like any other request, at the rates of the model that ran it. Refusals before any output in other categories are still not billed, and fallback credit is unchanged. This change applies on all platforms. See How refusals are billed. The Compliance API local session endpoints are out of beta for Claude for Microsoft 365 sessions in Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook (product_surface values beginning with office_agents). See Sessions on users' machines. The Compliance API Activity Feed no longer returns file names, project document names, or artifact titles. The filename and title fields on file, project document, and artifact activities are now always empty or omitted, including on activities recorded before this change. To look up a name or title by the ID on the activity, use a Compliance Access Key with the read:compliance_user_data scope. See Understand the Activity object.

news.title: We're expanding which refusals are billed to include refusals that arrive before any output when…
news.body: We're expanding which refusals are billed to include refusals that arrive before any output when stop_details.category is "bio", "frontier_llm", or "reasoning_extraction", the categories where we measure low volumes of false positives. Mid-stream refusals were already billed. The newly billed refusals are charged like any other request, at the rates of the model that ran it. Refusals before any output in other categories are still not billed, and fallback credit is unchanged. This change applies on all platforms. See How refusals are billed.

news.title: Cache diagnostics is out of beta on the Claude API and no longer requires the cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07 beta…
news.body: Cache diagnostics is out of beta on the Claude API and no longer requires the cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07 beta header. Include the diagnostics object on a Messages request to opt in; requests that still send the header work as before. Responses from POST /v1/messages now always include the diagnostics field, which is null when the request did not include the diagnostics object.

news.title: For cache diagnostics, a response to a request that sends the cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07 beta header now…
news.body: For cache diagnostics, a response to a request that sends the cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07 beta header now always includes the diagnostics field. The field is null when the request did not include the diagnostics object. Previously the field was omitted in that case. The Compliance API local session endpoints now also return transcripts of Claude in Chrome sessions (product_surface value claude_in_chrome), in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations, with your existing Compliance Access Key and the read:compliance_user_data scope. See Sessions on users' machines.

news.title: For cache diagnostics, the API now stores a request's fingerprint only when the request includes the…
news.body: For cache diagnostics, the API now stores a request's fingerprint only when the request includes the diagnostics object. A request that sends only the cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07 beta header is still accepted, but no fingerprint is stored. A later turn that points previous_message_id at it reports previous_message_not_found. Include diagnostics on every turn, with "previous_message_id": null on the first.

news.title: We've launched Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), a model for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work
news.body: We've launched Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), a model for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work. It has a 1M token context window by default, 128k max output tokens, and always-on adaptive thinking, at $4 / $20 USD per MTok (Claude Opus 5 is $5 / $25). Claude Opus 5.5 is available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude on Google Cloud, and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. See What's new in Claude Opus 5.5 for capabilities, API changes, and migration guidance. On Claude Opus 5.5, thinking can't be disabled: thinking: {"type": "disabled"} and thinking: {"type": "enabled", ...} return a 400 error. Omit the thinking field and control thinking depth with the effort parameter. tool_choice types any and tool also return a 400 error, as on Claude Fable 5.1; use auto with strict tool use. On the Claude API and Google Cloud, computer use on this model requires the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset and the earlier computer_20251124 tool returns a 400 error; on Amazon Bedrock, computer_20251124 keeps working. See the migration guide. Fast mode (research preview) is available for Claude Opus 5.5 on the Claude API. Tools can now be defined inside a m

news.body: The Compliance API local session endpoints now also return transcripts of Claude in Chrome sessions (product_surface value claude_in_chrome), in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations, with your existing Compliance Access Key and the read:compliance_user_data scope. news.title: The introductory pricing for Claude Sonnet 5 ($2 / $10 per MTok) is now the standard price
news.body: The introductory pricing for Claude Sonnet 5 ($2 / $10 per MTok) is now the standard price: the previously scheduled increase to $3 / $15 per MTok on September 1, 2026 will not occur. See Pricing.

news.title: The Messages API can now compact a conversation on demand on the Claude API
news.body: The Messages API can now compact a conversation on demand on the Claude API, in beta with the compact-2026-09-04 beta header. Send the top-level compaction parameter, and the API returns a signed compaction block that summarizes the messages you sent. On later requests, send that block first, in place of those messages. You choose when to compact, the request can run in the background, and you can keep recent turns word for word after the summary. On models with preserved thinking, the thinking in those kept turns can stay valid.

news.title: Claude Managed Agents permission policies now include auto
news.body: Claude Managed Agents permission policies now include auto: the server evaluates each agent or MCP tool call and runs it, denies it, or pauses for your approval. agent.tool_use and agent.mcp_tool_use events report how each call was evaluated in an evaluation field alongside evaluated_permission. See Let the server evaluate each call with auto. The ant CLI adds ant beta:sessions connect, which attaches your terminal to a Claude Managed Agents session. You can follow the session live, send messages, and allow or deny tool calls that are waiting for approval. Pass --web to serve the Claude Console's session viewer locally and open the session there instead. See Connect to a Managed Agents session from your terminal.

news.title: Version 1.30.0 of the ant CLI adds ant apply, which creates and updates agents, environments, skills
news.body: Version 1.30.0 of the ant CLI adds ant apply, which creates and updates agents, environments, skills, memory stores, and deployments from files in your repository. Describe each resource in a file, run ant apply, and approve the plan it prints. Commit the claude-lock.json lockfile it writes so that later runs, on your machine or in CI, update the same resources instead of creating new ones. See Manage resources as code with ant apply.

news.title: Mid-conversation system messages are available on Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, and Claude Opus 4.8
news.body: Mid-conversation system messages are available on Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, and Claude Opus 4.8, on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud. No beta header is required. This corrects earlier availability notes.

news.title: You can now manage the people in your Claude Enterprise (claude.ai) organization with the Admin API
news.body: You can now manage the people in your Claude Enterprise (claude.ai) organization with the Admin API, in beta for all Claude Enterprise organizations: list members and look them up by email address, change a member's role, remove members, send and withdraw invites, manage groups and their membership, and read custom roles. Group and custom-role requests require the anthropic-beta: ce-user-management-2026-07-13 beta header; member and invite requests take no beta header. An Admin API key with the read:org_audit scope can also call every user-management GET endpoint. See User management.

news.title: Dreams (research preview) now supports Claude Fable 5 and Claude Sonnet 5
news.body: Dreams (research preview) now supports Claude Fable 5 and Claude Sonnet 5. See Supported models. We've expanded the Access Transparency documentation of cmek_preserve events with a filter example, an example event payload, and two preservation reason codes (policy_violation_investigation, csae_report). The documentation now also clarifies that a preservation event is written whether the preservation was initiated by a human reviewer or an automated safety pipeline. See CMEK content preservation.

news.title: You can now set an expiration when you create an API key or an Admin API key in the Claude Console
news.body: You can now set an expiration when you create an API key or an Admin API key in the Claude Console. Choose a preset, a custom duration, or Never. For keys with a lifetime of at least 7 days, Anthropic emails the creator before expiration. Existing keys are unaffected. The Admin API reports each key's expiration in the expires_at field. See Authentication.

news.title: We've added the agent-memory-2026-07-22 beta header
news.body: We've added the agent-memory-2026-07-22 beta header, which changes how listing memories (GET /v1/memory_stores/{memory_store_id}/memories) behaves: results are returned in a stable, server-defined order and the order_by and order parameters are ignored; depth accepts only 0, 1, or being omitted (other values return a 400 error); and path_prefix must end with / and matches whole path segments instead of a substring. Page cursors issued without the header aren't valid with it, so restart from the first page when you adopt it. On memory store endpoints, agent-memory-2026-07-22 replaces managed-agents-2026-04-01; sending both returns a 400 error. On July 22, 2026, the managed-agents-2026-04-01 header adopts the same list behavior. See Beta headers. The Python (0.116.0), TypeScript (0.110.0), Go (1.56.0), Java (2.48.0), Ruby (1.55.0), PHP (0.36.0), C# (12.35.0), and CLI (1.16.0) SDKs now send agent-memory-2026-07-22 on all memory store calls instead of managed-agents-2026-04-01. If your code passes betas explicitly on memory store calls, replace managed-agents-2026-04-01 with agent-memory-2026-07-22 there rather than adding a second value.

news.title: We've restored access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
news.body: We've restored access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. See our statement for more information.

news.title: You can now set a budget on a Claude Managed Agents session: a hard cap on the session's spend
news.body: You can now set a budget on a Claude Managed Agents session: a hard cap on the session's spend, priced at public list rates. A session that reaches its budget pauses with the budget_reached stop reason instead of starting new model requests; changing or removing the budget resumes it. Deployments accept the same budget and apply it to each session they start. See Session budgets. You can now give a Claude Managed Agents session an advisor: a model at least as capable as the agent's own that the session's primary thread can consult mid-turn for strategic guidance. Configure it as a {"type": "advisor"} entry in the agent's multiagent roster, naming the model to consult. See Give the session an advisor. You can now control where model inference runs for a Claude Managed Agents agent. Set inference_geo inside the model object when you create the agent, or override it for a single session. See Data residency for the available geos and pricing. Claude Managed Agents sessions can now load skills from a GitHub repository. When a session mounts a repository, any skills in its root .claude/skills directory are discovered automatically at session start and available to the agent for that sess

news.title: Inference hooks are now in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations
news.body: Inference hooks are now in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations. Point Claude at your organization's AI security server, and each governed prompt across claude.ai, Cowork, and Claude Code is held for the server's allow or deny verdict before inference proceeds. Requests are signed, failure handling is configurable, and every denial is recorded in the compliance Activity Feed. See Inference hooks. We've retired the Claude Opus 4.1 model (claude-opus-4-1-20250805). All requests to this model on the Claude API will now return an error. We recommend upgrading to Claude Opus 5. Researchers can request ongoing access through the External Researcher Access Program.

See Sessions in the cloud.

news.body: Dreams (research preview) now supports Claude Opus 5. See Supported models.

news.title: We've launched Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5), a step-change improvement over Claude Opus 4.8
news.body: We've launched Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5), a step-change improvement over Claude Opus 4.8. Claude Opus 5 supports a 1M token context window (both the default and the maximum), 128k max output tokens, and thinking on by default, at $5 / $25 USD per MTok, the same pricing as Claude Opus 4.8. It's available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude on Google Cloud, and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. See What's new in Claude Opus 5 for new features, behavior changes, and migration guidance, and the models overview for complete specs. On Claude Opus 5, disabling thinking is allowed only at effort high or below: thinking: {"type": "disabled"} with effort xhigh or max returns a 400 error, a breaking change from Claude Opus 4.8. See What's new in Claude Opus 5. Effort is the primary control for steering Claude Opus 5: the model supports the full ladder (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), with max for capability-critical work. Mid-conversation tool changes are now in beta on Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Opus 5: add or remove tools between turns of a conversation while preserving the prompt cache. Include the mid-conversation-to

news.title: You can now set an effort level on a Claude Managed Agents agent's model configuration
news.body: You can now set an effort level on a Claude Managed Agents agent's model configuration. Pass effort inside the model object when you create the agent. See Effort levels for what each level does. Webhooks for Claude Managed Agents now cover the environment and memory store lifecycle: four environment.* event types and three memory_store.* event types. You can react to environment and memory store lifecycle changes without polling. See the Environment events and Memory store events tabs in Subscribe to webhooks. When creating a Claude Managed Agents session, you can now seed it with initial events. Pass initial_events on POST /v1/sessions with up to 50 user.message and user.define_outcome events. A non-empty list starts the agent loop in the same call, so you don't need a separate send-events request to start work. The version field is now optional when updating a Claude Managed Agents agent. Supply it for optimistic concurrency (a mismatch returns a 409 error), or omit it to apply the update unconditionally. See Update semantics. Claude Managed Agents session thread event streams now support event deltas. GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/threads/{thread_id}/stream accepts the same even

news.title: The legacy Workbench (platform.claude.com/workbench) in the Claude Console is being sunset with access ending…
news.body: The legacy Workbench (platform.claude.com/workbench) in the Claude Console is being sunset with access ending on August 17, 2026. Saved prompts, variables, and evals are not supported in the updated Workbench. You can export any data you want to keep from the banner and under your Organizational Settings. For more, see How do I use the Workbench? in the Claude Help Center. The experimental prompt tools APIs for generating, improving, and templatizing prompts (/v1/experimental/generate_prompt, /v1/experimental/improve_prompt, and /v1/experimental/templatize_prompt) are being retired along with the Workbench on August 17, 2026. After removal, requests to these endpoints will return an error.

news.title: We've launched Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1)
news.body: We've launched Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), the successor to Claude Fable 5 for long-running agentic coding, knowledge work, and research, alongside Claude Mythos 5.1 (claude-mythos-5-1) for Project Glasswing participants. Both models support a 1M token context window by default, 128k max output tokens, and always-on adaptive thinking, at $10 / $50 USD per MTok, the same as Claude Fable 5, with cache reads cut to $0.25 per MTok. Claude Fable 5.1 is available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude on Google Cloud, and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. See What's new in Claude Fable 5.1 for capabilities, API changes, and migration guidance. Prompt cache reads on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 cost $0.25 USD per million tokens: 0.025x the base input price, compared with 0.1x on other models. Cache writes are unchanged. See Prompt caching pricing. On Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, tool_choice types any and tool aren't supported and return a 400 error. auto and none are unchanged. To guarantee schema-conformant tool inputs, use strict tool use or structured outputs. Thinking blocks produced by Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.

news.title: In Python SDK 1.2.0, TypeScript SDK 0.122.0, Go SDK 1.68.0, Java SDK 2.59.0, Ruby SDK 1.67.0
news.body: In Python SDK 1.2.0, TypeScript SDK 0.122.0, Go SDK 1.68.0, Java SDK 2.59.0, Ruby SDK 1.67.0, and C# SDK 12.44.0, client.beta.files and client.beta.skills no longer send the files-api-2025-04-14 and skills-2025-10-02 beta headers and return the same shapes as client.files and client.skills. With this change, client.beta.skills.delete() deletes a Skill together with all of its versions, and the beta Messages type BetaSkill (the container Skill reference) is renamed BetaContainerSkill. Requests that still send the beta headers keep receiving the beta shapes. See Migrate from files-api-2025-04-14 and Migrate from skills-2025-10-02. You can now create personal keys and service account keys in the Claude Console. They act as you or as a service account, with the same permissions, and stop working when the linked account is removed from an organization. This lets organization admins more easily track usage for each account, and ensure key usage is legitimate. These API keys can be scoped to a specific workspace or work on admin endpoints and across any workspace the account has access to. Workspace API keys remain supported as a legacy option. See API keys for more information.

news.body: The Compliance API session endpoints are out of beta for Cowork and Claude Code sessions. See Retrieve session transcripts. The Compliance API local session endpoints now also return transcripts of Claude Science sessions (product_surface value claude_science) and Claude for Microsoft 365 sessions in Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook (product_surface values beginning with office_agents), in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations, with your existing Compliance Access Key and the read:compliance_user_data scope. They cover organization info, members, invites, workspaces and workspace members, API keys, rate limits, service accounts, workload identity federation issuers and rules, and customer-managed encryption keys.
