news.title: Flux TTS Inline Controls: Pause and Pronunciation
news.body: Flux TTS (/v2/speak) now supports inline pause and pronunciation controls in the text you send, alongside speed. Pause control. Insert silence with an escaped marker such as \{pause:1s\}: 500–3000 ms in 100 ms steps, up to 8 per request. Available on batch (REST) requests. Pronunciation control (Early Access). Override how a word is said with inline IPA, \{"word": "dupilumab", "pronounce": "duːˈpɪljuːmæb"\}, on both batch and streaming. Results can vary between generations while the feature is in Early Access, so generate each term several times before relying on it in production. Combination guardrails. Combinations that degrade audio are rejected with a clear error instead of producing bad audio: pronunciation cannot be combined with pause or with a speed other than 1.0, and speed is capped at 1.15 when a pause is present. Rejections return CONTROL_COMBINATION_INVALID or PAUSE_SPEED_CAP_EXCEEDED on batch, and ConfigureFailure or DATA-0002 on streaming. Reporting. Applied controls are counted in controls_applied on streaming and in the dg-pronunciations-applied and dg-breaks-applied headers on batch. See Speed, Pause, Pronunciation for syntax, limits, and error codes.

news.title: Toggle Numerals Mid-Stream on Flux STT
news.body: Switch Flux STT to digits for a PIN, phone number, or order number, then back to words, without reconnecting. To turn Numerals on or off during a Flux STT stream, send numerals as a boolean in a Configure message: { "type": "Configure", "numerals": true } The update applies to transcripts Flux STT sends after it processes the message, and ConfigureSuccess now includes numerals in the full active configuration it echoes. The numerals query parameter still sets the initial value when the stream opens. This replaces the connection-time-only behavior in the July 17 entry. Mid-stream numerals work on flux-general-en and on flux-general-multi for English, Spanish, French, German, Russian, Portuguese, Italian, and Dutch.

news.title: Correction: Browser Agent SDK has no client-side VAD
news.body: The Browser Agent SDK never shipped client-side Silero voice activity detection. Documentation published with the SDK described it as an available feature, and that documentation was wrong. The following did not exist in any released package: The vad option on MicrophoneOptions in @deepgram/agents. The speechThreshold and silenceThreshold VAD options. The speech-start and speech-end events on AgentMicrophone. The vad field in WidgetConfig and the widget's VAD configuration section. The @ricky0123/vad-web and onnxruntime-web peer dependencies. Uninstall them if you added them for VAD. MicrophoneOptions accepts sampleRate, echoCancellation, noiseSuppression, and autoGainControl. The microphone streams continuously while it is unmuted. Barge-in works, and it is driven server-side. The Voice Agent API emits user-started-speaking, which you pair with player.interrupt() to stop playback: session.on("user-started-speaking", () => player.interrupt()); @deepgram/react subscribes to that event and interrupts playback for you, so applications built on the provider and hooks need no change. The Browser Agent pages now reflect the shipped API. See JavaScript SDK, Widget Embedding Guide, and Rea

news.title: Correction: token minting uses ttl_seconds
news.body: The server-side token-minting example on the Browser Agent SDK overview posted {"ttl": 30} to POST /v1/auth/grant. The field is named ttl_seconds: body: JSON.stringify({ ttl_seconds: 30 }), /v1/auth/grant accepts unrecognized fields, returns 200, and issues a token with the 30-second default, so a request built from the old example raised no error while ignoring the requested lifetime. If you copied that example and increased the number, your tokens expired after 30 seconds. A 30-second token is enough for a full call. The token only has to be valid at the WebSocket handshake, and the connection stays open afterward. Minting a token requires an API key with Member permissions or higher. See Token-Based Authentication.

news.title: Hold a function call until the user's turn is confirmed
news.body: The agent begins building a reply before speech-to-text confirms the user has finished speaking. Agent audio is held until that confirmation, but function calls have always dispatched as soon as the LLM emitted them. For a function with an irreversible side effect, such as ending a call or booking an appointment, that meant the action could run for a turn the user then continued. defer_until_eot Add defer_until_eot: true to any function in agent.think.functions to hold it until the turn is confirmed. If the user keeps speaking and the turn resumes, the call is discarded before it does anything. { "name": "end_call", "description": "End the conversation and close the connection", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {} }, "defer_until_eot": true } The default is false, so existing agents are unchanged. Deferring one function does not delay the others: a function that did not opt in still dispatches immediately, even with a deferred call ahead of it in the same turn. defer_until_eot applies to every listen provider, not only Flux. news.title: Flux TTS is generally available, and is now the default agent voice
news.body: Flux TTS is the default agent.speak provider Flux TTS is generally available in the Voice Agent API. A Settings message that omits agent.speak altogether now uses Flux TTS with the flux-kit-en voice, where it previously used aura-asteria-en. Set agent.speak.provider.version to v2 with a flux-{voice}-{language} model to select Flux TTS explicitly, or v1 with an aura-* model for Aura. { "agent": { "speak": { "provider": { "type": "deepgram", "version": "v2", "model": "flux-alexis-en" } } } } The GA voice catalog is 36 English voices across seven accents. See the Flux TTS voice catalog. Breaking: default sessions requesting compressed audio are now rejected Flux TTS streams raw audio, so it accepts only the linear16, mulaw and alaw output encodings, with no container and no bit rate. Because it is now the default provider, a session that omits agent.speak and requests a compressed encoding (mp3, opus, flac, aac) or a container such as wav receives INVALID_SETTINGS where it previously received Aura audio. Name an aura-* model in agent.speak to keep the previous behavior: { "agent": { "speak": { "provider": { "type": "deepgram", "version": "v1", "model": "aura-asteria-en" } } }, "audio"

news.title: Wider speed range for Flux TTS
news.body: Flux TTS speed now runs from 0.5 to 1.5 in 0.05 increments, up from 0.85–1.15. The default stays 1.0, and every previously accepted value still works. The wider range applies everywhere speed is accepted on Flux TTS: the /v2/speak streaming WebSocket (at connection and mid-session with Configure), the /v2/speak batch REST endpoint, and agent.speak.provider.speed in Voice Agent sessions running provider.version v2. A value outside the range is still rejected with SPEED_OUT_OF_RANGE, and one off the 0.05 increment with SPEED_INCREMENT_INVALID. Aura speed is unchanged at 0.7–1.5. For details, see Getting Started with Flux TTS, Client Messages, and TTS Models.

news.title: Flexible turn-taking control for Flux
news.body: Flux now gives you full control over how turns end. Beyond Flux's native end-of-turn detection, you can override it, suppress it entirely, or blend the two — and switch between these modes on the fly, even for a single turn, with a Configure message. Turn-taking goes from a fixed behavior to something you shape around each moment of a conversation. Three modes of turn-taking Automatic (default). Flux's native end-of-turn detection decides when a turn ends. EndOfTurn events carry "trigger": "model". Nothing changes for existing integrations. Semi-manual. Keep Flux's detection running, but override it whenever you have a definitive signal — a push-to-talk release, a DTMF tone, a "send" tap — by sending a ForceEndTurn. The model handles the ambiguous endings; you handle the unambiguous ones. Fully manual. Set eot_threshold=1.0 to suppress native detection entirely and own every turn boundary yourself, driving each ending with ForceEndTurn. Ideal when you already run your own VAD or endpointing stack. See Bring Your Own Turn Detection. Switch modes mid-stream — even per turn Because eot_threshold can be updated live with a Configure message, you can change turn-taking behavior for exac

news.title: ForceEndTurn client message
news.body: You can now end the current user turn from your own signal instead of waiting for end-of-turn detection. ForceEndTurn Send ForceEndTurn to end the turn in progress immediately. The agent treats everything transcribed so far as the complete user utterance and moves on to think and speak. { "type": "ForceEndTurn" } Use it for push-to-talk release, DTMF tones, UI actions, or to drive turn taking from your own VAD or endpointing stack. ForceEndTurn requires a Deepgram V2 (Flux) listen provider (agent.listen.provider.version set to v2). With any other listen provider the server sends a FORCE_END_TURN_UNSUPPORTED warning and the turn does not end. For details, see Force End Turn. eot_threshold maximum raised to 1.0 agent.listen.provider.eot_threshold now accepts values up to 1.0. Set it to 1.0 to fully suppress natural end-of-turn detection and own turn taking with ForceEndTurn. For details, see Configure the Voice Agent and Bring Your Own Turn Detection.

news.title: Expressivity for Flux TTS voices, and two new OpenAI models
news.body: expressivity for Flux TTS agent.speak.provider.expressivity shifts a Flux TTS voice's delivery register along a calm to animated axis. It accepts the whole numbers -2 to 2 and defaults to 0, the voice's tuned delivery. Negative values produce calmer, steadier delivery; positive values produce more animated delivery with a wider pitch range. Every Flux voice supports it, and the value applies for the whole session. { "agent": { "speak": { "provider": { "type": "deepgram", "version": "v2", "model": "flux-haley-en", "expressivity": -1 } } } } expressivity is a beta parameter: its behavior may be tuned in future model versions, and non-default values raise the chance of hallucinations and pronunciation errors, so audition the value you plan to ship. 0 remains the only value validated for production. For value-by-value guidance, see Expressivity and Configure the Voice Agent. Two new OpenAI LLM models Deepgram's managed OpenAI provider adds two models: Model Pricing Tier gpt-5.6-luna Standard gpt-5.6-terra Advanced { "agent": { "think": { "provider": { "type": "open_ai", "model": "gpt-5.6-luna" } } } } For the full catalog, see LLM Models.

Both are validated before the request and rejected for non-flux-* models. Option Values Notes --speed 0.85 to 1.15 in 0.05 steps 1.00 is nominal --expressivity -2 to 2 Beta. 0 is nominal; negative is flatter, positive more animated dg speak "So exciting!" --expressivity 2 --speed 1.05 -o lively.wav Any GA voice works with -m. news.body: Set the real meeting date on audio uploads The uploadAudio mutation now accepts an optional meeting_date (ISO 8601 String) on AudioUploadInput. Higher rate limit for shareMeeting Increased the shareMeeting mutation rate limit from 10 to 60 requests per hour per user. The general API rate limits and the 50-email-per-request cap are unchanged. See Limits for details.

Share meetings with a password-protected link (Beta) The shareMeeting mutation can now create a password-protected link so guests can view a meeting without a Fireflies account. Set share_type to PASSWORD_LINK with a password, and build the guest link from the returned share_slug. Recipients in emails are notified with the link — the password is never emailed, so share it separately. This is in beta and is being progressively rolled out. Contact support to have it enabled for your organization.

File uploads can be disabled for your organization The uploadAudio, createUploadUrl and confirmUpload mutations now return a feature_disabled error when an admin has disabled file uploads for transcription in your organization. When uploads are enabled, behavior is unchanged.

news.title: Release: Slack CLI v4.9.0
news.body: Version 4.9.0 of the Slack CLI is here! We've added support for the settings.app_level_token_rotation_enabled app manifest property, which opts your app in to rotating app-level tokens. We fixed an issue where an expired login with an invalid refresh token caused the CLI to retry token rotation on every command. The CLI now asks you to run slack login again. We fixed an issue where the slack activity --tail and slack run commands kept requesting activity logs after the login token became invalid. The command now exits with the auth error.

news.title: Release: Slack CLI v4.8.0
news.body: Version 4.8.0 of the Slack CLI is here! The CLI falls back to manifest.json when the get-manifest hook is unavailable. We've added the slack manifest sync command to sync the app manifest between project and app settings. We've added a --manifest-source flag to the run and deploy commands. We've added support for the code_channels app manifest feature. We fixed an issue where interactive selection prompts left lingering rendered lines on screen after a selection is made.

news.title: Updated installation requirement for Slack Marketplace apps
news.body: As of July 2026, we require that apps submitting to the Slack Marketplace have at least 10 installations on active workspaces, up from the temporary lower threshold. Your app needs to stay at 10 or more installed workspaces throughout the entire duration of the review.

news.title: Release: Slack CLI v4.7.0
news.body: Version 4.7.0 of the Slack CLI has been released! We've added the slack app request command, which checks the status of your most recent request to have an app approved for install. We've added support for custom app icons. The slack run and slack deploy commands can now be used to upload an icon file. We've fixed the help template so hidden subcommands are no longer listed under their parent command.

news.title: The next wave of Agent messaging experience
news.body: We're rolling out a wave of updates to agents on Slack, along with an important heads-up about the road ahead for the Assistant messaging experience. Agent updates and the deprecation of assistant_view​ The Assistant messaging experience (assistant_view) will be deprecated in February 2027. The assistant-related methods that power it are being replaced by a new set of API methods: the Agent Sessions API. Agent sessions let users manage their conversations with your agent in one place, with a status, a title, and a stop button. The agents.sessions.setStatus and agents.sessions.rename API methods replace the assistant.threads.setStatus and assistant.threads.setTitle API methods, respectively. For now, your existing calls keep working through a compatibility bridge. See the Agent sessions guide to get started. The Agent messaging experience (agent_view) is already available, and we recommend moving to it now. If your app still uses assistant_view, follow the migration guide to move to the new experience. Read more in the guide to developing agents. What's new for agents​ Alongside this announcement, we're releasing a set of improvements to the agent experience: Upgraded Tools tab: a n

news.title: Announcing Slack Code
news.body: An agent can answer a question in a thread, but some tasks become bigger than a single question. A coding agent may need to implement a change, share a prototype, and iterate on it. A research agent may need to gather information and work through decisions with the people involved. This kind of work needs more than a single response. Slack Code is how agents and people work together to build with AI in Slack, creating dedicated channels for more involved work. A channel is created from an existing conversation, context is carried forward, and agents and collaborators have a shared, visible place to work. Within a session, agents can publish artifacts for people to oversee and iterate on: Code diffs, so people can review what changed Block Kit views, for structured interactive experiences HTML previews, for prototypes and generated interfaces Canvases, for longer-form content and collaboration The work becomes multiplayer: teammates can join channels, review work, add context, and help make decisions, all while collaborating in the same session and with the same artifacts. news.title: Decide what search engines can see
news.body: You now have full control over what gets indexed, on the Meta tags tab of the SEO & GEO page. Page by page: Each page has a search visibility toggle, and a column showing at a glance which pages are indexed. Turning a page off removes it from your sitemap and adds a noindex tag. Your whole app: Hide the app from search entirely, with a banner so you do not forget it is off. Meta tags and structured data: Switches for injecting meta tags and structured data into your pages. Read more: Page search settings

news.title: Your Superagent can use Base44-managed connectors
news.body: Your Superagent can turn on a Base44-managed connector once you approve it, and call connectors that charge for each use. Setting up a connector from the AI chat follows the same rules.

news.title: Schedule work for the last day of the month
news.body: A scheduled workflow can now run on the last day of the month, or on a particular weekday of the month such as the second Tuesday. Read more: Scheduled workflows

news.title: Find anyone working on your app
news.body: Click the collaborator avatars in your app editor to open a searchable list of everyone on the app, with an Invite button if the person you want is not there yet. Read more: Managing collaborators

news.title: Find members by pasting a list of emails
news.body: Paste a list of email addresses into member search to see every match at once, instead of looking people up one at a time.

news.title: Manage shared connectors from the app editor
news.body: The app editor's connector panel now handles app-user connector setup and full management of shared connectors: reconnect, rename, remove, or change access, all labeled as workspace-level. Read more: Connectors overview

media.alt: Code editor showing a Base44 backend function that posts a message to the #product-updates Slack channel.
media.caption: Slack connector in backend functions

media.caption: Viewing and managing your app connections

news.title: Refund payments straight from your app
news.body: The Refund button on an app's Payments transactions page is open to every app owner, with the usual balance and status checks.

news.title: Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT 6 for your apps
news.body: Your in-app agents, InvokeLLM calls, and AI gateway calls can now run on Claude Opus 5.5, GPT 6 Sol, and GPT 6 Luna. If you had picked one of the models they replace, your choice moves across to the new equivalent on its own and keeps working. Read more: Choosing your model

news.title: Superagent automations default to a faster model
news.body: A Superagent automation left on the default model now runs on GPT 6 Luna at low reasoning, which is quicker and costs fewer credits per run.

news.title: See who created and last updated a record
news.body: The entity record drawer shows who created a record, when, and when it was last updated. The table gains matching optional columns, hidden by default. The Superagent Data view gets the same information.

news.title: Real image thumbnails and direct uploads in the Data tab
news.body: Uploaded images show real thumbnails in the Data and Users tables, and URL fields in the record edit drawer take a file upload directly.

news.title: See which branch each collaborator is on
news.body: Collaborator avatars in the app editor show which branch each person is on, and clicking one jumps you to it. A toast announces a collaborator arriving on your branch.

news.title: New template categories, and smarter ranking
news.body: Templates now split into Apps and Websites, with more categories underneath, making it easier to find the right one. Ranking also takes into account how people actually use a template, not just how many times it was cloned.

news.title: Export your presentation to PowerPoint or Google Slides
news.body: You can now take a deck out of Base44 as an editable PowerPoint file, or as a copy in your own Google Drive. The first Google Slides export asks you to connect Google Drive, then gives you a link straight to the new file. Read more: Exporting your presentation

news.title: GitHub connections moved to the workspace level
news.body: GitHub connections now belong to the workspace instead of one person's account, under a new GitHub tab in your workspace settings. Connections you already had moved across on their own. One connection for the team: Anyone in the workspace can edit and publish synced apps without connecting GitHub themselves, and commits show Base44 as the author. Decide who can connect: Open adding organizations to everyone, or limit it to admins and owners. Control which organizations are allowed: Each connected organization has its own toggle, and members only see the allowed ones when they create or import a repository. See everything in one place: Every connection is listed with its status, and disconnecting one tells you how many apps stop syncing before you confirm. Base Code projects always use per user connections.

media.alt: Base Code showing AI chat, project files, a working branch, live Preview, and Create PR

news.title: Disconnect GitHub from the import dialog
news.body: A confirmed disconnect action sits next to Switch account in the repository-import dialog and on the Base Code page.

news.title: Test a table's permissions from the Data page
news.body: Click Test Permissions in preview in a table's More actions menu to open your app's preview as another user, on a page that reads that table, so you can check its rules before anyone using your app finds a gap. Read more: Changing data permissions

news.title: Ask the AI chat about your plan and credits
news.body: You can ask the AI chat about your plan, your message and integration credits, your limits, and who can see your app. It reads your workspace as it stands, so the answer matches what you would find in your settings. This works whichever kind of app you are building.

news.title: Superagent turns run for up to 20 minutes
news.body: A single Superagent turn can now keep working for up to 20 minutes before it times out, giving longer tasks room to finish.

news.title: The Sequence connector for every Superagent
news.body: Every Superagent owner can now connect Sequence.

news.title: A shared chat queue for collaborators
news.body: When you and a collaborator work on the same app, your queued chat messages now share one queue instead of two separate ones.

news.title: Claude Opus 5.5 Available in Base44
news.body: Base44 added Claude Opus 5.5 as a model option. At launch on September 22, Base44 offered a two-hour window to compare it with other models for free.

news.title: Compare Models Side by Side in Base44
news.body: Base44 introduced Compare Models, which builds the same request with two models so you can choose the result you prefer. At launch on September 22, the first five prompts were free from 9 AM to 3 PM ET. A related giveaway for ten 300-credit prizes closed that day at 4 PM ET.

news.title: Build a presentation in Base44
news.body: Describe the deck you want and Base44 builds a presentation you can edit, publish, and present. Edit slides directly: Change the text on a slide in Edit mode, and move between slides from the thumbnail rail. Speaker notes: Write notes under a slide, or have Base44 generate them. They save as you type and feed the speaker view. 4 ways to show it: A published deck opens in Overview, Speaker, Audience, or Print. Speaker view has a timer and can open a separate display for your audience. Read more: Building a presentation

news.title: Your Superagent replies like a person
news.body: Replies are shorter and read like ordinary conversation. Your agent drops the canned opener, stops repeating your request back to you, and skips the recap at the end, while still giving you everything you asked for.

news.title: Pick the country for your agent's phone number
news.body: Phone setup now takes a country from a searchable list, or a full international number you paste, and checks it on screen before it sends the verification text.

news.title: Open your store from the preview toolbar
news.body: A Store button now sits beside Edit and Canvas, so you can open your app's store straight from Preview or Dashboard, on desktop and on mobile web.

news.title: Dictation follows the language you speak
news.body: Dictation now works out the language you are speaking instead of taking it from your browser, so you can switch language without changing a setting.

news.title: Claim a custom domain another workspace used
news.body: Deleting an app no longer puts its custom domain back in the open. The domain stays reserved for the workspace that had it, and another workspace has to prove it controls the domain before connecting it. Your own workspace: Reconnecting a domain your workspace used before connects straight away, with nothing to prove. A different workspace: The add-domain dialog shows the TXT record to publish at your DNS provider. Add it, then try again. Still in use: A domain attached to a live app cannot be taken over. Whoever is using it has to remove it first. Read more: Claiming a domain another workspace used

news.title: See how AI assistants describe your app
news.body: The data behind this tab is available on the Builder plan and above. SEO & GEO has a new AI Visibility tab that shows how your app turns up when people ask an AI assistant. See whether assistants can read your pages, which of your pages they drew on to answer, and how a model describes your app. Read more: AI Visibility

news.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash uses more integration credits
news.body: An in-app agent or integration call running on Gemini 3.8 Flash now uses twice as many integration credits as it did before. The model and what it does are unchanged. The new rate follows a price rise from the model provider.

news.title: Follow your Superagent's calls from the chat
news.body: Watch a call as it happens: An outbound call now reports back into the conversation that started it, on WhatsApp, Telegram, iMessage, or the web chat, and the follow-up names who was called, why, and what came of it. Set up a number when one is needed: If a goal needs a call and your agent has no number yet, it walks you through setting one up in the chat rather than sending you to its settings.

news.title: Your Superagent greets people on Telegram
news.body: Starting a private Telegram chat with your agent now gets a welcome written by the agent itself, the way WhatsApp already did.

news.title: See which branch spent your credits
news.body: Your app's Usage page has a By branch card showing where your message credits went across main and each of your branches.

news.title: A Superagent tab in the Base44 mobile app
news.body: The Base44 mobile app has a Superagent tab of its own. The drawer's Agent toggle and the Superagent links inside the Apps view open it, and both drawers carry an Apps and Agent switcher at the top. Update to the latest version of the app to get it.

news.title: Start a workflow when someone signs up or logs in
news.body: A workflow can now start when someone signs up for your app or logs in, alongside the triggers you already had for publishing an app and taking a payment.

news.title: A tidier view of what your Superagent did
news.body: While your agent works you see the steps it is taking. Once it finishes, those steps fold into a single summary you can expand, so the answer itself is what stands out.

news.title: Your Base44 Superagent Can Now Make Phone Calls
news.body: Your Base44 Superagent can now make phone calls. It calls, chases the answer, and coordinates with people for you. Give it a multi-step goal and it is still working after you close the chat. Get your Superagent on Base44.

news.title: Data version history is now Backup & Restore
news.body: The Data tab's version history panel is now called Backup & Restore, and its wording follows: backups are kept for 7 or 30 days depending on your plan, and you restore your data to a point in time rather than to a version. How it works has not changed. Read more: Backup & Restore

news.title: Save code changes while you are on a branch
news.body: The code editor now saves your edits on a branch, so you can change a file where you are working instead of switching back to main first. Read more: Code on a branch

news.title: Every permissions change lands in the AI chat
news.body: Change your app's data permissions and the AI chat records a card describing what changed. You get the same card whether the change came from a schema edit, the Permissions editor, or the fix all action in the Data tab. Read more: Changing data permissions

news.title: Give a WhatsApp group its own picture
news.body: Open Manage group, then Details, and set the group picture by uploading an image or pasting a URL. You can also ask your Superagent to set it for you. Read more: WhatsApp groups

news.title: Claim your workspace's email domain
news.body: Once your workspace verifies the email domain it uses, you can turn on a workspace creation policy in workspace settings, under Auth and security. Anyone with an address on that domain then joins your workspace rather than opening one of their own, and the login and signup screens say so. Read more: About workspaces

news.title: Reconnect an app to the repository it left
news.body: An app that was disconnected from GitHub can connect back to the same repository. Base44 reads the commit history on both sides and works out whether to push your app's work up or bring the repository's version in. Read more: Bringing your own GitHub project

news.title: Delete a data table from its card
news.body: The menu on a table's card in the Data tab now deletes the table. If something else in your app still depends on it, the message names every table standing in the way. Read more: Managing your app data

news.title: Add a video to a Google Ads campaign
news.body: You can upload a video file to a Google Ads campaign from the create wizard, from the add video dialog, or when you swap one video for another. Base44 publishes it unlisted to the YouTube channel behind your Ads account. Read more: Google Ads campaigns

news.title: Your Superagent makes the record changes you ask for
news.body: Ask your Superagent to create, update, or delete records and it now carries out exactly what you named in the same turn, without asking you to confirm again. Background runs, sub-agent turns, and requests from anyone other than you still come to WhatsApp or Telegram for your approval first.

news.title: Filter data version history across your tables
news.body: The Data version history panel now filters across up to 200 tables at once, and refreshes on demand so you can check the latest changes without reloading.

news.title: Imported apps follow their own AGENTS.md rules
news.body: On an app imported from GitHub, Base44 now reads the AGENTS.md files along the path it is working in and follows the rules it finds there before it edits anything. Read more: Bringing your own GitHub project

news.title: Better outbound calls from your Superagent
news.body: Work through phone menus: Your agent can press keys during a call, so it can get past "press 1 for sales" and carry on with the same call. A warmer opening: Calls now open with a short introduction of who your agent is calling for, then ask one question at a time and respond to what the other person actually says.

news.title: Finish connecting a Telegram bot that took a different name
news.body: If the username you suggested was already taken, you now get a Finish connecting link that binds the bot Telegram actually created. If more than one of your bots can be connected, Telegram asks you which one you mean.

news.title: Connect GitHub without leaving your pull request
news.body: Opening a pull request on an imported app now offers to connect your GitHub account right there, whether you started from the toolbar or from the AI chat, and picks up where you left off once you are connected.

news.title: Your security scan checks for unauthorized credit usage
news.body: Running a security scan on your app now includes a Credit protection check, which finds places where someone could spend your credits without signing in. Each finding comes with a fix you can apply from your app's Security page. Read more: Running a security scan

news.title: Give your Superagent a goal it keeps working toward
news.body: A goal is a long piece of work rather than a single request. Your Superagent holds on to what you asked for, its own success criteria, and its open tasks across every run, picks the work back up on its own, and checks the result against what you wanted before it treats the goal as done. Start one anywhere: Type /goal in the chat and select Goal, or ask for it from a channel your agent is connected to, such as WhatsApp, Telegram, LINE, iMessage, or Slack. Follow the work: A Goal running banner shows how it is going, Sub-agents lists what is working on it, and Open goal shows the full list of tasks. Pause and come back: Pausing holds the goal with its tasks and results intact until you resume it. Read more: Set a goal

news.title: Your own encryption key for workspace secrets
news.body: Available on the Enterprise plan. Your workspace can now have a dedicated key for encrypting its secrets, such as API keys and integration credentials, instead of sharing one with other customers. Your existing secrets move across in seconds, with no downtime and nothing for you to do. Talk to your account team to turn it on.

news.title: Ask your Superagent for its own phone number
news.body: A dedicated phone number is available on the Builder plan and above. You can now set up a dedicated phone number by asking for one in chat, either in the web chat or in a direct message on WhatsApp, iMessage, Telegram, or LINE. Send back the verification code when it arrives and your agent finishes the setup itself, with no trip to its settings.

news.title: Compare any 2 versions of your app
news.body: Version history now shows the code behind each entry. Open Code changes on a version to see what changed, compare your current code against main or against your live app, and compare a branch straight from its row in the branch picker.

news.title: Skills and integrations in the slash menu
news.body: Type / in the AI chat to see your workspace's skills and the integrations available to it, with the ones you have already connected listed first. Picking a skill drops it into your prompt. Picking an integration you have not connected yet starts a prompt to connect it.

news.title: Your model choice follows you
news.body: The model you pick in the AI chat is now remembered for you rather than for the app, so your choice carries across your apps, main, and every branch. It does not change the model anyone else is working with.

news.title: Keep working on an app with a protected main branch
news.body: When an app's main branch is protected, the AI chat still answers questions and reads your code. Ask for something that would change the app and it offers to create a branch, then carries your request into it. Read more: Working with branches

news.title: Resolve pull request conflicts on an imported app
news.body: When a pull request on an imported app conflicts with the branch it is merging into, the AI chat now tells you in its pull request note and offers to work through the conflict with you. Read more: Bringing your own GitHub project

news.title: Google Ads Integration in Base44
news.body: Google Ads is now natively integrated into Base44. Turn app or website content into campaigns across Google Search, YouTube, Gmail, and more—then launch, track, and pay without leaving Base44.

news.title: Base44 Launches Global Communities
news.body: Base44 launched official communities for Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese speakers, with weekly educational programming plus day-to-day conversation and troubleshooting in each language.

news.title: Claude Sonnet 5 and Opus 5
news.body: Anthropic's newest Claude models are in the AI chat. Automatic mode runs Sonnet 5 for ongoing work, planning, and turns that involve images, and Opus 5 for your first message on plans that do not use cost-saving models. An app whose code names an older Claude model keeps working, and now shows that model's readable name. Read more: Choosing your model

news.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash in the AI chat
news.body: Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash sits directly under Fable 5.1 in the model picker. It suits fast responses on everyday tasks. Read more: Choosing your model

news.title: Less chatter while your Superagent works
news.body: Your Superagent reports less and does more. One acknowledgement per turn: It writes a single short sentence in the language you wrote in, then works through to the result. You hear from it again when it needs your input or hits something it cannot get past. Answers rather than screenshots: When it browses, it reads the page's content and sends a screenshot only when your request is genuinely visual, so a channel like WhatsApp gets the answer instead of a stream of images.

news.title: Open an app in a new tab
news.body: App, agent, and plan cards on the Apps page are real links now, so middle-click, cmd-click, and Copy link all work the way you expect.

news.title: Share an app with a group
news.body: Available on the Enterprise plan. An app's Users page has a Groups tab, and the invite dialog suggests the groups in your workspace, so you can give a whole team access to an app in one step instead of inviting people one at a time.

news.title: Seedream 5.0 Lite and Pro
news.body: BytePlus Seedream 5.0 Lite and Pro join image generation and editing. You can pick either by name, pass reference images, and get PNG or JPEG output.

news.title: Set up a managed connector from the AI chat
news.body: If you administer the workspace, you can ask the AI chat to set up a Base44 managed connector and approve it right there in the conversation. Workspace settings still works the same way. Read more: Connectors

news.title: Wix fonts in the font pickers
news.body: The Wix font catalog is part of the font pickers throughout the app editor. A font you upload yourself still wins if its name matches one in the catalog. Read more: Fonts

news.title: A quick reaction while your Superagent works
news.body: When you send your Superagent a direct message on WhatsApp and the answer takes more than a few seconds, it reacts to your message with an emoji so you know it is working. A reply that lands quickly arrives without one. This applies to direct messages, not group chats.

news.title: One model lineup for everything your app runs
news.body: InvokeLLM, in-app agents, and image and text generation now share a single lineup: Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT 5.6 Luna, Terra and Sol, Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Fable 5.1, GPT 6 Astra, and GLM 5.2. Every model is available on every plan, with credits as the cost control. An app that calls a retired model name keeps working.

news.title: Pausing a Google Ads campaign explains what you are pausing
news.body: When you pause a campaign that is still in its learning phase, the dialog tells you which situation the campaign is in: Never served, converting, running without conversions, or conversion tracking not set up. Every pause asks you to confirm, and where lowering your daily budget is the better move, the dialog suggests it. Read more: Managing your campaign

news.title: Fewer political declarations on EU campaigns
news.body: Every campaign that reaches the EU runs a political-intent check at launch and at retarget. A campaign the check reads as clearly non-political is declared for you. Anything political or unclear still goes to the declaration form. Read more: Creating and launching a campaign

news.title: Explore the component library from the AI chat
news.body: The plus menu in the AI chat carries Explore component library, so you can browse ready-made components and drop one into your app while you build. Read more: Design

news.title: Read the transcript of a phone call
news.body: Ask your Superagent for a recorded call's transcript and it fetches the text for you. Recent calls come back with their call IDs, and a long transcript arrives in pages. Adding a trusted caller now checks that the number is a valid international phone number.

news.title: Revert a message on a branch
news.body: Version history now offers Revert on any branch you can write to. Reverting restores that branch's checkpoint as a new commit on the branch itself, so main is untouched. Editing and resending a message stays on main. Read more: Using version history on a branch

news.title: The branch menu sits beside your app name
news.body: A Main pill next to the app name opens the branch menu. When you are on a branch, the pill carries the branch name in an accent color and the app name folds in behind a slash, so you always know where you are working. Read more: Switching between branches

news.title: Review a pull request without leaving Base44
news.body: On an app imported from GitHub, select the PR chip to open the files changed and their line counts, and edit the title and description inline. The chat keeps a record: Creating a pull request and merging one both appear in your chat history. Merge from the chat: Ask the AI chat to merge the pull request and it merges it for you. Read more: Opening a pull request

news.title: Placeholder values keep an imported app running
news.body: When an imported app is missing a variable it needs to start, Base44 generates an encrypted placeholder so the app boots anyway. The placeholders sit in their own collapsed section with a Replace value action, ready for you to drop in the real key when you have it. Read more: Adding secrets

news.title: An Infrastructure page on every imported app
news.body: Any app you import has an Infrastructure page showing its compose services, their health, and per-database statistics. Read more: Importing from GitHub

news.title: Filter and export your transactions
news.body: In the Transactions tab you can filter by status and export your whole payment history to CSV. The file carries the date, customer name and ID, transaction ID, status, amount, and currency. Read more: Transactions

news.title: Partners can get paid in the client chat
news.body: If you are a Base44 partner in the US, you can send a payment request straight into a client thread and get paid by card, powered by Wix Payments. Set it up once: Connect a Wix Payments account under Partners, in Messages, then send a request from any client thread. One-off or recurring: Your client gets a pay link in the chat and pays by card. Getting your money: Base44 takes 15%, and you withdraw the rest after 30 days once you complete the payouts identity check.

news.title: Plan mode is a conversation now
news.body: Plan mode used to walk you through a fixed set of question cards. Now it is a conversation: the AI reacts to what you say, asks about what is genuinely missing, and suggests things you have not thought of. Answer in your own words: Most questions come as plain text, so you can answer partly, skip one, or take the conversation somewhere else. Some still arrive as a card of options when the answer is a concrete choice. Keep typing: You do not have to wait to be asked. Send a message while a question is on screen and the AI takes it into account alongside your answers. Watch the plan fill in: Plan progress sits beside the conversation and tracks 4 sections, checking each one off once there is enough to write it: intent and goal, audience and roles, core flows, and design. Read more: Using plan mode

news.title: Open a transaction in full
news.body: In Payments, select a row in the Transactions tab to open that payment on its own page. It reads the same way for Wix and Stripe payments. The whole picture: You see the summary, fees and net amount, refund reference, payment method, and the order's line items with shipping and billing details. What happened when: A timeline shows each step the payment went through. Read more: Transactions

news.title: Turn analytics off from the AI chat
news.body: Ask the AI chat to switch analytics off for a web app or a browser game and Base44 makes the change for you. You need to own the app, and the app needs SDK version 0.8.46 or newer. Analytics in native mobile apps stay as they are. Read more: App analytics

news.title: GPT 6 Astra in the AI chat and Superagent
news.body: GPT 6 Astra is OpenAI's newest and most capable model, suited to the hardest reasoning and the most demanding builds. It uses more credits for each request. You can choose it in the AI chat and for your Superagent, where both model pickers now group models by the company that makes them. Read more: Choosing your model

news.title: Choose which note a saved selection joins
news.body: When you save a passage from a conversation, Add to note opens so you can create a new note or search for an existing one and add the text there. Read more: Saving part of a conversation

news.title: Mention your Superagent in Slack
news.body: Mentioning @Superagent in a Slack channel reaches the agent you connected yourself, on every Slack plan including the free one. If your agent does not recognize you yet, reconnect it once from its Slack tab. Workspaces that do not allow user groups have no agent handle, so @Superagent is the way to reach your agent there. Read more: Slack

news.title: See GPT-5.6's reasoning in AI chat
news.body: The thinking panel in AI chat now shows written reasoning summaries for GPT-5.6 Terra and Sol turns.

news.title: Backend functions can import sibling and shared files
news.body: Backend functions that import a relative file, such as './helpers/x.js' or '../../shared/x.ts', used to fail silently: the deploy would fail and Base44 would show the imported file as missing, with no clear error pointing to the real cause. These imports now work correctly.

news.title: The workflows list now shows every workflow
news.body: The workflows page used to stop at 200 workflows. It now pages through all of them, up to 1000, in both the app editor's Workflows page and the Superagent Workflows tab.

news.title: Upload larger Figma files
news.body: The Figma upload limit has been raised to 300 MB, up from 100 MB, so larger brand files no longer get blocked.

news.title: Your Superagent can manage your Base44 apps directly
news.body: Your Superagent can now list and edit your Base44 apps, check build status, and call their backend functions, with no sandbox CLI authentication or device-code login required.

news.title: Talk to your Superagent with your voice
news.body: You can now have a live voice conversation with your Superagent right in the editor.

news.title: Connect your Superagent to a Slack channel
news.body: You can now connect your Superagent to a Slack channel so it can take part directly in the conversation there.

news.title: Your Superagent can control your own Chrome browser
news.body: With the Superagent browser extension installed, your agent can now click, navigate, and read pages directly in your own Chrome browser, instead of using a separate cloud-hosted browser.

news.title: Base44 loads noticeably faster
news.body: Opening Base44 now loads far less code up front, so the app editor starts sooner, especially on a cold load.

news.title: Entity version history now available on the Elite plan
news.body: Reading, downloading, and restoring previous versions of your entity data was previously Enterprise-only. It's now available on the Elite plan too, with 7 days of history (Enterprise keeps its existing 30 days).

news.title: Redirect rules can point to any external URL
news.body: Page-redirect rules for your custom domain can now target a full external address instead of only an internal path, so something like /ads.txt can point to an externally hosted feed.

news.title: Connect your app's MCP server from Gemini and Google Antigravity
news.body: Registering your app's MCP server from the Gemini web app or Google Antigravity no longer fails with an "automatic registration" error.

news.title: Resume a stuck Stripe activation
news.body: If your Stripe account gets stuck mid-activation, Base44 now shows what Stripe still needs from you, along with a Resume setup in Stripe button so you can pick up where you left off. Read more: Setting up payments

news.title: See overdue payment status on your dashboard
news.body: If your workspace has an overdue payment, the compose box on your home dashboard now shows that status right away, even while you still have credits left. Before, it only appeared once your credits also ran out.

news.title: Your Superagent remembers what matters across conversations
news.body: Your Superagent now understands and keeps track of what matters to you, instead of just storing a long list of notes. Knowledge that updates itself: Important facts and preferences are saved automatically, categorized, and refreshed when they change or come up again. Working context per conversation: Each conversation keeps track of your goal, progress, decisions, blockers, and next steps. A memory log you can review: Browse daily summaries and past conversations any time. Full control: Add, edit, or delete what your Superagent remembers, and choose whether it is shared across conversations.

news.title: One security center for your whole workspace
news.body: Available for admins and owners on the Enterprise plan. A new Security Center gives you a single, portfolio-wide view of security across every app in your workspace, instead of checking apps one by one. Portfolio view: See risks found across RLS, secrets, backend functions, dependencies, static code, and headers, plus each app's scan and publish status. Search, filter, and export: Customize columns and export results to CSV. Take action directly: Run a security scan or unpublish an app, one at a time or in bulk, and transfer app ownership. Jump straight in: Open any app's Security page, preview, or dashboard from the same view.

news.title: Manage workspace roles with groups
news.body: Available on the Business plan and above. You can now assign a role to a group instead of to each member individually. Everyone in the group inherits that role, managed from a new Groups tab on the Members page. Custom groups: Create and manage groups directly in Base44, no SSO required. Identity provider groups: Sync groups from Okta, Entra, or Google through SCIM. They stay managed in your directory and read-only in Base44. Clear role resolution: If someone belongs to multiple groups, the highest role wins, and every change is logged.

news.title: Plan mode designs mockups from your own brief
news.body: The design directions Plan mode generates are now built from your own prompt and answers at higher resolution, instead of generic sample renders. You can respond, regenerate, or start building while they are still rendering.

news.title: Plan mode asks fewer, sharper questions
news.body: Plan mode now asks one or two compact cards of up to three questions each, scaled to what your brief actually left out, instead of five or more single-question rounds. A detailed brief can skip straight to the plan.

news.title: GLM 5.2 is now your Superagent's default model
news.body: Sonnet 4.6 has been retired from the model picker. If your agent was already set to it, that selection keeps working. New default: Agents using the default model now run on GLM 5.2 instead of Sonnet 4.6. Image and PDF turns still use Sonnet 5: Any turn where you share an image or PDF runs on Sonnet 5 regardless of your default model. Enterprise workspaces keep Sonnet 5 as their default: Workspaces on the Enterprise plan are not switched to GLM 5.2. They stay on Sonnet 5, including for the build-mode planner.

news.title: Branch your app to try changes safely
news.body: You can now branch your app from its name in the chat top bar, work in the branch's own preview, and merge back to main when you're ready. Build in parallel: Main and each branch run their own build queue, so up to five builds can run at once, and the branch menu shows which ones are still working. Edit mode follows your branch: Element selection and Edit mode changes save to the branch you're on, alongside the branch's own chat. Editing code directly in the code editor stays on main. Automatic branch names: Base44 names a new branch from your first message, in three words or fewer, always in English no matter what language you wrote in. Read more: Working with branches

news.title: Edit backend functions on a branch
news.body: You can now ask AI chat to add or change a backend function while you are working on a branch. The branch gets its own copy of the function, so your main app keeps running the version it already had until you merge. The preview runs the branch's version: A branch preview calls the functions you just changed, not main's. Shared files too: The files your functions import from your app's shared folder can be edited on the branch alongside them. Merging deploys them: When you merge the branch, its functions deploy to main. Publish from main as usual. Still main-only: Workflows and in-app agents have to be changed on main. news.title: Require workspace API keys instead of personal ones
news.body: Available for admins and owners on the Enterprise plan. You can now require that your workspace's apps and data use only workspace service keys and app-user authentication, which blocks personal API keys. A Business workspace can have workspace keys, but requiring them is an Enterprise control. See how personal keys are used: Your workspace's Authentication settings now show personal API key usage, including request counts and how many people are using them. Read more: Blocking personal account API keys

news.title: Set publishing permissions by workspace group
news.body: On the Business plan and above, workspace governance now shows group rows next to role rows, so you can set publishing permissions for a whole group at once. Read more: Setting publishing permissions for groups

news.title: Restore a deleted app from Trash
news.body: When you delete an app, it moves to Trash. You can restore it yourself for 30 days from the Trash view or the Undo toast, and a workspace admin can restore any app across the workspace. Restoring rebuilds your backend: Base44 also lists anything you need to set up again, since deleting immediately releases the app's custom domains, connected integrations, and automations. Read more: Deleting an app

news.title: Web search works with any AI model
news.body: Web search in AI chat now works with any model. Base44 runs up to three searches and merges what it finds into your request. Searches use credits.

news.title: Search your workspace settings by name
news.body: Search your settings by name from the settings sidebar. Results show each setting's name and the page it lives on, and selecting one takes you straight there.

news.title: Edit mode works on more elements
news.body: Edit mode now covers many more elements, including list items, table cells, buttons, and blockquotes. Edits to them save and update your live preview right away, and if one can't be applied, a message tells you why.

news.title: Git commits get real descriptions
news.body: Base44 now reads what a turn actually changed and writes the commit message and checkpoint name from it, so your connected repository's history reads like "Add pie chart component" instead of a generic label.

news.title: Your Superagent does more with your messages
news.body: Reaches your other apps: Message your Superagent on WhatsApp, Telegram, LINE, or iMessage and it can now answer about any app in your workspace, and write data across them, instead of only the app it belongs to. Messages from anyone other than the owner stay closed, as do workspaces using SSO or an IP allowlist. Takes a message mid-run: A message you send while your agent's turn is running now joins that run at its next step, instead of waiting for the turn to finish. This works from the Send now button in the agent editor, and automatically in a 1:1 WhatsApp, Telegram, LINE, iMessage, or Slack conversation. Shows images in chat: When your Superagent sends an image, or links to one directly, chat now shows the picture itself instead of a link.

news.title: A guided Payments tab for your app
news.body: The new Payments tab walks you through going live with payments. Connect Base44 Payments (powered by Wix) or Stripe, finish setup with your provider, and run a test transaction to experience checkout the way your customers will. The tab appears once you connect a payment provider. Guided setup: A step-by-step flow takes you from connecting a provider to your first real payment. Test checkout: Run a test transaction to see the checkout your customers will use. Transaction data in one place: See your payments and revenue from your provider without opening an external dashboard. Read more: Tracking payments in your app

news.title: Control which channels your apps can use
news.body: Available for admins and owners on the Enterprise plan. A new Governance policy lets you control which communication channels your workspace's apps and agents can use, in both directions. Set a channel to allowed or blocked once, and every app and agent follows it. Covered channels: WhatsApp, Telegram, LINE, iMessage, Slack, and email. Per-app exceptions: Allow a specific app to use a channel, with a reason recorded. Enforced for you: The policy is enforced on Base44's servers, so an agent cannot be talked into bypassing it. Read more: Controlling which channels your apps can use

news.title: A richer All Apps page
news.body: The All Apps page has new ways to find and organize your apps. Filter, search, and sort: Narrow down your apps and sort them the way you want. More at a glance: App cards now show details like publish date, number of users, and collaborators. Drag into folders: Drag and drop apps into folders to keep them organized.

news.title: Multiple conversations with your Superagent
news.body: You can now keep separate conversations with your Superagent instead of one long chat. Each conversation keeps its own context, so unrelated work does not get mixed together. Work in parallel: Keep different tasks in different conversations. Pick up where you left off: Move between conversations without losing track of where you were. Archive old conversations: Tuck away conversations you are done with.

news.title: Let AI resolve your GitHub sync conflicts
news.body: You can now resolve a GitHub merge conflict without leaving Base44. When a sync hits a conflict, AI chat shows a Resolve option, reworks each conflicted file so changes from both sides survive, then pushes the finished merge back to your repository.

news.title: Custom domains are included in the Starter plan
news.body: You can connect a custom domain from the Starter plan up, instead of needing a one-off grant. You can also remove the Base44 badge from your app. The Starter plan does not include the free 1 year domain, so you buy or bring your own. Read more: Setting up your custom domain

news.title: A branch behaves like a full copy of your app
news.body: A branch is now built and served on its own, so it works like a real copy of your app instead of a variation of main. Its own preview: A branch preview serves the branch's own pages and reads its own schema, and Edit mode and split-screen editing work there too. Its own version history: Version history reads the branch's history, so restoring a version brings back that branch's state instead of overwriting it with main's schema and navigation. Merge from AI chat: Ask AI chat to merge a branch into main, or update a branch from main, then confirm it from a card in the chat. Start one while your app is building: Create a branch before main finishes generating. It forks from the last completed version and starts building right away. Merging, deleting, and importing still wait until main is idle. On any GitHub-connected app: Create a branch on any app connected to GitHub, and import a repository branch as an app branch. From your phone: Switch, create, and merge branches on mobile web and in the iOS and Android app. Read more: Working with branches

news.title: Open a chat image full-screen
news.body: Click an image attachment in AI chat to open it full-screen. You can move through the other images, swipe between them on a phone, and open the original.

news.title: See which Superagents a member owns
news.body: As an admin or owner, click a member's Superagents count on the workspace Members page to see the agents they own, the same way the Apps count already works.

news.title: Claude Opus 5 is now available
news.body: Claude Opus 5 is now an option in both AI chat and your Superagent's model picker. Choosing a model by hand is available on the Builder plan and above. Read more: Using the AI chat

news.title: More schools qualify for the student discount
news.body: Base44 verifies student and educator email domains for the student discount, and the list of eligible institutions keeps growing, most recently across Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa, Latin America, and US K-12 schools. Read more: Who is eligible

news.title: One callback URL for every app in your workspace
news.body: Setting up a connector with your own OAuth credentials used to mean registering a separate callback URL for every app host, and every new app or custom domain sent you back to register more. Connectors now use a single callback URL that covers all of your apps. Register it once: Add https://connectors.base44.com/api/oauth/callback to your OAuth provider, and it keeps working as you build more apps and connect custom domains. Move older connections when you are ready: Connections created earlier keep their per-app URLs and show a Per-app URLs badge. Switch one over from Callback URLs in the connection, and switch it back from the same place. Read more: Registering callback URLs

news.title: More than 25 new fonts for your apps
news.body: The font pickers in your app editor now include a catalog of over 25 licensed font families, from classic serifs to modern display faces. Search by name or browse the list from the Fonts tab in the Theme panel. Read more: Fonts

news.title: See the element you picked in Edit mode
news.body: The element you select in Edit mode now sits in the chat input as a chip you can remove, and it stays visible on the message after you send it.

news.title: Refine a design option before you choose it
news.body: When the AI offers you visual design options, you no longer have to take one as it comes. Click the Expand icon on an option to open it in full view, shape it until it looks right, then click Apply. Adjust the details: Describe a targeted change, such as a lighter background or a more minimal layout, and the option keeps its direction while only those details change. Ask for something else: Request a completely different direction and that option is replaced with a fresh concept. Read more: Choosing a design option

news.title: Notes: A shared workspace with your Superagent
news.body: Notes gives you and your Superagent one shared workspace for the context that should stay useful beyond a single conversation. Open the Notes tab in Superagent to get started. Built for you: Connect your email and calendar and your Superagent turns useful information into organized topic pages, with a For you page for tasks, follow-ups, and deadlines. Edit together: Create rich pages yourself or ask your Superagent to create and update them from chat. Share a note: Share a note with another person by email so you can both edit it, or publish a page as an unlisted link.

news.title: Your Superagent joins your meetings
news.body: From the new Meetings tab, your Superagent joins your online meetings on Zoom or Google Meet, listens, and takes notes for you. Summary in your inbox: After the meeting, you get the notes and action items by email. Save it as a note: Keep the meeting summary as a note so it stays part of your shared workspace.

news.title: See the infrastructure behind your imported app
news.body: Apps imported from GitHub now have an Infrastructure page that shows the services your app runs, their health, and database statistics, so you can check on your stack without leaving Base44. Read more: Connecting your GitHub repository

news.title: A native Superagents experience in the mobile app
news.body: The Superagents tab in the Base44 mobile app is now fully native. You get a redesigned list to manage all your agents in one place, with native navigation, smooth scrolling, real gestures, and faster screens.

news.title: Bring an existing GitHub project into Base44
news.body: You can now import a GitHub repository and work on it like any other app. Base44 sets it up in a cloud environment, so there is no local setup and you can work from any browser. Make changes in AI chat: Ask for changes in AI chat and see them live in the preview. Ship back as a pull request: Send your changes back to the repository as a pull request, so the repository stays your source of truth. Private repositories: Connect private repositories through your own GitHub sign-in. Read more: Connecting your GitHub repository
