news.title: Introducing Dots in ChatGPT
news.body: OpenAI introduced dots, always-on agents powered by GPT-6 Astra that pursue your goals in the background across up to 4,000 connected apps. You name and customize your dot, set what it can do on its own, when it should ask first, and what it should never do, and message it from Slack, Teams, and more. Available now in ChatGPT for Pro and Business Premium users in eligible markets.

news.title: ChatGPT Comes to Microsoft Word
news.body: ChatGPT for Word can turn rough notes into drafts, revise difficult paragraphs, proofread, suggest edits, and flag formatting issues without leaving the document. ChatGPT for Word, PowerPoint, and Excel are available on all plans, including Free, with usage limits. Business and Enterprise users also have a GPT-5.6 Sol preview in Word from September 17–30, 2026, without affecting usage limits.

media.alt: OpenAI demonstration of ChatGPT in Microsoft Word

news.title: Track Your Credit Score in ChatGPT Finances
news.body: U.S. Plus and Pro users can securely connect their Experian credit report and VantageScore 3.0 score in ChatGPT Finances on web and the latest iOS and Android apps. ChatGPT can explain factors affecting the score, alert users to changes, and help them explore how credit relates to goals such as renting, paying down cards, leasing a car, or getting a mortgage.

news.title: ChatGPT Voice Adds Plugins and GPT-6 Models
news.body: ChatGPT Voice can now use plugins such as email, calendar, and Slack, and can run on GPT-6 Astra, Sol, or Luna. OpenAI is also bringing Voice to ChatGPT Work on web and mobile, where spoken requests can create documents, presentations, sites, and spreadsheets or handle browser tasks. The update is rolling out globally in the latest app version.

media.alt: OpenAI demonstration of the updated ChatGPT Voice experience

news.title: OpenAI Introduces MentalHealthBench
news.body: OpenAI released MentalHealthBench, an open benchmark for evaluating AI responses in realistic mental health conversations. More than 80 licensed mental health experts from 22 countries helped write criteria for synthetic scenarios spanning everyday concerns, serious distress, and emergencies. OpenAI reports improved model performance and has published the methods so other researchers can examine and run the evaluation.

news.title: GPT-5.5 Retires From ChatGPT and Codex on October 14
news.body: OpenAI will retire GPT-5.5 from ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex on October 14, 2026, across all plans, including consumer, Business, Enterprise, and Edu. The retirement does not apply to the OpenAI API. Codex users still on GPT-5.5 should switch to GPT-5.6 Sol or GPT-6 Astra and update any saved model settings, custom agents, scheduled tasks, and scripts that select gpt-5.5.

news.title: 16 Small Business Plugins in ChatGPT
news.body: ChatGPT’s small-business collection brings together 16 plugins designed to take work off owners’ plates, so they can focus on running their businesses.

news.title: ChatGPT for Financial Services
news.body: ChatGPT for Financial Services is a tailored ChatGPT Work experience combining built-in financial data with GPT-6 Astra’s reasoning. Teams can develop research, build financial models, and create customized client materials.

news.title: Dropbox, Box, and SharePoint in ChatGPT Library
news.body: Dropbox, Box, and SharePoint are now natively integrated into the ChatGPT Library across ChatGPT and ChatGPT Work. The rollout begins this week for paid users.

news.title: Data Agent in ChatGPT Work
news.body: ChatGPT Work now includes a Data agent that turns company data into answers, interactive dashboards, and action. Add the Data Plugin, connect the sources and context you already use, and start asking questions.

news.title: Stock Watchlists in ChatGPT Finance
news.body: Stock watchlists are rolling out in ChatGPT Finance for US Plus and Pro users. Tell ChatGPT which stocks to follow and it will monitor what is happening and proactively bring you updates.

news.title: GPT-Live-1 API Now Available
news.body: GPT-Live-1 is now available in the API, bringing ChatGPT’s natural back-and-forth to apps with voice agents that listen while they speak and work with the models and harness you choose.

news.title: ChatGPT Feature Drop — September 11
news.body: This week's ChatGPT feature drop brings a faster, more precise ChatGPT Images model, smoother iOS messaging and pull-to-start-new-chat gestures, easier sharing for files created in ChatGPT, better location-aware answers with permission, and higher-intelligence GPT-6 Astra in Voice.

news.title: Pets and Mini on ChatGPT Desktop
news.body: ChatGPT desktop pets can now keep track of your chats while you’re away and start a new chat for you. Prefer a smaller footprint? Choose Mini for the same shortcuts and updates in less space.

news.title: GPT-6 Astra: A New Generation of Intelligence
news.body: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Astra with advances in computer use, browsing, coding, and professional work. For creators, the model brings stronger visual judgment and better support for producing websites, documents, spreadsheets, and presentations. OpenAI says Astra is rolling out first to a limited set of organizations, with availability over the coming days for ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, as well as through the OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, and AWS Bedrock.

news.title: Save a Temporary Chat
news.body: A Temporary chat can now be personalised with your existing memories, custom instructions and plugins, and saved to your history if it turns into something worth keeping. Temporary chats still create no new memories and stay out of the sidebar unless you save them.

news.title: ChatGPT Feature Drop — August 28
news.body:
OpenAI's weekly ChatGPT feature drop:
• Scheduled tasks for free users — anyone can now set a recurring request, like a Thursday rundown of events happening nearby that weekend.
• Stickers — Imagegen turns any photo into a sticker pack to share on iMessage or WhatsApp.
• Save temporary chats — keep a temp chat in your sidebar after you have started it, and choose whether it uses memory.
• Multiple Google accounts — paid users can connect more than one account and ask about email and calendar across all of them.
• Voice widgets on the lock screen — voice conversations now show things like weather and sports in the iOS Live Activity.

news.title: ChatGPT Feature Drop — August 14
news.body: OpenAI's weekly ChatGPT feature drop: quizzes generated in chat from 'Quiz me on [topic]'; reservation search you can describe in plain language, like a table for two next Saturday somewhere with a good outdoor patio; Google Drive files added to your ChatGPT Library for paid users, via the + menu and 'Add from Library'; and suggestions on the ChatGPT home page for paid users.

news.title: Computer History in ChatGPT
news.body: Computer History lets ChatGPT learn from what you do on your computer, so it can understand how you work, finish tasks you're in the middle of, and suggest skills and automations based on how you actually use your machine.

news.title: Google Drive Files Side by Side in ChatGPT
news.body: You can now open any Google Drive Doc, Sheet, or Slide right inside ChatGPT and work on it side by side, without switching tabs. Rolling out on web to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in ChatGPT and ChatGPT Work.

news.title: ChatGPT Desktop App for Linux (Preview)
news.body: Now in preview: the ChatGPT desktop app for Linux. Use ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex where you already work and build, with your projects and browser workflows on supported Linux systems. Available for desktop variants of Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and 26.04 LTS, Debian 13, and Fedora 43 and 44 — install with .deb or .rpm packages for x64 or ARM64.

news.title: ChatGPT Weekly Feature Drop
news.body: This week's ChatGPT drop: the web composer keeps rich formatting when you paste in emails or documents, paid users get GPT-5.6 Sol with a slider to choose how much thought ChatGPT puts into a response, free users get GPT-5.6 Luna with unlimited text messages rolling out soon, the Android camera flow is much faster, and the new voice experience powered by GPT-Live now supports file uploads.

news.title: GPT-5.6 Sol for Plus and Pro, Luna Free for Everyone
news.body: OpenAI is making better intelligence easier to access in ChatGPT for everyone. GPT-5.6 Sol now powers both Instant and deep reasoning for Plus and Pro users, delivering more factual, focused responses. Free and Go users get unlimited text chats with GPT-5.6 Luna.

news.title: Adobe Plugin in ChatGPT
news.body: Adobe introduced the Adobe plugin in ChatGPT: more than 70 pro-grade tools from Photoshop, Firefly, Acrobat, Adobe Express, Premiere, Lightroom, Illustrator, InDesign, and Stock in one unified plugin that works across ChatGPT Work and Codex. Describe what you want to create and it brings together the right Adobe tools behind the scenes, then hands off to Adobe's apps when you want pixel-level control. Available globally today on ChatGPT web and app: start as a guest, or sign in with an Adobe account to unlock generative features and your Creative Cloud files.

news.title: ChatGPT Gets Better Around the Web
news.body: ChatGPT is getting better around the web. In the Chrome extension's Side Chat, ask about a YouTube video, reference your open tabs, or highlight text on a page and ask away. In the desktop app, get URL suggestions as you type, revisit your browser history, and choose how it's managed. Rolling out today.

news.title: GPT-5.6 Price Cuts + Fast Mode for Sol
news.body: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna's price by 80% and Terra's by 20%, with the lower prices reflected in Codex and ChatGPT Work usage. A new Fast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol in the API delivers up to 2.5x the speed at 2x the standard price. Auto-review in the ChatGPT app and Codex CLI also upgraded from GPT-5.4 to GPT-5.6 Luna, expected to cost about 10x less at the new pricing.

news.title: Share and Adopt Custom Pets
news.body: Your Pet is ready to meet other builders. On ChatGPT web, create a shareable link for your custom pet and send it to a friend to adopt.

news.title: ChatGPT Work Agent Can Use Sign-In Sites
news.body: Your ChatGPT Work agent can now use websites that require you to sign in. Take over the cloud browser to log in, then let your agent continue the task. Your login persists across sessions, so you only have to sign in once.

news.title: Writing Tones
news.body: New in ChatGPT: Writing tones. Steer the style of ChatGPT's writing to match the voice you want.

news.title: Health in ChatGPT
news.body: OpenAI rolled out Health in ChatGPT to all U.S. users 18+ across Free, Go, Plus, and Pro on web and iOS. Link Apple Health and records from US hospital systems, One Medical, or Function Health, and ChatGPT can pull medications, lab results, recent visits, sleep, and activity into any conversation (with your permission). People were already making 300M health-related queries a week.

news.title: ChatGPT Back on WhatsApp in the EEA
news.body: ChatGPT is available again on WhatsApp in the EEA, part of OpenAI's work to make AI accessible in the apps people already use. Message the verified 1-800-CHATGPT contact to ask questions, upload images, send voice notes, create images, and use ChatGPT in many languages.

news.title: ChatGPT Desktop App Updates
news.body: OpenAI updated the new ChatGPT desktop app based on feedback: conversation history and projects are back in the sidebar, Chat and Work history now sync across web, mobile, and desktop (local tasks stay on your computer), and you can easily switch between Chat and Work modes, now consistent with web and mobile. Nothing changes for Codex mode.

news.title: Docs, Spreadsheets, and Slides in ChatGPT Work
news.body: Create and edit polished docs, spreadsheets, and slides in ChatGPT Work, right inside the desktop app.

news.title: Faster, More Powerful Chat Search
news.body: Search across your chats just got faster and more powerful. From the sidebar, search chats, projects, images, and documents in one place across web, iOS, and Android. Use filters to narrow results, then select anything to open it directly in ChatGPT.

news.title: ChatGPT for PowerPoint Generally Available
news.body: ChatGPT for PowerPoint is now generally available worldwide across all plans — making decks a little less painful and a lot more productive.

news.title: GPT-5.5 Instant

news.title: SvelteKit 3 just works on Netlify
news.body: SvelteKit 3 is out today, and it just works on Netlify on day one. To upgrade, run: npx sv migrate sveltekit-3 The migration tool handles most of the mechanical changes for you, including moving your config and updating imports. You can also check out the official migration guide. What’s new Some highlights include: Vite 8 — SvelteKit 3 requires Vite 8, bringing faster builds powered by Rolldown. Config lives in vite.config.ts — SvelteKit configuration moves out of svelte.config.js and into your Vite config, so Vite plugins can read it right away. Explicit environment variables are stable — Declare the environment variables your app depends on in src/env.ts, and specify whether each one is public and whether it’s resolved at build time or when the app boots. You get validation and type safety out of the box. $lib is now #lib — The $lib alias is replaced by #lib, using Node’s subpath imports. Imports need to be unambiguous, so write #lib/foo.ts or #lib/foo/index.ts. Shallow routing is built into goto — Use goto() with shallow: true instead of pushState and replaceState. Consistent error handling — All errors, including ones you throw with error(...), now go through your handleError

A crafted URL can cause an affected app to return attacker-controlled HTML from its own origin, which may run attacker-supplied JavaScript in a visitor's browser. news.title: Security Update: Multiple vulnerabilities in Next.js
news.body: The Next.js team has disclosed seven security vulnerabilities in Next.js (one high, five medium, one low), patched on September 30, 2026 in 15.5.27 and 16.3.8. The issues span server-side request forgery (SSRF), cache poisoning, and information disclosure. Several of them do not affect apps hosted on Netlify. Here's what Netlify customers need to know. Summary Some of these vulnerabilities affect Next.js sites hosted on Netlify (details in Impact on Netlify), so if you run Next.js on Netlify, we strongly recommend upgrading next to 15.5.27 or 16.3.8 and redeploying. The OpenNext Netlify Next.js adapter must also be updated to @netlify/plugin-nextjs 5.16.1; it's auto-installed by default, so a redeploy picks it up (a manual upgrade is only needed if you pin the version). See What should I do? for full steps. Vulnerabilities All issues are patched in 15.5.27 and 16.3.8. Vulnerability: GHSA-cjq9-62q9-8jv4 / CVE-2026-94483 — Image optimizer SSRF Severity: High Affected: 16.x with an attacker-controlled remote host in images.remotePatterns Vulnerability: GHSA-4jqv-mc3x-m676 / CVE-2026-94543 — Cache poisoning of SSG/ISR pages (cross-route) Severity: Medium Affected: 15.x/16.x Pages Route

news.title: Security Update: Critical Next.js vulnerability in ImageResponse
news.body: The Next.js team has disclosed a critical severity vulnerability in an upstream dependency that can lead to remote code execution when ImageResponse renders untrusted input. It is patched in 15.5.26 and 16.3.6. Applications that do not pass untrusted input into ImageResponse are not expected to be affected. Here’s what Netlify customers need to know. Vulnerabilities GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j / CVE-2026-94545 — Remote Code Execution in next/og ImageResponse. Critical. Patched in 15.5.26 and 16.3.6. Impact on Netlify Netlify sites are affected only if they use ImageResponse and the image it generates includes untrusted input — text, or an image loaded from the request. Sites that don’t use ImageResponse, or that only render trusted content through it, are not affected. For sites that do, the impact is limited to a crashed function invocation, not code execution. On Netlify, this has minimal impact: our autoscaling serverless architecture means that a malicious request resulting in a crashed function does not affect other requests. However, active exploitation could increase your function costs. What should I do? We strongly recommend upgrading as soon as possible to patched releases: next

news.title: TypeSafe Jev now available in AI Gateway
news.body: TypeSafe’s Jev model is now available through Netlify’s AI Gateway with zero configuration required. Install @typesafe-ai/sdk and use it directly in your Netlify Functions — no API keys to create, no provider config, no base URLs to wire up. AI Gateway handles credentials automatically, and usage is billed to your Netlify credits like every other model in the gateway. Jev is TypeSafe’s first “System One” model, and it works differently from the chat models you’re used to. Instead of generating prose, you send it your program state along with a set of typed questions, and it returns typed answers with calibrated probabilities. There are three question primitives: choice picks one option from a set, score rates against ordered levels, and noul returns a yes/no probability between 0 and 1. Answers are constrained to the options you declare, so there’s no JSON parsing or schema coercion on your end. Every question in a request is evaluated in parallel against the same state, which means batching a dozen questions into one call costs little more than asking one. news.title: Agent Runners: Get a working result when low on credits
news.body: Agent Runners are now better at completing their work when a run has less credits remaining than the task requires. If you are close to running our of credits during a run, the agent will start focusing on delivering the most useful result it can with the credits it has left. It finishes work already in progress, leaves the project in a working state, and provides a clear summary of what it completed. Previously, an ambitious task could end abruptly before the agent wrapped up, leaving partial changes and little explanation. Now, you’re more likely to get a working result you can use right away, or a solid, clearly documented starting point for your next run. This improvement applies automatically to every agent and model available in Agent Runners. There’s nothing to enable or configure. Learn more in Make changes with Agent Runners and how credits work.

news.title: Agent Runners now use smarter scoping for new projects

news.title: Simplified single sign-on (SSO) process
news.body: If your team uses SSO (single sign-on) with an identity provider, you can now sign in with just your email address without using your team ID. Netlify recognizes your domain and sends you straight to your identity provider. Previously, SSO required you to know your Team ID. That meant every new hire had to know and enter a Team ID, and anyone who forgot or didn’t know it was stuck at the login screen. It was a small detail that quietly created support work for the people administering the team. Now the flow is simplified: enter your email, get redirected to whichever identity provider your team has configured, authenticate there, and land back in Netlify. This is live for every team using SSO with an identity provider that lets you use your email address to authenticate. This means your existing SAML setup already carries everything Netlify needs to route people to the right place. Learn more about configuring SAML SSO in the Netlify documentation.

news.title: SolidStart 2 just works on Netlify
news.body: SolidStart 2 is out, and it deploys to Netlify with no framework-specific adapter to install, a first for full-stack frameworks on Netlify. While SolidStart 1 deployed to Netlify through Nitro under the hood, SolidStart 2 no longer includes Nitro, building directly on Vite’s Environment API instead. The Netlify Vite plugin can now take the server build Vite produces and prepare it for deployment on its own, with no SolidStart-specific Netlify adapter needed in between. How to deploy Install the Netlify Vite plugin: npm install -D @netlify/vite-plugin Then add it to your Vite config with its build support turned on: // vite.config.ts import netlify from '@netlify/vite-plugin'; import { solidStart } from '@solidjs/start/config'; import { defineConfig } from 'vite'; export default defineConfig({ plugins: [solidStart(), netlify({ build: { enabled: true } })], }); That’s the whole setup for a new project. Netlify detects SolidStart and fills in your build settings, and your SSR pages, API routes, server functions, and middleware deploy to Netlify Functions. Prefer to build with Nitro? news.title: GitHub stacked pull requests now create Deploy Previews
news.body: Netlify now creates a Deploy Preview for every pull request in a GitHub stack when the stack ultimately targets your project’s production branch (usually main). You can review and share each layer of a larger change before it merges. A GitHub stacked pull request showing a successful Netlify Deploy Preview check GitHub Stacked Pull Requests help teams split a larger update into smaller, connected pull requests. Each pull request can focus on one step of the work, making changes easier to review and merge in sequence. Previously, Netlify only created a Deploy Preview for the first pull request in your stack while additional pull requests in the stack didn't get their own Deploy Previews. Now, every pull request in the stack gets its own Deploy Preview. There’s nothing new to configure. Create and update your stack in GitHub as usual, and Netlify automatically adds a Deploy Preview to each eligible pull request. news.title: Agent Runners can now ask clarifying questions
news.body: Agent Runners can now ask you clarifying questions before they start building. When a few details could significantly improve the result, the agent pauses and asks instead of guessing. The clarifying questions UI in an Agent Runners session, asking: What should the tracker dashboard keep track of? How clarifying questions work Say you start with something broad, like “Build a tracker dashboard.” Previously the agent had to make every call for you: what the dashboard should track, whether entries should be editable and saved to a database or live in the code as a read-only placeholder, whether the look should be dark and high-contrast or light, clean, and editorial. Now it can ask, and you can answer directly where the agent run works. Answer, skip, or add your own context Answering questions is always optional so you can answer the ones you have opinions about and skip the rest. Or you can skip all questions and let the agent decide. Finally, you can always add context in your own words alongside your answers. news.title: Manage your team invitations from your Netlify dashboard
news.body: Invitations to join an existing team now show up within your Netlify dashboard, where you can accept or decline them directly without checking your email inbox. Previously, the invitation email was the only way in. If it got buried, filtered, or sent to an address you no longer check, then getting collaboration started with your teammate took a lot longer than it needed to. Now, when you sign in to Netlify with an email address that has a pending invitation, you’ll see it waiting for you. Accept it and you’re on the team immediately. Decline it and it’s cleared out. Either way, you never have to go digging through your inbox. Nothing changes about how invitations are sent. Invitees still receive the same email they always have, and accepting from that link works exactly as before. This is simply a second, more reliable path to the same place. Learn more about inviting and managing teammates in Manage team members in the Netlify documentation.

news.title: Bending Spoons to Acquire Airtable
news.body: Bending Spoons entered a definitive agreement to acquire Airtable in an all-cash transaction at a $1.285 billion enterprise value, roughly $2.25 billion in equity value including Airtable's net cash. Airtable's ARR reached about $480 million as of June 2026, growing over 20% year over year. It's Bending Spoons' first acquisition since its Nasdaq listing on July 1, and co-founder Howie Liu says the deal gives Airtable the resources and long-term commitment to build the AI-native platform of the future. The deal is expected to close later in 2026.
